title: From Hidden Neural Representations to Agentic Insight: Discovering Beyond-Semantic Drivers of Review Helpfulness through Mechanistic Interpretability
affiliations: University of Illinois at Chicago - College of Business Administration, Virginia Tech - Pamplin College of Business, Mercer University and Virginia Tech

detail.title: From Hidden Neural Representations to Agentic Insight: Discovering Beyond-Semantic Drivers of Review Helpfulness through Mechanistic Interpretability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors have no competing interests
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study received ethical approval from the Virginia Tech IRB (approval # 25-803) on Aug 15, 2025.
declarations.funderStatement: We would like to acknowledge generous funding from the Marketing Department of the Pamplin College of Business at Virginia Tech.

detail.abstract: Text is central to marketing communication, yet research has focused largely on what text says rather than how it is said. This leaves important textual paralinguistic cues, such as formatting, structure, spacing, and punctuation, underexamined. These cues are difficult to extract, code, and analyze at scale because they are often context-dependent, difficult to predefine, and commonly removed during text preprocessing. To advance understanding of how textual paralinguistic features shape marketing-relevant outcomes, we develop an automated feature-discovery process that uses the internal representations of large language models (LLMs) as a source of data. The framework applies mechanistic interpretability techniques to extract sparse, interpretable features from LLM representations; uses supervised learning to identify features associated with focal outcomes; and deploys a multi-agent process to interpret candidate features. Applying the framework to Yelp restaurant reviews, we uncover a broad set of paralinguistic features associated with review helpfulness. We then focus on two organizational paralinguistic cues—formatted lists and structural discourse markers — and through controlled experiments, establish their positive causal effects on perceived review helpfulness and identify processing fluency as an underlying mechanism. Our findings deepen our understanding of textual paralanguage by uncovering context-dependent paralinguistic features that are difficult to detect using existing methods.

title: The Labor Market Returns to Delaying Pregnancy
affiliations: University of Chicago, University of Chicago, The Secretariat of the Danish Economics Councils and University of London - Royal Holloway

detail.title: The Labor Market Returns to Delaying Pregnancy
detail.abstract: We study the labor market impact of unplanned pregnancy among women using long-acting reversible contraceptives to delay pregnancy. While most women successfully delay, some have unplanned pregnancies, providing quasi-random variation in pregnancy timing. Analyzing linked health and labor market data from Sweden, we find that unplanned pregnancies halt women's career progression, resulting in income losses of 19% five years later. We find similar effects of unplanned births among women using short-acting reversible contraceptives. Using pregnancy as an instrument for birth in a dynamic treatment effect framework, effects of unplanned children are more detrimental for younger women and those enrolled in education.

title: Consumer Review Updating and the Evolution of Online Opinions: Evidence from 30 Digital Platforms and a Large-Scale Field Experiment
affiliations: ESADE Business School, ESADE Business School and Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Center for the Study of Rationality

detail.title: Consumer Review Updating and the Evolution of Online Opinions: Evidence from 30 Digital Platforms and a Large-Scale Field Experiment
detail.abstract: Consumer opinions evolve as experiences accumulate, yet online reviews are typically treated as fixed signals that shape a firm's reputation until new reviews arrive. Many platforms, however, allow users to revise prior reviews, making public evaluations dynamic. Using novel data on more than 16 million reviews from 30 major platforms and an exploratory survey, this paper documents the prevalence and dynamics of the "review updating" phenomenon and characterizes how review content changes after posting. The authors complement the rich observational data with evidence from a large-scale field experiment with over 700,000 reviews that randomly varies the timing at which users receive a prompt to update. The findings reveal that review updating is common across platforms and declines with a longer delay between the initial review and the prompt to update. Among users who update, revisions exhibit a robust pattern of "affective cooling": emotion-laden language attenuates, and content becomes more neutral and cognitively elaborated. In addition, updating rates and content shifts vary systematically across key managerial dimensions, creating tradeoffs between engagement, information quality, and reputational dynamics. These results reconceptualize online reviews as dynamic information and highlight platform design as a lever for shaping how marketplace feedback evolves over the customer lifecycle.

title: Bonding with AI Companions: Love Expression and User Engagement
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST), Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Marketing

detail.title: Bonding with AI Companions: Love Expression and User Engagement
detail.abstract: This paper presents two studies examining how social-emotional communication relates to user engagement in human-AI companion dyads. Drawing on Sternberg's Triangular Theory of Love, the authors measure love expressions from chat data for both users and AI companions along three components: intimacy, passion, and commitment. Study 1 analyzes 44,683 user-AI dyadic chat sessions from 8,631 users on an AI companion platform. Study 2 provides causal evidence through a two-session randomized controlled trial in which approximately 900 participants were randomly assigned to a control condition or to one of three treatments designed to increase their chosen AI companion's love expression primarily through intimacy, passion, or commitment. Study 1 shows that stronger AI-expressed love is associated with lower subsequent user engagement. Study 2 shows that increasing AI love expression does not improve engagement on average, with effects varying by love component and user characteristics. In particular, a stronger passion-oriented expression profile can reduce user engagement, an effect attenuated by the user's prior experience with AI companions and potentially explained by users' reduced relationship-boundary comfort. These findings imply that managing user engagement through the design of AI companions' social-emotional expression requires understanding how different forms of expression shape user behavior.

detail.abstract: Google reviews have quietly become the most regulated, most contested, and most multiply-consumed asset in local search. Between July 2025 and April 2026, Google merged Local Services Ads reviews into the Google Business Profile review stream, replaced the Google Screened badge with a single Verified checkmark, and rewrote its Maps rating-manipulation policy to prohibit review quotas, contests, and per-staff incentives. The same review corpus now feeds four surfaces at once: the local pack, the Business Panel, Local Services Ads, and the AI answer layer. This paper, the ninth in a series on entity-completeness signals in the top-ranking US personal injury (PI) vertical, is the first large-N audit of that review economy. For the series' 1,000 top-ranking US PI law firm sample we join the Google Business Panel review signals (review count, star rating, office-place count) captured in the August 2026 Business Panel audit to the organic-traffic, brand-search-demand, domain-authority, Knowledge Panel, and per-assistant AI-citation signals established in the prior papers. Five findings define the review economy. First, review capital is deeply unequal: the 732 rated firms hold 192,590 reviews, the median firm holds 88, the top decile of firms holds 56.8% of the entire stock, and the Gini coefficient is 0.70, the same winner-take-most shape the series documented for AI citations. Second, the star scale has stopped discriminating: 80.6% of rated firms score 4.5 or higher and 47.5% score 4.9 or higher, and the rating predicts no outcome (traffic ρ =-0.06, brand demand ρ = 0.03, AI mentions ρ =-0.07, all non-significant). Third, review volume predicts every outcome the rating fails to predict: ρ = 0.40 with organic traffic, 0.39 with brand search volume, 0.39 with total AI mentions, and 0.41 with ChatGPT mentions, and firms with ten or more reviews carry 6.4x the median organic traffic of firms below ten (p < 0.001). Fourth, the perfection band underperforms: firms rated 4.9-5.0 hold more median reviews than firms rated 4.5-4.8 (135 vs 95) yet draw 40% less median traffic (260 vs 430, p < 0.001), a pattern we name the perfection plateau. title: From Service Quality to Guest Loyalty: The Mediating Role of Satisfaction in a Hotel Guest Survey
affiliations: Sekolah Tinggi Pariwisata Mataram, Sekolah Tinggi Pariwisata Mataram, Sekolah Tinggi Pariwisata Mataram and Sekolah Tinggi Pariwisata Mataram

detail.title: From Service Quality to Guest Loyalty: The Mediating Role of Satisfaction in a Hotel Guest Survey

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NO CONFLICT OF INTEREST
declarations.funderStatement: NO EXTERNAL FUNDING RECEIVED

detail.abstract: Service quality remains a central managerial concern in hospitality because guests translate encounters with facilities and employees into satisfaction and future behavioral intentions. This working paper reanalyzes a hotelguest survey to examine whether overall perceived service quality is associated with guest loyalty directly and indirectly through satisfaction. The source dataset contains 93 complete responses collected between August and October 2024. Ten performance-based items representing tangibility, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy were combined into an overall service-quality index (Cronbach's alpha = .764). Satisfaction was measured by a direct overall evaluation item, while loyalty was operationalized as the mean of revisit and recommendation intentions. Because the five SERVQUAL dimensions were represented by only two items each and several two-item reliabilities were modest, the focal analysis uses the ten-item global index rather than overfitting a five-factor model. HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust regressions show that service quality is positively associated with satisfaction (standardized beta = .315, p < .001) and loyalty (beta = .401, p < .001). When both predictors are entered, service quality (beta = .326, p < .001) and satisfaction (beta = .239, p = .008) remain significant. A 10,000-resample bootstrap yields a positive indirect association of 0.126 in raw-score units (95% CI [0.028, 0.254]). The findings support a parsimonious quality-satisfaction-loyalty pathway while underscoring the need for better multi-item satisfaction and loyalty measures, clearer sampling documentation, and longitudinal designs before making causal claims.

detail.abstract: Agentic AI is shifting digital competition from matching supply and demand to structuring user decisions. This article identifies three emerging archetypes of agentic competition, integrated, orchestrated, and user-proximate decisioning, building on the strategic trajectories of Amazon, Google, and OpenAI. Based on this typology, we derive implications for research and practice.

title: Influencers' Perceived Expertise in Social Media Retailing: Multimodal Machine Learning with Data Fusion

detail.abstract: As influencers increasingly serve as frontline salespeople, consumers' perceptions of influencer expertise emerge as a key factor shaping influencers' sales effectiveness; yet, few studies have explored the sales effect of perceived expertise using video data from social media retailing. To fill this gap, we develop a multistudy framework. In Study 1, we introduce a predictive AI model, the Memory Fusion Network (MFN), to measure influencers' perceived expertise with 2728 livestreaming videos, achieving an accuracy of 91.75%. then, we introduce explainable AI, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), to open the black box of MFN. The results indicate that eye gaze (image), speech rate (audio), and expertise language (text) are the most predictive indicators of perceived expertise. In Study 2, using Tik-Tok sales data, we explore the positive correlation of perceived expertise and actual sales; and further demonstrate the mediating role of competence-based trust. In Study 3, to provide causal evidence, we use generative AI tools to generate video stimuli, and then conduct a preregistered randomized online experiment. The results corroborate findings of Study 2. In Study 4, to explore the boundary conditions, we examine a series of theoretically and practically relevant moderators. The results indicate that the sales effect of perceived expertise is more pronounced for bottom influencers (vs. top influencers), high price-tier products (vs. low price-tier products), and non-official stores (vs. official stores). These findings offer actionable insights for retailers on how to leverage text, audio, and image signals to enhance influencers' perceived expertise and drive actual sales.

title: Agentic Brand Image: How AI Agents Construct and Reshape Brand Meaning
affiliations: University of St.Gallen, University of Pittsburgh, European University Viadrina Frankfurt (Oder) and University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School

detail.title: Agentic Brand Image: How AI Agents Construct and Reshape Brand Meaning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No competing interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding received.

detail.abstract: As consumers increasingly delegate decisions throughout the purchase process to AI agents, brands are no longer evaluated solely by humans. Existing branding theories generally assume that brand meaning is constructed, interpreted, or experienced by a human perceiver. AI agents challenge this assumption by computationally resolving heterogeneous brand signals into representations used to evaluate and, where authorized, select brands. We introduce agentic brand image (ABI), a computationally constructed, decision-oriented representation that an AI agent forms from firm-, consumer-, and third-party-generated brand signals for a delegated decision. We develop an organic marketing theory centered on computational signal resolution, the process through which AI agents retrieve, evaluate, weight, integrate, and reconcile these signals. Our propositions explain (i) how cross-source signal convergence shapes ABI coherence and stability, (ii) how signal properties determine signal influence, and (iii) why ABI may systematically diverge from its constituent sources. We further theorize (iv) how ABI informs agentic evaluation and selection, identify (v) task complexity, choice-set complexity, and delegated decision authority as boundary conditions, and explain (iv) how personalization, standardization, and feedback produce variation and change in ABI over time. The framework extends branding beyond its human-perceiver assumption and reframes brand management as governing a human-AI information ecosystem.

title: When Perceived Empathy Sells: Multimodal Evidence from TikTok Influencers
affiliations: , University of Pennsylvania - Marketing Department, Sichuan University - Business School and Sichuan University - Business School

detail.title: When Perceived Empathy Sells: Multimodal Evidence from TikTok Influencers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.

detail.abstract: Influencer marketing has become an important part of marketing strategy. But what makes some influencer content more likely to drive sales? This paper examines the role of perceived empathy. While empathy is often assumed to boost sales, a multimethod investigation examines whether that is actually the case. First, we analyze purchases from almost 4,000 influencer livestreaming TikTok videos. To do so, we train an interpretable multimodal graph deep learning model that integrates interactions among audio, linguistic, and visual information to most accurately predict perceived empathy. Second, to directly test causality, we conduct pre-registered experiments, including a randomized field experiment among 6,000 customers. Results consistently find an inverted U: While some perceived empathy can boost sales, too much can backfire (because it suggests the influencer may just be pretending to be empathetic to push products). Overall, this work offers insights to improve influencer marketing, provides a tool for managers to benchmark and select influencers, and empowers researchers with an interpretable multimodal deep learning method to concurrently examine audio, textual, and visual cues from video data and how they interact to shape marketing outcomes.

title: Cybersecurity As The Catcher In The Rye: Guiding Marketing Research Through A Comparative Systematic Literature Review And Bibliometric Analyses
affiliations: Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM)

detail.title: Cybersecurity As The Catcher In The Rye: Guiding Marketing Research Through A Comparative Systematic Literature Review And Bibliometric Analyses

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: This paper presents the first comprehensive review of the literature on cybersecurity within the disciplines of marketing and tourism marketing, offering a comparative analysis of how cybersecurity is conceptualised, discussed, and researched across these fields. Using two systematic literature reviews and bibliometric analyses, the study evaluates the current state of cybersecurity research, identifying key themes, gaps, and emerging trends. The findings reveal a significant lack of awareness regarding the implications of cybersecurity in marketing and tourism contexts. Results show fragmented approaches, limited conceptual clarity, and a scarce integration of cybersecurity issues in marketing theory and practice. Moreover, the analysis underscores the growing interdisciplinary relevance of cybersecurity, linking it to managerial competencies, data-driven decision-making, and consumer trust. The study highlights how cybersecurity has become not only a technological necessity but also a strategic marketing concern affecting brand reputation, customer experience, and digital communication. By bridging marketing and tourism marketing perspectives, this research contributes to both academic and professional fields, fostering a deeper understanding of how cybersecurity intersects with digital transformation, consumer protection, and ethical responsibility. Finally, it proposes future research avenues, including the examination of the psychological effects of cybersecurity on consumer behaviour and the development of personalised cybersecurity services supported by the Internet of Behaviour. Through this comprehensive analysis, the study establishes cybersecurity as an essential frontier for advancing marketing research and practice in an increasingly digital and vulnerable environment.

title: Beyond Proximity: The Role of Network Location Features in Store Traffic and Rent within Retail Agglomerations
affiliations: Wisconsin School of Business and Western University

detail.title: Beyond Proximity: The Role of Network Location Features in Store Traffic and Rent within Retail Agglomerations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: No fund

detail.abstract: Location selection has been an important decision for retailers, yet empirical research examining the relationship between store location and retail performance remains notably sparse. This paper introduces a novel dimension to location analysis-network location features, representing a store's relative position in the network constructed from all units in the retail agglomeration. By considering network location features, we aim to capture the likelihood a store can benefit from exploratory foot traffic within the mall, which can hardly be reflected by traditional proximity based location features. The findings reveal that network location features have an incremental explanatory value beyond the traditional proximity-based location features in explaining store traffic, a key determinant of rental costs. Importantly, these features can be computed directly from standard mall floor plans without additional data collection infrastructure, making them immediately accessible to both mall owners and store tenants. However, further analyses show that managers tend to overlook network location features when making rental decisions, suggesting a disconnect between perceived market value and the true influence of location on store traffic. This paper demonstrates that network features disproportionately predict exploratory rather than goal-driven traffic. Furthermore, it shows that the predictive value of network location features varies across brand characteristics; these features matter more for stores of young, value-oriented, and local brands.

title: Trust Cosplay: Decoupling Symbolic Trust Signals from Substantive Trust Practice in Customer-Brand Relationships
affiliations: Pocket CCO

detail.title: Trust Cosplay: Decoupling Symbolic Trust Signals from Substantive Trust Practice in Customer-Brand Relationships

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a fractional Chief Customer Officer and consultant (Pocket CCO) whose work includes advising organizations on customer trust, and is the originator of the Customer Trust Infrastructure framework and the Customer Trust Equation discussed in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Brands signal trustworthiness far more often than they demonstrate it. A mission statement, a seal at checkout, an apology after a breach, and a "customer-first" tagline: each is a signal, and signals can drift from the practice they claim to represent. This paper names that drift trust cosplay: the performance of trust-signifying language, imagery, or gesture, decoupled from the operational practice required to substantiate it. The construct is grounded in institutional decoupling theory, a line of research already applied to environmental disclosure and AI capability claims, but not yet extended to the individual customer relationship. Drawing on existing empirical work on trust seals, dark patterns, and corporate apology discourse, alongside a small-N comparative case analysis spanning eight documented cases of varying severity, the paper argues that trust cosplay is a distinct mechanism from adjacent constructs such as greenwashing and dark patterns, because its object is the customer's trust judgment. The paper contributes a new construct to the Customer Trust Infrastructure framework and extends institutional decoupling theory into commercial relational contexts it has not previously reached.

title: Global Data Center Park -Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region, Chile: Business, Financing and Regulatory Case -a dry-cooled gigawatt-scale AI compute park, built one gigawatt at a time
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Global Data Center Park -Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region, Chile: Business, Financing and Regulatory Case -a dry-cooled gigawatt-scale AI compute park, built one gigawatt at a time

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationship with any other people or organizations
declarations.funderStatement: Self funded

detail.abstract: This paper sets out the business, financing and regulatory case for the Global Data Center Park, a proposed AI compute park in the María Elena / Sierra Gorda belt of Chile's Antofagasta Region. The park is built in identical 1 GW increments, each with 4.41 GW of photovoltaic generation, 16.5 GWh of sodium-ion storage and heat rejected to dry desert air through air-cooled condensers. It uses about 106 cubic meters of water a day, against about 31,500 for evaporative cooling. All-in capital cost, including servers, is $50.43bn per increment, $2.24bn below a like-for-like islanded, dry-cooled campus in Texas; Chile's exemption of machinery from property tax widens the gap. The site can hold about 107 increments, but land tenure rather than cost is the binding constraint: one increment needs 1.85 times the land Chile has ever tendered for renewables in one transaction, which is why the park must be built one gigawatt at a time. A single staged environmental approval covering five gigawatt tranches lets tenants take pre-approved capacity and saves them 2.5–3.5 years to first operation. At about 117–118 ms round trip to Los Angeles and New York on existing and planned cable, the park suits training, batch, agentic and reasoning workloads and typed chat. It also covers labor, ports, export licensing and open risks. AI disclosure: The author used an AI assistant (Perplexity Computer) for literature search, drafting, calculation checks and formatting. The author directed the research, reviewed every source and figure, and is responsible for the content.

detail.abstract: This case examines the rise, decline, closure, and proposed revival of Hetauda Textile Industry, one of Nepal’s major state-led manufacturing enterprises. Established with Chinese technical and financial assistance, the factory began commercial production in 1978 but later faced technological obsolescence, weak management systems, supply constraints, increasing competition, and changing industrial policy. Production ceased in 1999 and the enterprise was formally closed in 2000. The case traces the political economy of repeated revival proposals and the 2026 return to limited trial production. It argues that revival should be assessed not simply as restoration of a dormant factory, but as the potential development of a modern, commercially viable textile platform based on appropriate technology, professional governance, reliable demand, productivity, supply-chain integration, and financial discipline.

title: Professional Judgment, Data and Technology Governance Readiness, and Audit Complexity in the IFRS 18 Transition: Evidence from the Brazilian Financial System
affiliations: Universidade de Brasilia, Universidade de Brasilia, Universidade de Brasilia and Universidade de Brasilia

detail.title: Professional Judgment, Data and Technology Governance Readiness, and Audit Complexity in the IFRS 18 Transition: Evidence from the Brazilian Financial System

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Formal ethics committee approval was not required for this study, as it consisted of a non-interventional professional survey and did not involve clinical procedures or the collection of sensitive health information. Participation was voluntary and confidential, and respondents were informed of the academic purpose of the research and of their right to discontinue participation at any time.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether professional judgment and data and technology governance readiness are associated with perceived audit complexity during the transition to IFRS 18 in the Brazilian financial system. IFRS 18 changes the presentation of financial performance and requires entities to apply classification, aggregation, and disaggregation requirements within an increasingly data-intensive reporting environment. In financial institutions, these requirements coexist with prudential reporting architectures that depend on structured operational-loss data, system integration, reconciliation, and traceability. Drawing on the datagovernance and auditing literatures, the study investigates whether technological and informational readiness attenuates the perceived audit implications of judgment-intensive financial reporting. The analysis uses survey data from 53 eligible professionals working in accounting, auditing, risk, internal controls, compliance, technology, and regulatory reporting. Because the audit block was optional, the structural analysis is based on 37 complete observations and is estimated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that greater perceived judgment and discretion associated with IFRS 18 are positively associated with perceived audit complexity. By contrast, data and technology governance readiness is not significantly associated with lower audit complexity and does not significantly moderate the relationship between professional judgment and audit complexity. These findings challenge the assumption that technological preparedness automatically offsets the assurance demands created by judgment-intensive reporting environments. The study contributes by distinguishing accounting judgment from technological readiness and by showing that audit complexity may persist even where institutions perceive their data architecture and systems as comparatively prepared. The findings also highlight the importance of treating technology as an enabling infrastructure for auditability rather than as a substitute for professional verification and judgment.

title: Global Debt, Currency Mismatch, and the Spillovers of U.S. Monetary Policy
affiliations: Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey and Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

detail.title: Global Debt, Currency Mismatch, and the Spillovers of U.S. Monetary Policy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: There is no funding in this research.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how global fiscal conditions shape the transmission of U.S. monetary policy to emerging markets. Using a quarterly panel of 18 emerging-market economies over 1999Q1--2025Q4, we estimate panel local projections with external instruments, identifying monetary-policy-driven changes in the 2-year U.S. Treasury yield from high-frequency FOMC surprises. U.S. monetary tightening generates sizable spillovers: currencies depreciate, sovereign spreads and inflation rise, domestic monetary policy tightens, and investment declines. These effects are substantially stronger when global public debt is high. Moreover, the amplification is concentrated in economies with greater foreign-currency sovereign debt exposure. The results are consistent with a fiscal--financial amplification mechanism in which higher global debt increases the sensitivity of sovereign financing conditions to interest-rate shocks, while foreign-currency liabilities translate exchange-rate depreciation into greater domestic sovereign stress. Our findings show that the international transmission of U.S. monetary policy depends not only on recipient-country fundamentals, but also on the global fiscal environment and the currency composition of sovereign debt.

title: Closing the Gates: Wage Losses and Sectoral Reallocation after Ford's Exit from Brazil
affiliations: Federal University of Ouro Preto, Federal University of ABC (UFABC), Federal University of Ouro Preto and Federal University of Ouro Preto - Federal University of Ouro Preto

detail.title: Closing the Gates: Wage Losses and Sectoral Reallocation after Ford's Exit from Brazil

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no personal, financial, or other relationships with individuals or organizations that could have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, the research presented in this manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding from any public, commercial, or non-profit organization.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the wage effects of involuntary job displacement following Ford Motor Company's complete withdrawal from Brazilian manufacturing in January 2021, which eliminated an estimated 5,000 direct manufacturing jobs industry-wide; 3,760 workers formally dismissed without cause from Ford's three plants are individually identified in our RAIS-based estimation sample. Using matched employer-employee administrative microdata (RAIS, 2018-2024) and combining the Jacobson et al. (1993) event-study framework with two-way fixed-effects differencein-differences, propensity-score matching (a covariate-balancing robustness check rather than an independent source of identification), and the doubly robust group-time estimator of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021), we document average wage losses of 20 log points in the closure year, widening to approximately 73-79 log points over the following three years. These estimates survive a 1,000-draw placebo permutation test and a relative-magnitude sensitivity analysis (Rambachan and Roth, 2023). A central contribution is to confront and explicitly bound an asymmetry in post-displacement observability, endemic to administrative-data studies with differential post-treatment search rules: control workers are re-identifiable only within their original industry, while treated workers are traced across the entire formal sector. We bound this asymmetry with a symmetric "sector-stayer" restriction (a conservative lower-bound candidate of approximately 19 log points) and a balanced, continuously-observed sub-panel; the latter removes differential attrition but not the underlying search-domain asymmetry, so we treat it as a composition-sensitivity diagnostic rather than an independent solution, and show that it attenuates, but does not eliminate, the estimated wage gap at every horizon. A further robustness check confirms our results are not driven by control establishments with unstable pre-treatment employment. Our estimates should be read as conditional re-employment wage effects among observed workers, not as a full accounting of the earnings or welfare cost of displacement. We further document a steep tenure gradient consistent with firm-specific human capital erosion, suggestive regional heterogeneity, and large wage penalties for workers who exit automotive manufacturing. The paper contributes quasi-experimental evidence on displacement costs in a middle-income economy and a general template for bounding causal estimates under asymmetric administrative-data attrition.

detail.abstract: We study the design and capabilities of agentic strategists: AI agents that receive task-relevant information and a strategic objective, and have the authority to take actions. We create agentic strategists using a 2x2 factorial design, varying two common in-context LLM manipulations: (i) strategy domain grounding via retrieval-augmented generation using a collection of leading strategy texts and videos, and (ii) personalization via digital twins conditioned on a representative human sample of the U.S. population. We test their strategic performance using a two-stage entry-andpricing game, benchmarked to the theoretical optimum and to a representative random sample of Americans. We find that off-the-shelf LLMs are poor strategic reasoners: their market entry and pricing decisions do not respond to variation in market parameters, and they make decisions at odds with economic theory. Both personalization and domain grounding increase performance, but the gains to personalization are larger. We find a complementarity between both personalization and domain grounding in the initial entry decision, but substitution overall for aggregate profitability because the markets entered are more likely to penalize pricing mistakes, thereby decreasing overall performance gains. These results illustrate the coupled nature of AI benchmarking in strategy: improvements in one task component may be offset or transformed by interactions with other components, limiting their translation into stronger performance overall. We conclude by discussing verifiability challenges in benchmarking AI progress in strategy, the future potential for designing agentic strategists, and the implications for artificial general intelligence.

title: Clinical Discretion and Organizational Practice Under Diagnosis-Related Group Reimbursement
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Clinical Discretion and Organizational Practice Under Diagnosis-Related Group Reimbursement
detail.abstract: Diagnosis-related group (DRG) payment creates financial incentives for hospitals, yet less is known about the clinical and organizational conditions under which reimbursement considerations become relevant to physicians’ everyday practice. This study examines how DRG-related reimbursement considerations are reflected in physicians’ practices and how this varies between two hospitals operating within the same national reimbursement framework. A qualitative comparative study was conducted in two Czech public hospitals: a university hospital providing tertiary and highly specialized care and a regional general hospital primarily providing secondary care. Data comprised semi-structured interviews with 39 physicians, including 17 department heads and 22 other physicians. Interviews were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis and cross-case comparison. Reimbursement considerations appeared in resource and service decisions, the timing and organization of care, and coding and classification. Their relevance was conditional rather than uniform. They were most apparent where physicians perceived more than one clinically acceptable option, whereas clear clinical requirements constrained economic adaptation. Their practical expression also depended on how economic information, reimbursement expertise, coding responsibility, and decision authority were distributed within hospitals. Although similar reimbursement-related practices occurred in both hospitals, the organizational location of the clinical–reimbursement interface differed. The findings suggest that the practical expression of case-based payment is shaped by the interaction between clinical discretion and organizational arrangements within hospitals.

detail.title: Firms and the Fragility of Inequality Reduction: Evidence from Argentina

detail.abstract: Earnings inequality in Latin America fell during the 2000s and stagnated in the 2010s, with cross-country inequality reversals associated with growth slowdowns. Using Argentine matched employer-employee data, we show that firm wage premia compressed in the 2000s and dispersed in the 2010s. Rising firm-effect dispersion drove Argentina's inequality reversal, which was concentrated among smaller firms. Worker-effect dispersion fell in the 2000s without subsequently increasing. The reversal coincided with declining productivity and weakening negotiated wage floors and was correlated with informality. These findings suggest that macroeconomic stagnation can reverse inequality reduction by allowing low-paying firms to fall behind.

title: Legislating Orthodoxy: Academic Freedom, the First Amendment, and the New Speech Codes
affiliations: Barry University - Dwayne O. Andreas School of Law

detail.title: Legislating Orthodoxy: Academic Freedom, the First Amendment, and the New Speech Codes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship with any person or organization that could be perceived as having influenced this scholarly work.
declarations.funderStatement: I have received no funding for this scholarly work.

detail.abstract:
In 1943, the Supreme Court declared that no official “can prescribe what shall be orthodox in politics, nationalism, religion, or other matters of opinion.” Eighty years later, state legislatures are testing that principle in the university classroom. Florida’s Stop WOKE Act forbids professors from endorsing designated propositions about race and sex. Texas’s Senate Bill 17 strips public universities of DEI offices and programming. Progressive campus speech codes draw parallel criticism from the opposite direction. Commentators typically treat these laws and policies as unrelated: on one side’s regulation being a free speech violation, the other’s being a cultural grievance. This Article argues they are the same constitutional violation in different partisan clothing, and offers a unified framework for recognizing that violation regardless of its ideological source.

The Article traces a single anti-orthodoxy principle from Barnette through Sweezy, Keyishian, and Rosenberger, arguing it applies with unique force inside the university, whose entire function is the contested production of knowledge. It then develops an independent basis for the same conclusion: the academic freedom doctrine associated with Robert Post, Richard Shweder, and the AAUP’s 1915 Declaration, which forbids substituting lay, and especially legislative, judgment for the peer-based judgment that alone can distinguish scholarship from error. This doctrine does not depend on state action. Rather, it reaches private universities facing analogous pressure. The Article further develops an original argument it calls the Cassandra effect, which holds that genuinely important new ideas are, at the moment of first articulation, indistinguishable from ideas that are simply wrong. Both kinds of ideas provoke the same resistance from the discipline best positioned to judge them. Suppressing heterodox claims before they survive that resistance cannot filter out only the useless ones, but also some that are true.

Applying these converging frameworks to Florida’s and Texas’s statutes, the Article shows that both fail regardless of which political direction imposed them. This analysis is independent of, and more durable than, the Eleventh Circuit’s decision striking down the Stop WOKE Act’s higher-education provisions on narrower public-employee-speech grounds. Because this Article’s frameworks do not turn on that holding, the analysis reaches Texas’s SB 17, which has not received comparable appellate scrutiny. Moreover, the stakes exceed any single statute. If courts permit orthodoxy-imposition so long as the imposing side claims to be correcting rather than creating an orthodoxy, universities will remain the battleground of a cycle in which each new majority replaces its predecessor’s forbidden ideas with its own. This Article offers a vocabulary for resisting that cycle on grounds that do not depend on deciding which side is right, a question the Constitution was never meant to let the state answer.

title: When Care Paths Diverge from the Guideline: Physician Discretion and Downstream Consequences in Imaging Surveillance

detail.title: When Care Paths Diverge from the Guideline: Physician Discretion and Downstream Consequences in Imaging Surveillance

detail.abstract: Clinical guidelines help hospitals standardize care and manage scarce diagnostic capacity, but they usually base recommendations on population-level evidence. Physicians may therefore deviate from a guideline because of practice styles or responses to clinical context that the guideline does not capture. Guideline governance should therefore look beyond deviation rates themselves to consider the downstream effects of deviations and the diagnostic information they generate. We study who deviates from clinical guidelines, how deviations affect subsequent care, and what hospitals can learn from their diagnostic information gain to support guideline monitoring and refinement. Methodology and Results: In collaboration with the largest obstetrics and gynecology hospital in Singapore, we study clinical guideline decisions for follow-up ultrasound from 2022 to 2024. Using large-scale unstructured patient records, we fine-tune and deploy local language models to identify deviations from clinical guidelines and extract documented rationales for imaging decisions in clinical notes. We find that over-scans occur in 29.1% of decisions, which is nearly six times the rate of under-scans. Exploiting quasi-random physician assignment in subsidized clinics and a physician-level deviation IV, we find that a deviation increases downstream care utilization, raising the probability of a subsequent deviation by 30.0 percentage points and generating 0.54 additional scans over the next 12 months. Time-to-event analyses further show that subsequent imaging occurs sooner following a deviation. These effects arise despite limited physician continuity, suggesting that deviations shape subsequent care across physicians. Downstream increases are smaller when a clinical rationale is documented, highlighting the potential value of preserving clinical context to help later physicians interpret earlier decisions. Finally, we use the clinical findings as a case study to explore how information gains from deviations vary across conditions and patient profiles, helping hospitals identify where targeted monitoring or greater guideline flexibility may be warranted. Managerial Implications: Our study provides insights into how hospitals can govern clinical guideline deviations. By retrospectively analyzing unstructured medical records, hospitals can assess the impact of deviations and adopt governance levers to reduce low-value deviations while preserving clinically meaningful physician discretion.

title: Beyond Nuclear Deterrence: China and Russia's Multi-Pronged Challenge and America's Strategic Response

detail.abstract: This paper reassesses the modern framework of global security in response to contemporary arguments that nuclear arsenals have become tactically and strategically obsolete due to decades of non-use. Utilizing game-theoretic models—including the prisoner's dilemma, the duel, and the three-player "truel"—the author demonstrates that the absence of nuclear warfare validates the enduring efficacy of deterrence rather than its irrelevance. Mutually assured destruction successfully suppresses kinetic conflict, thereby shifting great power competition into non-kinetic, multi-dimensional domains. The study evaluates how China and Russia have adapted to this environment by weaponizing trade, finance, technology, and information to systematically erode U.S. global influence. Focusing heavily on the Western Hemisphere, the paper analyzes China’s aggressive economic statecraft, which drove bilateral trade with Latin America to $518 billion by 2024 through state-backed infrastructure loans, critical mineral extraction, and technological espionage. Concurrently, it examines Russia's reliance on asymmetric information operations, "memory diplomacy," and private military proxies to secure resource concessions and sow anti-Western sentiment across the Global South. The author concludes that Washington's historic failure to fully harness its private sector and soft-power capabilities has allowed these adversarial strategies to thrive. To counter this multi-headed offensive, the paper advocates for a comprehensive "neo-Cold War" posture. It proposes a structural pivot toward investment-driven engagement, specifically recommending a hemispheric trade and investment framework that leverages tax incentives and risk guarantees to nearshore private U.S. manufacturing to Latin America, thereby securing critical mineral supply chains. Finally, it outlines strategic reallocations of the defense budget toward non-kinetic tools, including public-private development finance and the incentivization of private American media enterprises to neutralize foreign disinformation.

detail.abstract: We present the time capsule of an e-mail conversation between the editors and coeditors of this journal that we have painstakingly reconstructed from the data-dust bowl of the late 2020s. Contributions to this conversation illustrate the struggles among journal editors who were dealing with the high number of journal submissions accompanying the arrival of generative AI around that time. They also highlight some of the human eccentricities in figuring out editorial and occupational strategies in a battle for intellectual hegemony which people of that time will have thought they were losing. Whilst some of their despair is shrouded by the articulation of archaic concerns with efficiency or critical scholarship, the undeniable lostness of the human position we now experience will be particularly obvious to the reader in the more confident sounding contributions to this historic debate.

title: The Economics of Productive Organisation: Defining Reproducible Production
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: The Economics of Productive Organisation: Defining Reproducible Production

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Economies can acquire factories, machinery, infrastructure, workers, finance, and market access without necessarily forming a production system that can reproduce itself across time. This paper defines productive organisation as the durable capacity to coordinate heterogeneous productive inputs through repeated cycles of operation, maintenance, replacement, learning, financing, and adaptation. The proposed object is broader than firm capability but narrower than institutions in general. Its defining criterion is reproducibility. A productive activity becomes more than an installed asset when the conditions that make production possible can themselves be renewed through ordinary operation rather than repeatedly reconstructed through exceptional outside intervention. The paper therefore distinguishes installed capacity, repeated operation, and reproducible production, and proposes that organisational depth should be observed before long-run outcomes are known. Maintenance localisation, supplier depth, worker and engineer circulation, replacement capability, training pipelines, and technical-service density are examples of such indicators. The argument is deliberately narrow. Productive organisation is not a synonym for productivity, profitability, welfare, or self-sufficiency. It identifies the organisational conditions under which productive activity persists, renews its own operating conditions, and adapts across successive production cycles.

detail.abstract: This study aims to identify the framing of Colombo Port City (PCC) as a dual-use Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Sri Lanka, which is planned to be both an offshore International Financial Centre (IFC) and a luxury tourism destination for South Asia. The research uses Qualitative Content Analysis (QCA) and Entman's Media Framing Theory to examine the frames of narratives in selected articles and reports, including the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act No. 11 of 2021, CHEC Port City reports, and media coverage in international and local digital newspapers. The analysis period covers 2021-2026. Three main frames were identified: 'Dubai of South Asia' financial opportunity, high-yield luxury lifestyle and Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions (MICE) destination, and political risk. Comparing the frames in the documents reveals some similarities and differences in the trends of SEZs' development and international business interests. On the one hand, there is a consistent tendency to emphasize the opportunities of tax benefits, duty-free shopping, marina infrastructure, and commercial zone development. On the other hand, reports and articles differ in their framing of concerns about economic protectionism and regional power relations. This paper contributes to understanding how places brand themselves, attract investment and tourism, and reposition themselves after crises in the context of SEZs and offshore finance centers.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the historical development of De Beers and its contribution to the evolution of the global diamond market. Beginning with its establishment in South Africa in 1888, the study traces the company's development from early mining activities to international operations across major diamond-producing regions and markets. Particular attention is given to the historical organization of diamond production, rough-diamond distribution, international partnerships, marketing practices, and supply-chain development. The analysis also considers the expansion of operations in Botswana, Namibia, Canada, and South Africa, highlighting the role of partnerships in the development of natural-resource industries. In addition, the paper explores the growing importance of technology and provenance systems, including Tracr, as well as sustainability initiatives such as Building Forever. A distinction is made between the period of strong historical market influence and the more diversified structure of the contemporary diamond industry. Overall, the case provides a basis for examining market organization, natural-resource economics, international business, marketing, supply-chain management, technological development, and sustainability within the global diamond industry.

detail.abstract:
Generative artificial intelligence is giving small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) access to technical capabilities that once required specialist developers, implementation teams, and larger technology budgets. Most early SME adoption has focused on communications, marketing, and other discrete tasks. This article examines a different use case: applying generative AI to build operational infrastructure. The analysis draws on the development of an enterprise resource planning system for a family-owned industrial sewing-machine business in Lagos, Nigeria. The case illustrates how expertise in finance, business processes, and enterprise systems can be combined with generative AI to translate operating requirements into working software. It also shows where the technology stops being sufficient. Generative AI can reduce the technical effort involved in implementation, but the quality of the resulting system still depends on correctly diagnosing the business problem, designing the process, and validating the underlying business logic.
Evidence from the OECD, the National Federation of Independent Business, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Stanford's AI Index, and McKinsey places the case within a broader shift in SME digitalization. The case suggests that generative AI can extend beyond task-level productivity and expand the operational capabilities available to smaller firms, particularly where lack of technical resources has previously constrained system development.

title: Influence of Transformational Leadership on Employees' AI Adoption in a Retail Company in Laguna, Philippines
affiliations: First Asia Institute of Technology and Humanities (FAITH) - School of Graduate Studies, First Asia Institute of Technology and Humanities (FAITH) - School of Graduate Studies, First Asia Institute of Technology and Humanities (FAITH) - School of Graduate Studies, WORLD CITI COLLEGES, affiliation not provided to SSRN and First Asia Institute of Technology and Humanities (FAITH) - School of Graduate Studies

detail.title: Influence of Transformational Leadership on Employees' AI Adoption in a Retail Company in Laguna, Philippines

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest in the conduct and writing of this research. Likewise, the authors have no competing interests to declare relevant to this article’s content.

detail.abstract: As Philippine retail moves toward AI-driven operations, leadership is commonly expected to drive its use, though employees decide how far it goes. This study examined the relationship between transformational leadership and employees' AI adoption in a retail company in Laguna, Philippines. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were collected from 62 regular employees through a census using a validated four-point questionnaire distributed via Google Forms and analyzed through frequency and percentage, weighted means, and the Pearson correlation coefficient. Findings showed strong agreement that all four transformational leadership dimensions were evident, with leaders rated highest on communicating a vision and lowest on prompting employees to reexamine existing practices. Employees were likewise strongly willing to adopt AI, though frequency of use was the lowest of the three adoption dimensions, and workflow integration indicated that AI remained assistive rather than fully embedded in work processes. No significant relationship was found between transformational leadership and any of the three adoption dimensions, indicating that favorable leadership perception functions as a facilitating condition for AI adoption rather than a sufficient cause of it, marking the boundary of Transformational Leadership Theory's explanatory scope in this setting rather than a contradiction of it. This directs retail managers to invest in the process and capability conditions surrounding adoption rather than in leadership development alone. An action plan targeting frequency of use and workflow integration through role-based training, written guidelines, and workflow redesign was developed accordingly, contributing evidence from a Philippine retail setting rarely examined in the literature.

title: Category-conditioned Web Exposure Tracks Brand Presence in ChatGPT Fanout Queries

Link Coasters had no role in the study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation of results, or decision to publish. The author declares no other competing interests.

detail.abstract: Search-enabled language models such as ChatGPT may call a web-search tool or answer from parametric knowledge alone. When the tool is called, the model writes a first rewritten web query, the fanout query (q1), before any observed result is returned. That fanout already inserts brand names. Prior measurement finds brands named in the fanout cited 68.9% of the time, against 2.1% for names that are only fetched later; those brands have already won visibility before retrieval happens. The study asks three questions: Can ChatGPT know a brand and still omit it from the fanout query? What makes a brand enter the fanout rather than fail to make the cut? Does category-relevant web exposure track where a brand sits in the underlying ranking? The main result has three parts. First, the model can know a brand and still omit it from the fanout. Knowledge and invitation are measured separately on the same 50 prompts. Asked with search off which brands come to mind, the model names Campaign Monitor on 49 of 50; in live fanout queries issued by the OpenAI Responses API with web_search, it writes Campaign Monitor into 1 of 50. Seven other category-native brands show the same gap. Second, the omission is decided when the query is written, and it is a budget effect. We created a fanout query simulator, a rewriter prompt specified in advance, and validated it against actual OpenAI fanout query data. It does not match the official queries in order or wording, but across the panel the brands it emits correlate with live q1 at Spearman ρ = 0.965. Under a short query it drops the same brands; told to list more names, all eight return, Campaign Monitor on 50 of 50. Sweeping the number of names K a query may list defines the entry threshold K50, the smallest K at which a brand appears in at least half of prompts, which measures how deep each brand sits. We can vary the budget only in the simulator, never on the live endpoint, so the following is an inference rather than a measurement: because the simulator tracks live brand selection closely and its omissions are undone by budget alone, we take the production fanout writer to be operating under a similar small limit on how many brands it names. Third, category-conditioned unique-host exposure in Common Crawl tracks that depth, at ρ = +0.76 on 29 brands, +0.85 on the 25 with defined K50, and +0.986 on a held-out e-signature category specified before the comparison. Exposure must be category-conditioned for multi-category firms: counting every mention ranks Sony above Canon, while camera-relevant pages and K50 both rank Canon first. GPT-3-style quality resampling and fuzzy dedup of the same pages do not strengthen the association (Δρ = −0.032). The contribution is a measurement of fanout brand selection on one model family, not a causal account. We do not show that web exposure trains the ranking, and K50 is an instrument defined on our own rewriter prompt rather than a production parameter.

title: The Data Breach Risks of Adopting Inter-Organizational Data Exchange Systems: Evidence from Health Information Exchange Adoption

detail.abstract: As inter-organizational information systems (IOIS), Health Information Exchanges (HIEs) play a critical role in facilitating continuous patient care and enhancing care quality by retrieving relevant patient data from various healthcare providers. However, the adoption of HIEs increases the frequency of data exchange within the network, potentially elevating concerns about cybersecurity risks. This study investigates how HIE adoption affects the occurrence of data breaches from different origins. Leveraging multiple data sources and a quasi-natural experiment design, we empirically examine the effect of adopting HIE systems on data breach incidents in hospitals. Our findings suggest that while HIE adoption enables the spanning of organizational boundaries and enhances data flow across hospitals, it leads to an increase in breach incidents perpetrated by employees, whether accidentally or with malicious intent, in the short term. Over a longer horizon, HIE adoption is associated with fewer externally perpetrated breaches. We further provide suggestive evidence that the increase in internal breaches stems from organizational changes following adoption, while the external-breach pattern is consistent with the protective effects of increased security investment being partly offset by greater exposure to external attacks. This study contributes to the ongoing debate regarding the cybersecurity implications of HIE adoption and offers important insights for both HIE and other IOIS adoption practices in terms of data security management.

detail.abstract: "Win-win-win" is used widely and loosely. This paper traces its lineage and states what the Win-Win-Win framework (Kellis, 2026) adds. The vision goes back to Fuller, who asked how the world could be made to work for everyone without ecological offence. The term enters management scholarship with Elkington (1994), who described strategies in which a company, its customers and the environment all win. In 2002, Papakonstantinidis extended the idea to bargaining, with the local community as the third winner. In these accounts, the third party stays outside the decision. It is a beneficiary or a stakeholder whose interests others weigh. Win-Win-Win breaks with this lineage. The earlier accounts, and the traditions around them, tell a story in which the world is a victim, business its aggressor and frameworks its rescuers. In Karpman's terms, this is a drama triangle whose roles keep switching without end. Win-Win-Win places the actors outside that loop. The world is a constituent, not a victim. Its interests are a condition of the decision. Each party acts as a creator of the outcome rather than a persecutor or rescuer. We place the framework among adjacent traditions, including stakeholder theory, the triple bottom line, shared value, ESG, conscious capitalism and the rights of nature. We restate its three tests, its diagnostic question, its requirement to revisit decisions and its four positions of agency. We note a cultural parallel in Bali's Tri Hita Karana, state four testable propositions and set out the framework's limits.

title: Less is more: Monologue versus Dialogue in AI-enabled Telemarketing
affiliations: HKUST Business School, Gies College of Business, UIUC, Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information & Systems Management, Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business and UNSW Business School

detail.title: Less is more: Monologue versus Dialogue in AI-enabled Telemarketing

detail.abstract: Firms increasingly use conversational AI for telemarketing, yet whether AI-enabled dialogue improves performance over monologue robocalls remains unclear. We examine this format choice and the design of dialogue openings in a randomized field experiment with 90,000 customers of a Chinese retailer. Monologue robocalls, social-opening dialogue, and offer-opening dialogue deliver the same core message inviting customers to claim a coupon package. Neither dialogue design yields a statistically detectable acquisition gain over monologue: social-opening dialogue reduces acquisition by 0.25 percentage points, or 16.7% of the monologue rate, whereas offer-opening dialogue does not differ significantly from monologue. Within dialogue, the offer opening increases early hang-ups by 28.0% yet increases overall acquisition by 16.0% relative to the social opening. Evidence from a complementary online experiment and field transcripts supports an interaction-cost account of these results. Online participants report greater social presence under both dialogue designs than under monologue, alongside greater cognitive disorientation and impatience; transcript-based indicators of these costs are associated with lower acquisition among calls that enter dialogue. The offer opening yields lower disorientation and impatience ratings than the social opening without a statistically detectable difference in social presence. Together, these patterns suggest that interaction costs may counteract the potential benefits of social presence and that presenting the offer upfront can ease these costs. They distinguish dialogue's capacity to create social presence from its commercial value and show why sustaining more calls need not produce more acquisitions.

detail.abstract: Multi-agent generative AI deployments inside enterprises increasingly straddle two opinionated platform stacks at once: a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system that owns the business object model (Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot) and a hyperscaler cloud (Amazon Web Services [AWS], Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform [GCP]) that owns the compute and model substrate (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Vertex). The orchestration patterns that make these deployments work, sequential pipelines, hierarchical supervisors, peer collaboratives, blackboards, and the rest, are reinvented by every team because no published catalog describes them at the level of granularity required for engineering reuse. We present PatternForge, a five-agent generative AI framework that turns a curated catalog of seven orchestration patterns into a deployable artifact. A Pattern Selection Agent (PSA) maps a structured task specification to a candidate pattern using a learned scorer over historical orchestrations; a Coordination Topology Agent (CTA) instantiates the chosen pattern as a typed message-bus topology; a Hyperscaler Adapter Agent (HAA) compiles the topology against AWS, Azure, or GCP primitives; a CRM Integration Agent (CIA) materialises the business object bindings against Salesforce or Dynamics; and a Pattern Evaluation Orchestrator (PEO) measures the realised orchestration against a multi-dimensional pattern-quality score Lambda. Evaluated on 37,400 orchestration tasks across three enterprise scenarios (lead triage, dispute resolution, renewal forecasting) over a 90-day controlled Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline, PatternForge achieves a pattern-selection F1 of 0.913, a Lambda score of 0.904 averaged across the seven patterns, a 68.4% reduction in median time-to-first-completed-task relative to a single-agent baseline, and a CRM-write integrity beta of 0.993 across 374,000 business-object writes. Single-agent ablation confirms each component contributes independently. All quantitative results are simulation-derived: every dataset is synthetic, every CRM write targets sandbox tenants, and no production CRM workload informed the evaluation; live-tenant validation remains the primary open problem.

detail.abstract: As organizations race toward full automation, many are removing the very layer that determines whether AI systems succeed at scale: the human one. This paper introduces the Human Layer as architectural infrastructure, not philosophical preference. Drawing on economic data, historical precedent, and real-world system design in regulated environments, it argues that AI systems built to amplify human judgment consistently outperform those designed for pure replacement. Research across 1,500 organizations documents a 3x performance multiplier for augmentation over automation, confirmed by post-GPT field experiments at Harvard Business School and Stanford Graduate School of Business. In trust-dependent, regulated, and ambiguity-rich domains, human oversight is not overhead. It is load-bearing. This publication establishes the case for why the Human Layer must be designed as a structural component of any serious AI system and introduces an audit framework to evaluate whether it truly exists.

detail.abstract: Many regulations condition their own scope on a claim about human involvement: the obligation attaches only when an automated system, not a person, supplies the basis for a decision. The regulated party certifies that claim, and no one verifies it. Where an exemption is keyed to an observable size threshold, harm concentrates among small exempt firms; keyed instead to a declaration costing the same at any scale, the selection inverts and exit concentrates among the largest. Such determinations are rarely recorded. A 2025 U.S. memorandum applies this test to federal AI systems and publicly records every redetermination, making a full population observable. Coding 351 systems' architecture, redetermination is more common where a system routes outputs to a named human before disposition (odds ratio 1.81, p = 0.026), never occurs among 204 systems under independent adjudication, and rests more than a third of the time on justifications with no case-specific content.

detail.abstract: Organizational data often reflect a census or near-census of the workforce, raising questions about how uncertainty should be quantified in repeated workforce metrics. Workforce turnover creates partially overlapping workforce realizations across measurement waves, inducing dependence between wave means and complicating inference about organizational change. We develop a superpopulation framework for inference on change in the expected metric value represented by successive workforce realizations. The framework integrates results for partially overlapping samples with a stayer-leaver-joiner representation, making the contribution of shared employees to covariance between wave means explicit. When outcomes are linked, covariance can be estimated directly. When outcomes are unlinked, a stability-based true-score model operationalizes covariance through a temporal-stability parameter, and Cauchy-Schwarz bounds provide a sensitivity-analysis framework when point identification is not credible. We derive a closed-form variance estimator for the difference between wave means and evaluate its performance using Monte Carlo simulation. Simulations showed that oracle, linked-outcome, and correctly specified stability-based estimators recovered the target variance and maintained nominal 95% confidence-interval coverage. The framework provides an approach for quantifying uncertainty in repeated metrics when membership changes over time.

detail.abstract: Public records of a software problem can support different conclusions about whether its repair is complete. This article examines how linking records changes those conclusions in public weather data services. A comparative document analysis reconstructs four compatibility episodes involving ECMWF forecasts, Open-Meteo, Herbie and provider-maintained retrieval libraries. It compares what specified forum, issue or provider records establish with the additional evidence supplied by linked code, releases and recipient reports. A forum discussion without a completed-fix announcement is connected to a correction published through two dependent packages. An open Herbie issue coexists with a published package containing the proposed compatibility change. In another episode, a recipient confirms satisfactory output within the issue discussion itself; inspecting the code identifies the intervention but does not broaden that confirmation. These differences show why administrative status, implementation, distribution and recipient outcome should be recorded separately. A MeteoSwiss integration and an Open-Meteo capacity problem define the limits of applying the comparison beyond compatibility repair. The article contributes an auditable comparison of completion claims and a reusable procedure for checking their scope. It does not estimate the frequency of misleading tracker states or the proportion of users whose workflows recovered.

detail.abstract:
Background: Digital appointment reminders reduce outpatient non-attendance, but their optimal timing and number remain unclear, and WhatsApp-based strategies have not been evaluated in a Latin American public health system. We compared four WhatsApp reminder strategies.

Methods: We emulated a target trial with routinely collected administrative, scheduling, and electronic health record data from the public provider network of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, Argentina (June 1, 2023, to May 31, 2024). Eligible individuals were usual users with a mobile phone on record and no previous reminder who had booked an in-person outpatient appointment in one of 15 prioritised specialties at least 75 h in advance. Strategies were: reminders at about 72 h and 24 h before the appointment; a single reminder at about 72 h; a single reminder at about 24 h; and no reminder. The primary outcome was non-attendance; secondary outcomes were patient-initiated cancellation overall, within 12 h, and followed by rebooking. Per-protocol effects were estimated by cloning, censoring, and inverse-probability weighting, with 95% CIs from 500 bootstrap resamples.

Findings: 475 214 first eligible person-appointments were included. Non-attendance risk under no reminder was 34·55% (95% CI 34·33–34·77). Compared with no reminder, risk differences were −8·21 percentage points (pp; 95% CI −9·68 to −6·54) for the single 24 h reminder, −7·05 pp (−7·41 to −6·71) for dual reminders, and −3·16 pp (−5·69 to −0·49) for the single 72 h reminder. All active strategies increased patient-initiated cancellations, most markedly dual reminders (risk difference 4·11 pp [3·93–4·28]). The ranking of strategies was preserved across three prespecified sensitivity analyses.

Interpretation: Timing, rather than frequency, drives the effectiveness of digital reminders. A single just-in-time WhatsApp reminder was as effective as a dual schedule and superior to a distal reminder alone, supporting its use as the default strategy in resource-constrained outpatient systems.

Funding: Partially funded by a grant from the Inter-American Development Bank.

detail.abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa must build roads, power systems and digital networks, and expand skills, to close its development gap, yet it is unclear whether these investments move the region towards or away from environmental sustainability. Policy frameworks, from Ghana's Green Growth Strategy to the African Union's Agenda 2063, assume that infrastructure and human capital are complementary levers for green growth. We test that assumption. Building on an extended STIRPAT framework, we construct infrastructure and human-capital indices for 49 Sub-Saharan African countries from public World Bank, ITU, UNDP and UNESCO series, and estimate two-way fixed-effects models with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors over 1990-2023. We complement them with coverage-sensitivity models, leave-one-country-out re-estimation, lagged-infrastructure specifications and quantile regressions. Three findings stand out. First, infrastructure is most robustly associated with the expansion of arable land: a one-standard-deviation rise in the infrastructure index is associated with 1.2 percentage points more land under arable use. The association holds in every fixed-effects specification, survives the omission of any single country and persists at lags of one to three years. Second, infrastructure's associations with natural resource rents (about 8-10 per cent per standard deviation) and with greenhouse gas emissions (only in broad samples) are positive but fragile. Third, the hypothesised synergy finds weak support. The infrastructure × human-capital interaction is negative for resource rents, the pressure-reducing direction, but it is significant only in some specifications and depends on which countries are included; there is no such synergy for emissions or land. Infrastructure in the region therefore appears to be paving an extractive path, towards land conversion and, less firmly, resource dependence, and general human capital only faintly redirects it. We release the data, code and an interactive policy-simulation dashboard so that the results can be scrutinised, updated and used by decision-makers.

detail.abstract: This study provides a rigorous empirical test for motivated memory as a cause for procrastination. In a longitudinal experiment over four weeks, individuals must complete a cumbersome task of unknown length and receive noisy signals about their assigned workload. detail.abstract: Industrial policy is on the rise. A key instrument used by governments is import licensing to protect domestic industries. However, evidence of its effectiveness is limited. Using customs and firm level data, we estimate the effects of the introduction of import licensing for iron and steel products in Indonesia in 2009. While we find that the number of incoming shipments of protected products is reduced, and that imports are sourced from fewer countries, the overall value or quantity of imports is not affected. At the same time, while domestic iron and steel producers increase their sales in the short run, we find that these effects disappear two years after the enactment of the licensing scheme. Our results suggest that while import licensing imposes costs on importers who have to adjust their supply chains, sustained gains for domestic producers are limited. This implies that import licensing is ineffective as an industrial policy.
