detail.abstract:
Every Nationally Determined Contribution assumes that companies will deliver their share of national emissions reductions. This paper tests whether the capital behind that assumption is protected. Across 1,052 of the largest listed companies on twenty-one exchanges in eighteen Asia-Pacific and Middle Eastern economies, 70 (6.7 per cent) hold transition capital ring-fenced against reallocation as at September 2026. Only 11, about one in a hundred, do so by deliberate board choice; the rest are protected by structure or by financial institutions' lending and investment policy. Thirteen of the eighteen economies show little or none of this protection. The pattern recurs across very different economies: it is a feature of the system, not of any one market. On current evidence, there is little protected corporate capital for a sovereign to lean on. 

The evidence already sits in company accounts: supervisors can ask for it now, and central banks can use it as an observed input to scenario work that currently models corporate transition.

title: A Bargaining Theory of the Leverage-Profitability Relationship
affiliations: University of Brescia - Department of Economics and Management

detail.title: A Bargaining Theory of the Leverage-Profitability Relationship
detail.abstract: This paper extends the Leland trade-off model by introducing shareholder creditor bargaining over the perpetual debt coupon. A single parameter ϕ ∈ (0, 1) measures shareholder bargaining power and indexes the deviation of the negotiated coupon from the firm-value-maximising level. The main result is sharp: at the parity configuration ϕ = 1/2, the bargaining solution exactly recovers the Leland firm-value optimum, irrespective of every other parameter of the model. Deviations from parity generate a structural wedge whose direction is signed by ϕ − 1/2. When shareholders dominate (ϕ > 1/2), the negotiated coupon undershoots the value-maximising level and increases in shareholder power push leverage down while pushing earnings yield up, generating the negative leverage–profitability slope documented since Titman & Wessels (1988). When creditors dominate (ϕ < 1/2), the coupon overshoots and the slope reverses sign. The result maps cleanly into accounting data: under fair-value-oriented (IFRS) measurement the leverage–ROA slope inherits the sign pattern in closed form, while under historical-cost (GAAP) measure ment the cross-sectional slope along the bargaining axis is mechanically zero. The model delivers three testable predictions tied to measurable institutional characteristics: shareholder bargaining power, accounting regime, and insolvency efficiency.

detail.abstract: The first three papers in this series established why the Human Layer matters, how to build it, and how to measure it. This paper addresses the question those papers raise but do not answer: if the evidence for augmentation over automation is this consistent, why does capital continue to flow toward replacement? The answer is not that executives are irrational. It is that the current incentive architecture makes removing the human layer structurally rational at the individual and organizational level, while externalizing the costs to a later period, a different line item, and often a different team. This paper identifies three capital incentive structures driving organizations toward automation: venture capital pricing dynamics, AI vendor pricing model evolution, and executive performance measurement. It introduces the concept of organizational automation bias: the systematic institutional tendency to overweight visible, near-term automation benefits and underweight deferred oversight costs. It then documents the three forces now collapsing the temporal gap that makes this externalization possible: regulatory enforcement becoming actualized, insurance and liability pricing beginning to incorporate AI risk, and institutional market access emerging as a gating function rather than a compliance aspiration. The paper closes with an empirically grounded argument, drawn from the SOX, GDPR, and ISO 27001 precedents, that the Human Layer Score introduced in Paper 3 is positioned to function as a capital markets signal for organizations operating in regulated, trust-dependent environments, and that governance infrastructure of this kind has historically been acquired most advantageously in the window before enforcement concentrates the market toward already-compliant actors.

detail.abstract:
Employee behavior is one of the most important factors affecting organizational effectiveness.
Organizations do not operate solely through strategy, financial resources, or technology; they depend on
individuals whose attitudes, emotions, personalities, perceptions, decisions, and motivation shape how
they perform their work. This project examines the relationship between five interconnected areas of
organizational behavior: job attitudes, emotions and moods, personality and individual differences,
perception and individual decision making, and motivation. The research is based on secondary data
drawn from professional and academic sources, including Eurofound's European Working Conditions
Survey 2024 (Eurofound, 2025, 2026), Gallup's State of the Global Workplace 2026 (Gallup, 2026), the
American Psychological Association (2011, 2018), OpenStax's Organizational Behavior textbook (Black
& Bright, 2019), and peer-reviewed psychological and management research. The geographic scope
covers four European countries — Germany, France, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom —
compared with the United States. The evidence shows that job quality is associated with motivation,
engagement, trust, cooperation, and employees' intention to remain with their organization. Eurofound
(2025, 2026) reports that more than 80 percent of European workers considered their work useful and felt
that it was well done, while 85 percent felt fairly treated. Gallup (2026), using data collected in 2025,
reports substantially different levels of employee engagement across countries: 32 percent in the United
States, compared with 14 percent in the Netherlands, 11 percent in Germany, 10 percent in the United
Kingdom, and 8 percent in France. The findings indicate that employee motivation and engagement
cannot be explained by financial reward alone. Job design, recognition, meaningful work, personality
differences, emotional experience, perceived fairness, and the quality of the working environment interact
to shape engagement. The project concludes that managers should treat employee motivation as a
multidimensional organizational issue rather than the product of a single incentive or technique

detail.abstract:
Capital-intensive manufacturing, energy, mining, and infrastructure projects rely heavily on extended supplier networks. In practice, however, the buying organization often has limited visibility into critical upstream dependencies. Traditional supplier qualification processes tend to look at financial stability, technical specs, compliance, quality, safety, and commercial terms as siloed checkboxes. Rarely do these legacy checks account for how critical a specific procurement package actually is to the overall project timeline, nor do they map hidden multi-tier bottlenecks or quantify financial distress objectively.

This practitioner paper introduces an integrated Multi-Tier Supplier Risk Governance Framework (MSRGF) built around four core phases: mapping the supply network, assessing risk at both the supplier and package levels (including an objective 5-pillar quantitative scoring model), deploying targeted mitigations, and maintaining event-driven monitoring post-award. To solve real-world friction, the framework tackles common hurdles head-on—such as cross-functional silos, lean team burnout, and supplier pushback on sub-tier transparency. To ensure immediate operational utility, it concludes with a simple Practitioner Playbook, explicit Package Criticality formulas, a Risk Prioritization Matrix, and a comprehensive Supplier Risk Calculation Matrix. Rather than offering an academic model, it provides a practical decision-making tool that helps procurement professionals turn fragmented supply data into actionable, proportionate contracting and risk management strategies.

detail.abstract: Two bodies of law ask whether an entity possesses consciousness and answer through incompatible procedures. Disorders-of-consciousness doctrine demands maximal diagnostic caution, treating any residual uncertainty as a reason to maintain life-sustaining treatment due to the high moral cost of a false negative. Conversely, artificial-mind and animal-personhood law adopts a strategy of categorical avoidance, resolving personhood questions through functional criteria, capacity-based tests, or designated guardian structures without engaging the question of machine or animal experience. This article coins the term consciousness-attribution asymmetry to describe this pattern, arguing that it reflects distinct institutional risk calculi rather than conflicting philosophical views on consciousness. To address this tension without disrupting institutional functions, the article proposes a modest procedural remedy: evidentiary-direction disclosure, requiring courts and legislatures to state openly which evidentiary direction they apply and why.

detail.abstract: The clean-energy transition is simultaneously a technological, environmental, and workforce transformation. Although research increasingly links artificial intelligence (AI) with green human resource management (GHRM), existing work largely emphasizes efficiency, green behavior, or sustainable performance, leaving the workforce consequences of decarbonization insufficiently theorized. This conceptual article develops a capability-conversion framework explaining how AI-driven GHRM can support a just energy transition through workforce reskilling. Integrating ability-motivation-opportunity theory, the natural resource-based view, and dynamic capabilities theory, the framework positions AI-driven GHRM as an organizational capability that converts transition intelligence into green workforce capabilities through reskilling, redeployment, participation, and responsible performance management. It distinguishes sustainable performance from just-transition outcomes and argues that environmental gains are incomplete when they are achieved through exclusion, occupational downgrading, inequitable access to training, or opaque algorithmic decisions. Responsible AI governance-comprising human oversight, transparency, contestability, employee voice, and distributive justice-is theorized as a cross-cutting boundary condition. Seven propositions specify the relationships among transition pressures, AI-driven GHRM, reskilling, green workforce capability, sustainable performance, and just-transition outcomes. The article contributes to GHRM and AI-HRM scholarship by shifting attention from technology adoption to capability conversion and from aggregate sustainability to the distribution of workforce opportunities, risks, and benefits. A future research agenda outlines longitudinal, multilevel, comparative, and algorithm-audit designs for empirical testing.

keywords: Is Resisting Disease and Extending Life Good? When Does Preservation Become Denial of Creaturely Limits? BCFT-MLAAM-1 v1.0 -Biblical-Theological and Bioethical Monograph medicine

detail.abstract: Medicine presents Christian theology with an apparent paradox. Scripture names death an enemy, records acts of healing as goods, and commands love of neighbor; yet the same biblical canon teaches that human beings are mortal creatures whose days are finite, whose bodies are subject to decay, and whose final hope is resurrection rather than indefinite biological survival. This monograph develops a stewardship-versusfinitude framework for evaluating disease resistance, life extension, intensive treatment, palliative care, and emerging longevity interventions. It argues that resisting disease and extending life are ordinarily genuine goods when they restore or preserve embodied capacities, relieve suffering, protect relational responsibilities, and serve proportionate human flourishing. Nevertheless, preservation of biological life is not an absolute good that overrides every other moral consideration. A treatment may cease to be obligatory when burdens become disproportionate to expected benefits, when intervention no longer serves a patient as an integrated person, when technical possibility is mistaken for moral necessity, or when the project of medicine shifts from caring for mortal persons to treating mortality itself as an engineering defect that must be abolished. Theologically, the crucial distinction is between opposing premature, preventable, or pathological death and denying creaturely mortality as such. Acceptance of death does not require passivity toward disease, and resistance to disease does not require refusal to die. Medicine is most faithful to its vocation when it neither abandons life nor absolutizes it: it heals when possible, relieves suffering when cure is unavailable, accompanies the dying, and recognizes that the conquest of death promised by Christianity is eschatological and divine, not a technological achievement.

title: Bank competition and credit risk: the conditioning role of capital

detail.title: Bank competition and credit risk: the conditioning role of capital
detail.abstract: This paper examines how bank capital conditions the effect of competition on credit risk in lending markets, informing the debate on banking competition, deregulation, and risk-based supervision. Using ECB supervisory data for 146 euro area banks across 19 countries over 2020Q2–2025Q3, we analyze whether this relationship depends on banks’ regulatory capital positions. We find that greater market power is associated with higher subsequent credit risk, while stronger capitalization is associated with lower risk. Crucially, competition reduces credit risk primarily for well-capitalized banks, whereas the effect is weak or absent for banks with lower capital ratios. By aligning the measurement of competition and risk with the pricing-based mechanism, the paper provides a direct empirical test of the borrower-risk channel and offers an explanation for mixed evidence in the competition–risk literature. The results highlight the importance of considering the interaction between competition and prudential capital requirements when assessing financial stability.

title: Tipped Off: Information Leakage in the Municipal Securities Market
affiliations: Yale School of Management, McMaster University - Michael G. DeGroote School of Business, New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business, Yale School of Management and Yale School of Management

detail.title: Tipped Off: Information Leakage in the Municipal Securities Market

detail.abstract: Regulators have long been concerned about the leakage of credit-relevant information in the U.S. municipal securities market. To assess how widespread information leakage is in this market, we examine trading before the announcement of credit rating downgrades. Our findings reveal a marked increase in selling activity in the weeks leading up to a public downgrade announcement, particularly in the week before. This pattern is stronger before severe downgrades, when private information is more valuable. These information transfers likely happen through formal networks; institutional investors are more likely to initiate these sales and selling pressure is stronger when issuers have greater incentives to share information with institutional investors. These patterns persist in the absence of pre-period EMMA disclosures and other observable indicators that could predict downgrades, consistent with the leakage of nonpublic information.

detail.abstract: Our study examines the influence of corporate integrity on capital structure decisions using a novel text-based measure derived from sophisticated textual analysis of earnings conference calls. Using a large sample of U.S. firms spanning 2001–2018, we document a robust negative association between corporate integrity and leverage. Our results are consistent with the interpretation that firms with stronger corporate integrity tend to adopt more conservative financial policies, viewing debt default as a serious ethical violation. We further analyze interaction effects and find that this negative association is significantly weaker for firms with substantial cash holdings and stronger liquidity positions, suggesting that financial flexibility mitigates the costs of leverage even for high-integrity firms. A comprehensive set of robustness checks, including propensity score matching, entropy balancing, and instrumental-variable analyses, supports the stability of our findings. Finally, we show that leverage attributable to corporate integrity is positively related to firm value, as measured by Tobin's Q. Overall, our study highlights the economically meaningful role of corporate culture, particularly integrity, in shaping capital structure choices and firm value.

detail.abstract: Nested logit models are simple to estimate, but nested logit errors have long resisted closed-form simulation. Galichon (2022) resolves a longstanding conjecture to show that nested logit errors decompose into standard Gumbel and positive stable components. I combine this result with the Kanter (1975) representation of positive stable variables to demonstrate a method for simulating error vectors for arbitrary trees. The method is fast, exact, and scales well. Monte Carlo simulations and timing benchmarks demonstrate its advantages over existing methods employing numerical inversion or moment-matching. It is a practical tool for discrete choice applications requiring full vectors of correlated shocks.

title: AI as a Business: Like the Airlines, but Much, Much Worse? Capital Intensity, Depreciation, and the Chimera of Capturing the Gains
affiliations: Scitility PBC

detail.title: AI as a Business: Like the Airlines, but Much, Much Worse? Capital Intensity, Depreciation, and the Chimera of Capturing the Gains

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence will become one of the largest and most useful industries in history. This is hard to doubt. This paper argues that many of the firms, especially those that build its infrastructure, face a serious risk of barely earning their cost of capital or failing to earn it. This implies the right comparison for those firms is not Microsoft or Google in their prime but the airlines, only much, much worse.

This is because, given the speed at which capital must be deployed again and again, AI is much worse than an airline: accelerators have an economic life of four to five years, against decades for an airframe. Under the paper's illustrative asset mix, an installed AI infrastructure stock of about $3.8 trillion, a conservative figure beside current estimates of spending, some 60 percent of it compute and the rest power plant and buildings, carries a replacement bill of roughly $600 billion a year before it earns anything. A trivial calculation then shows that such an enterprise must bring in roughly $1.1 to $1.3 trillion of revenue a year if the cost of capital is between 8 and 12 percent, and close to $900 billion merely to replace itself and cover its operating costs at a zero return. Even if the compute lasts eight years, the fleet must still bring in close to $1 trillion a year to earn its cost of capital.

But there are multiple forces pushing prices down. Frontier capabilities converge, so suppliers become fungible. Learning routers make model identity irrelevant. Competition commoditizes the routers. And portable compilers weaken hardware lock-in. Much of the demand is not "time is of the essence," so idle compute has to be sold much as airlines sell an empty seat. Finally, on sufficiently narrow professional tasks, small models distilled on data the customer owns can do much of the needed work at a small fraction of frontier cost. We will soon arrive in a world where customers can actually build their own "planes."

The labor savings from automation are real and will likely run to trillions of dollars a year. But there is no reason to believe, especially given that open models trained on a customer's data will be so much cheaper, that the savings will flow to the companies providing the frontier models. Instead they will flow to the buyers of intelligence and, through competition among those buyers, to their customers. The builders of the "fleet" potentially face massive losses on the capital sunk in the buildout. A formal model shows why the survivors should then expect ordinary returns at best. Open weights, which no bankruptcy removes, turn the supply of intelligence below the open frontier into an approximately free-entry business wherever serving is standardized, and a rival paid by a complementary business can rationally run the token business at a loss.

detail.abstract: This study extends quantile-regression analysis by introducing the concept of geometric heterogeneity, which examines whether predictive relationships differ in the shape of their response surfaces across conditional quantiles. Using quarterly data for Chinese CSI 300 constituent stocks from 2005 to 2025, we integrate quarterly double sorting with linear and nonlinear quantile regression to estimate quantile-specific response surfaces for Growth and Valuation characteristics. The empirical results reveal substantial cross-quantile differences in interaction patterns, curvature, and the spatial configuration of predicted returns, beyond conventional coefficient heterogeneity. Quantile-difference surfaces further identify where favorable and unfavorable return outcomes diverge within the characteristic space. The findings indicate that return predictability is better characterized by a family of quantile-specific nonlinear response surfaces than by a single conditional-mean relation. The proposed framework extends the interpretation of quantile regression beyond coefficient comparisons and provides an interpretable approach for analyzing heterogeneous predictive structures in empirical economic and financial research.

detail.abstract: Multi-factor stock-selection strategies require not only the choice of relevant signals but also the allocation of importance across them. Yet conventional weighting approaches typically produce particular weight vectors without systematically characterizing how portfolio performance varies over the constrained factor-weight space. This study develops a mixture-design framework for factor allocation in weighted-scoring stock selection. Using five signals-price-to-book ratio (PB), return on equity (ROE), market capitalization (MV), Beta, and prior-quarter return scored in the reversal direction (MOM)-the framework combines a five-component simplexcentroid design, historical portfolio backtesting, second-order Scheffé response-surface modeling, and constrained optimization. Thirty-one structured factor-weight combinations are evaluated using quarterly data for CSI 300 stocks, and continuous surfaces are estimated for portfolio return, risk, and the Sharpe ratio. The empirical results show that portfolio outcomes vary materially with the joint composition of factor weights. The estimated surfaces exhibit economically meaningful nonlinearities across factor combinations, indicating that the consequences of a factor allocation cannot be inferred from standalone factor performance alone. Optimization of the fitted return and risk surfaces further shows that the return-maximizing factor composition changes as the admissible level of portfolio risk varies, generating a Factor Synergy Frontier in factor-weight space. In addition, period-specific Sharpe-ratio optimization reveals substantial shifts in the location of the optimal allocation across subperiods, providing descriptive evidence that the estimated optimal factor composition varies across the realized subperiods. These findings position factor weighting as a constrained and potentially timevarying allocation problem rather than as a one-time choice of fixed signal weights. The study contributes an integrated framework for mapping and optimizing factor compositions and extends the analysis of time-varying factor performance from individual signals to optimal multi-factor allocations.

detail.abstract: Abstention by a language-model trading agent is not neutral: the agents do not disagree with the rule that has their inputs, they abstain, and for an agent that holds a position an abstention is a sale avoided. We run a preregistered paper-trading system in which three agents decide daily trades in five ETFs beside the moving-average rule on the same price inputs. In 262 live and 2,173 anonymised historical decisions the agents opposed the rule in 0% and 1.1% of cases, with no detectable gain. A larger model, on 300 points that over-represent days on which the close is within two per cent of a long-term (150-day) moving average, opposed it 1 time and abstained on 80% of those days. A calendar of scheduled macroeconomic events changed 64 decisions, 59 of them into abstentions; this is a change of behaviour, and we find no improvement in quality. Live, the agent ledgers and the rule ledgers hold different positions on about one asset-day in five, and the consensus gate between agents blocked 22 decisions, all of them sales. The abstention depends on one sentence of the prompt: replacing it with an instruction to commit lowers the abstention rate from 55% to 19%, and the released decisions follow the rule. The same input sent twice changes 9% of decisions. We propose a minimal evaluation protocol for agent papers. The results cover two models from one provider and a short live record.

detail.abstract: The United States is weighing a 90-day ban on diesel exports. We ask whether such a ban lowers gasoline stock cover in Indonesian provinces, which import most of their gasoline from Singapore and Malaysia. We link a three-level computable general equilibrium model of world, national, and provincial fuel markets to a refinery satellite and a daily stock module. A full ban raises Indonesia's delivered refined-fuel price by 1.82 percent, but refiners shifting output toward diesel withdraw 28.8 thousand barrels per day of gasoline, 7.38 percent of Indonesia's gasoline imports before replacement cargoes. Domestic refineries replace 1.7 percent of the fall in imports. We derive a cover threshold: a province falls below a 7-day stock only if its initial cover is below about 8.7 days under a full ban, or 12.3 days under stress. The threshold classifies all 34 provinces correctly. A 15-day provincial stock floor removes every shortfall in the stress case.

detail.abstract: We ask what a simple trend-abstention rule delivers to a retail investor with a small account, and what it does not. The rule holds each of five US-listed ETFs while its price is above a 150-day moving average and refuses new entries when the long-term trend is broken. Over 2004-11-18 to 2026-09-04, with dividends, next-open fills and costs, it earns 7.7% a year against 10.7% for buy-and-hold, with the same Sharpe ratio (0.71 against 0.73; Ledoit-Wolf 𝑝 = 0.89) and a maximum drawdown of 13.5% against 31.8%. The return is fully explained by market and time-series-momentum exposure (alpha 0.47% a year, 𝑡 = 0.45), and the rule is statistically indistinguishable from the ten-month rule of Faber (2007). After deflating for the 91 configurations we tried, its Sharpe ratio is not significant. What survives is protection: the drawdown reduction holds in 98% of bootstrap resamples and in 55 of 56 ETFs outside the universe. Two abstention devices we designed first, a volatility gate and a circuit breaker, did not work. An average income of KRW 5,000 per trading day requires about KRW 16.2 million under this rule; with KRW 3 million it would require a return of 42% a year. The main claims rest on backtests; the preregistered live record is too short to test them.

title: AI Displacement without Immiseration: A Ricardian Perspective on Jagged AI Growth
affiliations: Department of Economics

detail.abstract: We develop and estimate a Ricardian model of labor displacement under explosive AI growth. A key feature of the model is that agentic AI, though jagged, can hold an absolute advantage over humans in every task. Yet wages rise as AI displaces labor, with an elasticity governed by the jaggedness of the AI capability frontier. At the macro level, explosive but jagged AI growth generates unbounded growth in the average wage. At the micro level, every worker can gain without switching sectors, provided AI capabilities are jagged but adoption is sufficiently even across sectors to prevent Baumol's cost disease. We estimate the jaggedness of the AI frontier from micro data comparing human and AI costs on similar tasks, and calibrate the jaggedness of adoption to occupation-level measures of AI exposure. The estimated model matches the untargeted wage effects of AI growth observed over 2022-25. If AI capabilities keep growing at their current pace but remain jagged, the model predicts that average real wages will rise 3.5% per year over the next five years, even as labor is displaced from 30% of tasks. If the AI frontier were five times less jagged than estimated, displacement would be larger and real wage gains would all but vanish. Distributional effects are modest: every education group gains, even without switching sectors, simply by taking over tasks in AI's blind spots. These results suggest that AI growth, despite its scale, may be less immiserizing than earlier labor-saving technologies such as trade or engines, because its capability frontier is more jagged and its adoption more even across the economy.

detail.abstract: Geographic market integration changes not only where production takes place, but also which firms compete and which find it profitable to operate. We study these margins in the Yunnan-Guangdong electricity market, where substantial physical transfers predated the introduction of coordinated cross-provincial spot trading. We combine hourly evidence from China's Southern Regional Electricity Market pilot with a two-region Cournot model of transmission constraints and annual supplier participation. Pilot hours are associated with higher imports into Guangdong and lower local thermal generation, system marginal costs, and price-cost markups. We then compare segmented markets with counterfactual arrangements that introduce crossprovincial reallocation, cross-regional competition, and endogenous supplier participation in turn. Reallocation contributes the most to Guangdong's price decline, while competition and participation together account for approximately 37% of it. Markups fall sharply in Guangdong, while in Yunnan the trade-induced increase is offset once the two regions clear as a single market. Integration raises market surplus by approximately 29.4 billion RMB but raises emissions by approximately 68.9 million tonnes, because the expansion in Yunnan exceeds the contraction in Guangdong. Integration is therefore a trade, competition, and supply-structure reform at once, whose gains depend on transmission access and on the carbon policy applied to the long-run supply response.

detail.abstract: Since 2003, 28 U.S. states have enacted permitless carry laws, allowing concealed carry of handguns by legal gun owners without a specific permit to do so. Employing a difference-in-differences approach in annual state panel data spanning 2000 to 2023, we find that relative to a baseline of shall issue laws, which require a permit for concealed carry but with minimal costs and qualifications beyond those of gun ownership, permitless carry adoption has raised handgun death rates by a statistically significant 3.9 percent on average. This response is attributable primarily to a rise in handgun homicides, and handgun suicide and unintentional handgun deaths likewise are significantly increased, while long gun and nongun deaths are unaffected. The significant handgun homicide effect is observed in both CDC and FBI data, and is accompanied by a nearly nine percent increase in aggravated assaults by gun and large rises in forced entry burglaries and overall theft. Corresponding jumps in the prevalence of licensed gun dealers and background checks for handgun purchases, but not non-dealer/firearm licensees or long gun checks, suggest that the laws elevate the perceived net benefit of handgun ownership.

detail.abstract: State Attorneys General, along with private agents and the federal government, play a role in enforcing competition laws. While investigating a firm for anticompetitive conduct, State Attorneys General may uncover additional instances of misconduct within the industry, an informational spillover that may impact future enforcement patterns. I investigate these informational spillovers using a National Association of Attorneys General (NAAG) dataset listing all antitrust cases filed by State Attorneys General from 2005 to 2023. Estimating a model with state-year and industry-year fixed effects using the Poisson Pseudo Maximum Likelihood (PPML) estimator, I find that there is a positive and statistically significant relationship between the number of cases that a State Attorney General files against firms in an industry and the number of cases in previous years that the official filed against firms in that industry. My preferred model specification predicts that each additional case in the previous year is expected to increase the number of cases in current year by 45.5%. This paper is the first, to my knowledge, to explore the determinants of state-level antitrust enforcement with data at the state-industry-year level. * I would like to thank Christiaan Hogendorn for his advice and guidance. Moreover, I would like to thank Abigail Hornstein and David Kuenzel for their help. Lastly, I want to thank my parents for their unwavering support throughout my academic career.

detail.abstract: Smart grids couple electrical infrastructure with communication, computing, and control layers, and this coupling has created an attack surface that conventional, rule-based protections were not designed to cover. Machine learning (ML) has become a prominent response, with a substantial body of work applying supervised, unsupervised, and deep learning methods to false data injection (FDI) detection, network intrusion detection, and the discrimination of cyber-attacks from natural disturbances. This paper reviews that literature critically rather than exhaustively. It synthesizes published surveys and representative primary studies across three detection layers (measurement and state estimation, communication and protocol traffic, and substation or field devices) and examines how datasets, evaluation practices, and modelling assumptions shape the conclusions that can be drawn. Three recurring weaknesses emerge: heavy reliance on simulated benchmark systems, limited attention to adversarial robustness and concept drift, and a shortage of work that connects detector output to operator decision-making. Building on these observations, the paper proposes a conceptual, layered framework in which cross-layer detection, privacy-preserving collaborative learning, explainability, and operator-in-theloop response are treated as design requirements rather than optional extensions. The framework is presented as a set of testable propositions and has not been empirically validated. No new experiments or datasets are reported. The paper closes with practical implications for utilities and a research agenda focused on realistic evaluation, robustness, and integration with existing security operations.

Machine-learning systems are often evaluated with data partitions that do not match the structure of intended deployment. This study examines how deployment-aligned holdouts constrain the generalization claims that can be supported across two heterogeneous applied-learning tasks. The paper does not estimate a formal magnitude of distribution shift and does not compare structured holdouts against random splitting; instead, it asks what evidence is defensible when time or geography is used as the unit of separation and the final holdout is excluded from development. Case I uses 17,379 hourly Capital Bikeshare observations (2011-2012) under a conservative monthly temporal protocol. Among the reported forecasting configurations, a weather-enhanced Histogram Gradient Boosting model produced the lowest observed errors (MAE 36.59, RMSE 61.88, RMSLE 0.461) on 5,919 evaluation observations, a 52.6% lower MAE than the historical baseline under the same protocol. The preserved notebook also shows lower HGB-weather MAE than the baseline in every plotted monthly evaluation window. Case II uses an author-defined cross-city split of the Inria Aerial Image Labeling dataset: Austin, Chicago, and Kitsap for training, Tyrol-W for validation, and labeled Vienna imagery as a held-out final evaluation city. A deterministic seed-42 U-Net/ResNet-34 execution achieved mean IoU 0.588, Dice 0.716, Precision 0.635, Recall 0.886, and Boundary F1 0.297 on 576 sampled Vienna patches. A sensitivity analysis restricted to the 543 patches containing building pixels produced similar region metrics, and retained qualitative failure cases expose substantial false positives and boundary errors. The contribution is a bounded claim-evidence reporting discipline supported by preserved computational artifacts, not a new learning algorithm or a universal robustness result.

detail.abstract: This article examines the relationship among border workload, agency capacity, and U.S. asylum adjudication times during FY2021-FY2024. The analysis draws on data from U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, the Executive Office for Immigration Review, the Government Accountability Office, and oversight bodies within the Department of Homeland Security. The measures are interpreted in light of the distinctions among recorded encounters, unique individuals, applications, court proceedings, and case completions. The aggregate tables used here do not expose record-level identifiers or permit reconstruction of a cohort through every stage of the asylum process. The article therefore combines descriptive comparisons with analysis of administrative pathways and does not attribute observed changes to any single policy measure or administration. Between FY2021 and FY2024, the pending immigration court caseload rose from 1.69 million to 3.92 million, while the number of judges increased from 559 to 735. EOIR's July 2026 revised historical table placed the FY2024 year-end asylum inventory at 2.53 million applications; the October 2024 snapshot reported 1.48 million. USCIS had 1.37 million principal applicants with pending applications in its affirmative asylum caseload. Growth in completions did not stop the backlog from expanding. During the period, the end of Title 42 border expulsions, expanded appointment scheduling at ports of entry, the Circumvention of Lawful Pathways rule, and the 2024 restrictions changed formal routing and screening requirements. Here, systemic overload describes a persistent pattern in which pending inventories grow despite higher output or staffing, together with documented episodes in which resources are moved from one queue to another. The article proposes three directions for evaluating the system: joint resource planning, case management that accounts for case age and readiness, and cohort-based reporting that distinguishes access to process, merits decisions, and procedural dispositions.

title: The Electoral Consequences of High-Profile Police Violence

detail.abstract: How do salient acts of state-linked violence reshape electoral politics? This paper studies this question in the context of high-profile police killings in the United States. Using a differencein-differences design, I find that exposure shifts partisan vote shares from Republican toward Democratic candidates across multiple electoral contests, while effects on turnout are mixed. The shift is larger following incidents that receive greater media attention, generate more protest activity, involve racial minority victims, or involve gunfire. In contrast, total police killings have substantially smaller electoral effects, underscoring the role of public salience in translating police violence into electoral consequences.

detail.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to introduce a fully integrated, risk-informed, probabilistic framework that carries over seamlessly from enterprise portfolio decision making to operational risk and opportunity management.  It accomplishes this function by adhering to the following six principles and premises:  (1) that quantitative, probabilistic risk analysis and management methods need to be used not only at the level of projects and programs, but also for enterprise portfolio planning and execution;  (2) that success at enterprise level requires continuously considering not only the financial, safety, security, and technical gains that emanate from mission accomplishment, but also potential aspirational gains that are not directly quantifiable at the time planning occurs;  (3) that the consideration of aspirational gains requires tapping into the insights and tacit knowledge of stakeholders and other affected parties by introducing and applying affective performance measures (e.g., their degrees of enthusiasm or concern);  (4) that a key element of the analysis should be the initial derivation of an integrated resource allocation scheme and its subsequent updating to continually optimize the balance between competing objectives;  (5) that the first four premises motivate the use of Monte Carlo methods to account for all important sources of uncertainty; and (6) that the overall methodology should be extendable to decision-making arenas that require national and international cooperation such as AI and climate change.  The paper presents a formalism that accommodates these and other related principles and premises and demonstrates how the results of the analyses can be effectively communicated to management.

detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of a compounding crisis like war and pandemic, businesses have not had it so difficult before and thus require resilience, the ability to adapt, and be in tune with society. An example of such an adaptive business model is Ankor Pharm, a pharmaceutical chain operating in Odesa, Ukraine, a country adversely affected by the course of the war in Ukraine. Since its inception in 2003, the establishment has integrated quality control, service-driven innovation, functional flexibility, and access to the community to support business continuity during the war. Based on the information provided on the web resource www.ankor.od.ua and using such theoretical concepts as dynamic capabilities and supply chain resilience, this paper comments on the ability of Ankor Pharm to respond to disruption and continue providing services and generating trust. Through certified qualities of supply chains, socioeconomic addition program, 24/7 with delivery, in-house, and community-oriented services, Ankor Pharm provides an extensive business model in crisis-affected situations. The article is informative to the firms which intend to gain a balance between efficiency, resilience and social responsibility in a volatile environment.

detail.abstract: Organisations that want to govern the use of generative AI need to talk about AI tools as groups, organised by what each tool does. We present a two-level functional taxonomy of AI tools with 18 categories and 165 subcategories, applied to a register of 11,890 active AI tools observed on 26 September 2026. Tools carry on average 1.97 subcategory labels, and 34 subcategories account for half of all subcategory labels. Established products with added AI features ("AI-enabled") make up 11.3% of tools overall, but a quarter in marketing and in data and analytics, where AI often arrives as a new feature in software that organisations already use. We then examine the stated training policies of 9,853 tools whose policy documents we analysed. Only 7.0% state that customer inputs are used for training by default and 18.8% state that they are not; 72.0% state no policy at all. The share of tools that state no policy is highest in customer support, marketing and vertical business software, and lowest in design and productivity tools. We argue that functional categories combined with policy statistics give acceptable-use policies and AI inventories a practical level of description between individual products and AI as a whole. The taxonomy counts and statistics are released as open datasets.

title: Attitudes and Perceptions Towards Advanced Automation in the Nuclear Domain
affiliations: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, Finnish Institute of Occupational Health, Finnish Institute of Occupational Health, Finnish Institute of Occupational Health, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

detail.title: Attitudes and Perceptions Towards Advanced Automation in the Nuclear Domain
detail.abstract: This study examined the attitudes and perceptions of main control room (MCR) operators at a Finnish Evolutionary Power Reactor (EPR) nuclear power plant (NPP) towards advanced automation systems a few years after the plant’s commissioning. The analysis draws on group and individual interviews and on results from the revised Automation-Induced Complacency Potential Scale (AICP-R). The interview themes were based on a conceptual model of the association between automation features and automation attitudes and perceptions. Seven operating crews, 28 operators in total, participated in the interview sessions. The respondents viewed advanced automation as essential to plant operation but emphasised the need for human supervision, especially during failures. They generally trusted automation in routine tasks but monitored it closely and were prepared to intervene manually when necessary. The complexity of automation systems and the possibility of failures underline the importance of training, clear procedures, and close collaboration with maintenance personnel. The findings suggest that attitudes towards automation evolve with experience and with improvements in system reliability and operator competence.

title: Propagation and Deterrence of Unpunishable Collusion in Networks
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) and  Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

detail.title: Propagation and Deterrence of Unpunishable Collusion in Networks
detail.abstract:
We study how communication networks shape the formation and deterrence of collusive
coalitions. Consider a principal who faces agents who can seize the surplus if a sufficiently large
coalition forms; once this threshold is reached, the coalition can conceal the deviation and avoid
punishment. We model this problem as a sequential bargaining game on a network, where an
initiator recruits agents through communication links and the principal can commit to rewards
for agents who refuse to join.
The model delivers a network-specific critical threshold: collusion is robustly deterrable if
and only if the required coalition size exceeds this threshold. The threshold is computable
for arbitrary networks and increases weakly with the addition of communication links. Thus,
denser networks make collusion harder to deter by giving initiators redundant recruitment paths.
Complete networks are most vulnerable, while rings and appropriately incentivized star networks
are most resistant.
We test these predictions in two experiments. Collusion success falls sharply when the
required coalition size crosses the predicted threshold, and success rates generally follow the
theoretical ordering across networks. The results provide a game-theoretic and experimental
account of how network structure determines the limits of internal governance.

detail.abstract: Credit union growth is commonly evaluated through assets, loans, earnings, and membership, but these outcomes do not independently establish whether an institution has increased its capacity to serve members through changing conditions. This conceptual and practitioner-oriented article examines growth as a leadership decision that connects cooperative purpose, risk appetite, lending discipline, organizational culture, board oversight, and member outcomes. It integrates the author's published phenomenological study of 16 U.S. credit union executives with research on organizational culture and learning, National Credit Union Administration data and guidance, and the International Cooperative Alliance's principles. The article develops a purposecapacity-risk-learning framework and illustrates how boards and management can pair growth measures with indicators of credit quality, operational capacity, member experience, and institutional resilience. The proposed framework is an interpretive synthesis rather than a validated predictive model. Sustainable growth, in this account, is growth that expands a credit union's ability to deliver durable member value without outrunning its capital, liquidity, controls, talent, or cooperative identity.

detail.abstract: The prospective disintegration of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan constitutes a decisive inflection point for postwar stabilization and the reconstitution of the security sector. This study synthesizes disarmament, demobilization and reintegration (DDR) scholarship, transitional justice (TJ) theory, and empirical lessons from Sierra Leone, Liberia, Colombia and Rwanda to develop an integrated operational model for handling RSF defectors who seek alignment with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF). Expanding the eight-point operational outline proposed by El Fatih and Al Mardi (2024), the paper offers a theoretically anchored and evidence-informed blueprint that reconciles security imperatives, juridical accountability and social reconciliation. It interrogates recurrent failures of Sudanese DDR efforts (Ibrahim, 2011; Saeed, 2024), the hybrid Gacaca experience as a community-based justice innovation (Mokoena & Nshimiyimana, 2025), Colombia's collective reincorporation model (Harvard Review, 2025), and recent advances in integrating mental health and psychosocial support into DDR programming (P-DDRCS, 2025). The proposed framework sequences cantonment, individualized screening, tiered accountability, conditional reintegration and community-led reconciliation, supported by original visualizations and an implementation timeline. The analysis contends that DDR without rigorous vetting risks reproducing violence, whereas a context-sensitive merger of DDR, SSR and transitional justice can advance sustainable peace and a professional, accountable military.

detail.abstract: The current wave of artificial intelligence cannot be measured solely by the technical progress of its models. This paper argues that it must instead be understood through three interlocking consequences: a change in the logic of knowledge production and verification; a redistribution of control over computational and data infrastructure as a new source of power; and a legitimacy crisis that arises when machine output enters the human decision chain. These three axes, knowledge, power, and legitimacy, cannot be fully understood in isolation from one another. The paper traces the technical shift from models to tool-using agents, distinguishes output, information, and verified knowledge, proposes measurable proxies for the otherwise diffuse concept of "control," and develops four analytical scenarios for the sector's near-term trajectory, illustrated with a worked country example. Empirical claims are kept explicitly separate from analytical inference and scenario-based speculation throughout, and the paper states its own evidentiary limitations directly, including uneven empirical depth in its economic sections, rather than leaving them implicit.

title: Process Optimization of Thermal Laser Separation (TLS) to Minimize Cutting-Induced Losses in HJT Solar Cells
affiliations: Contrada Blocco Torrazze s.n, Contrada Blocco Torrazze s.n, Contrada Blocco Torrazze s.n, Contrada Blocco Torrazze s.n, CNR IMM, CNR IMM and Contrada Blocco Torrazze s.n

detail.title: Process Optimization of Thermal Laser Separation (TLS) to Minimize Cutting-Induced Losses in HJT Solar Cells
detail.abstract:
Thermal Laser Separation (TLS) has emerged as a key technology for the dicing of high-efficiency Silicon Heterojunction (HJT) solar cells. However, the cutting process if not well managed can introduce significant edge recombination and mechanical stress, leading to Cell-to-Module (CTM) efficiency losses.
After examining the various cell separation processes and evaluating their impact on HJT technology, this study presents a technological and operational best practice for the systematic optimization of the TLS process and equipment parameters to mitigate the cutting-induced losses. By implementing a rigorous control of process water quality and a fine-tuning of the laser power for both the scribing and cleave stages, the cutting-induced degradation was significantly minimized. Furthermore, the optimization of the drying temperature ensured the removal of residual moisture without compromising the passivation layers.
Notably, the study confirms the process versatility, showing no discernible impact on performance regardless of whether the laser cutting is performed on the front or the back of the cell. 
Although ultimate loss-free cell cutting is potentially achievable with the assistance of edge passivation, these findings provide a robust framework for high-yield dicing in industrial HJT production lines, preserving the high-efficiency potential of the heterojunction architecture.

title: Breach Risk and Life Loss of Cascade Reservoirs with Upstream-Large and Downstream-Small Storage Under Extreme Floods by a Physics-Trained Surrogate
affiliations: Beijing University of Technology, Beijing University of Technology, Beijing University of Technology, China Institute of Water Resources and Hydropower Research (IWHR) - State Key Laboratory of Simulation and Regulation of Water Cycle in River Basin, Beijing University of Technology, Beijing University of Technology, Beijing University of Technology and Beijing University of Technology

detail.title: Breach Risk and Life Loss of Cascade Reservoirs with Upstream-Large and Downstream-Small Storage Under Extreme Floods by a Physics-Trained Surrogate
detail.abstract: The need for quantitative frameworks to assess cascading dam-break risk is increasingly critical as climate change and continued dam construction in mountainous river basins increase the potential for catastrophic flood events. Engineers and risk managers require reliable methodologies to estimate breach probability and life loss for emergency planning. This study develops the MDMHP system, coupling Monte Carlo simulation with DB-IWHR, Muskingum, and HEC-RAS to propagate parameter uncertainty through the full physical cascade chain. A deep learning surrogate (PG-TCANet-LTD) was trained to replace HEC-RAS for large-ensemble simulations, achieving near-exact agreement while reducing computation time from 150 minutes to 3 seconds per simulation—a speedup of 3,000 times. Sobol sensitivity analysis identified the upstream flood peak scaling factor (first-order: 0.32; total-effect: 0.38), lateral erosion coefficient (total-effect: 0.22), and peak timing scaling factor (total-effect: 0.11) as the dominant controls. Applied to the Changheba–Huangjinping cascade, the downstream overtopping probability reached 99.7%. A grid-based mortality model assessed life loss under three warning scenarios (no warning, 0.5 h, and 1.0 h). Expected casualties decreased from 5,816 to 2,500 to 541—a reduction exceeding 90%. The framework enables probabilistic risk assessment for cascade reservoirs where historical breach data are unavailable. The quantified relationship between warning time and life loss reduction provides a basis for emergency planning. In the case study, a 1-hour warning reduced casualties by over 90% compared to no warning, offering decision-makers a quantifiable metric for prioritizing early warning investments.

detail.abstract: This article examines the multidimensional nature of doctoral student success, going beyond just degree completion. It highlights key factors contributing to success, including supportive supervision, scholarly community, flexible program design, research rigor, and professional relevance. The literature reviewed suggests that doctoral success encompasses not only intellectual and procedural mastery, but also professional identity development, knowledge application, and sustained use of doctoral knowledge beyond graduation. However, the evidence is fragmented, with mostly conceptual, discipline-specific, or small-sample studies. The article identifies a need for longitudinal, multi-institutional research to better understand how relational, programmatic, and institutional factors influence the doctoral journey from beginning to end.

title: A Falsificationist Cycle Analysis of Cryptocurrencies

detail.title: A Falsificationist Cycle Analysis of Cryptocurrencies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Cryptoverso (Logika.studio), which develops and sells educational products, books and analysis software related to market cycle analysis, including tools based on the detector studied in this paper. The cycle detector and its calibration are proprietary and are described but not released; the evidence files needed to verify every reported result are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23004322. No other competing interests.

detail.abstract:
For more than half a century, the cycle analysis of markets has produced rich conceptual frameworks that have rarely been subjected to empirical falsification. The three historical schools — classical American (Hurst), Italian (battleplan and inverse cycle) and quantitative DSP (Ehlers) — are adopted as alternative doctrines, almost never tested jointly on a statistically relevant sample. This work formalizes a Popperian protocol that puts each founding claim of the three schools to the test on a multi-asset dataset — Bitcoin and Ethereum since 2017, Solana since 2020, extended to thirty-seven instruments in six classes and to six stock indices with up to ninety-nine years of daily history — over several thousand phased hierarchical cycles.
The methodology is causal by construction and deterministic, and both properties are formalized in automated tests. The non-repainting of the module that detects Bayer tongues, tested in walk-forward mode over the whole series, holds — with a maturity margin derived from the measured latency — on every asset/timeframe combination that can be tested, but one of the five cannot be tested yet: it is therefore not proven, not demonstrated. To this scaffolding the protocol adds four requirements, which are the part of the work that outlives the individual results: the null value of a measure must be measured, not assumed, with surrogate series that preserve the power spectrum and destroy the temporal structure; a conditional rate must be accompanied by its own marginal, that is, by the same condition counted on the cases the event does not select; a negative outcome does not count until it has been shown that the test would recognize the phenomenon if it were there; and every level must be measured on the timeframe that resolves it, because the daily timeframe does not separate the shortest levels of the hierarchy and measuring them there changes the very numbers under discussion.
The results refute the most exposed canonical assertions: Hurst’s fixed harmonic nesting and the principle of harmonicity — the latter with a test whose power is verified on a true synthetic scale, where on the daily ruler none of the markets with enough peaks turns out to be closer to the rungs than a set of periods drawn at random from the same grid —, the sequential mean-reversion of durations, Bayer’s canonical threshold for connecting cycles, the peak hold, and — by tautology — two claims of the Italian school: the inverse cycle, whose operational definition is not falsifiable ex ante, and the unconditional swing, whose success condition is true almost always even without the swing — in all the parent cycles of the daily, and in at least nine out of ten on every ruler. They confirm, with statistical significance and cross-asset convergence, the cyclic commonality of durations — strong at the short levels and, on long history, equally strong at the high levels —, cyclical translation as a predictor of polarity, the violation of the previous peak and, in a rewritten form that eliminates a set-theoretic inclusion, the two bearish signals of the Italian corpus.
The same yardstick applies to the regularities the work could claim as its own, and there it is more severe. The short-cycle tail, measured against one hundred phase-randomized surrogates and one hundred AAFT per market with each level on the ruler that resolves it, leaves the cloud in one asset/level combination out of thirty-three, below the falsification threshold: it is what the detector produces, not what the market does. The same holds for the deviation from the nominal period and for the position of the peak within the cycle. And the work’s starting axiom, according to which a quaternary structure would be a binary of binaries, cannot be decided with this instrument: the trough that would separate the two binaries is the lowest of the three internal ones in 1.3% of the 557 measured cycles, within the band that the same detector produces on noise; and on synthetic series in which the binary of binaries is implanted, the detector never recovers it in numbers sufficient to vote.
The contribution is threefold: a falsifiable and reproducible protocol applied uniformly to the whole corpus, regardless of the origin of the assertion; the verification of causality and determinism of the central analytical component, with non-repainting measured over the whole series instead of on a few points; and the systematic distinction between what the market produces and what the detector produces, which on several occasions changes the sign of a conclusion — to the point of removing, among the regularities this work could have claimed as its own, those that seemed most solid.

title: Post-Acquisition Investment in Acquired Human Capital: Navigating the Risk of Turnover
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, INSEAD - Strategy and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Post-Acquisition Investment in Acquired Human Capital: Navigating the Risk of Turnover
detail.abstract: Post-acquisition employee turnover in acquired firms is both common and detrimental, especially in deals motivated by opportunities to generate additional revenue. Investing in employees following the acquisition may help to reduce such turnover. Yet, because employees may leave, firms must be judicious in their investments in acquired employees, and little is known under what conditions and how firms make such post-acquisition investments in employees. Our unique sample of growth-oriented acquisitions includes detailed data on human capital investments (training and compensation) to examine when and how acquirers invest in acquired employees. We find post-acquisition employee investment increases for a large majority of targets. To mitigate the threat of turnover, acquirers are more likely to invest in employees when anticipated integration frictions are greater and when external labor markets are buoyant (increased turnover risk), as well as when they are more dependent on acquired human capital and knowledge is embedded in employees (increased turnover cost). Surprisingly, employee investments were highest in acquisitions seeking to leverage the target's products as opposed to its innovative capabilities as we had predicted. Overall, our study advances research on acquisitions, strategic human capital, and corporate strategy.

detail.abstract: Allowances in the EU ETS are allocated, surrendered and cancelled at the installation, but the competitiveness literature estimates at the firm and proxies exposure by the static annual net position. We return the expanded dynamic allowance balance of a companion paper to the level at which it is built. Among plants that keep operating the accumulated position does little: it enters log emissions with a coefficient of-0.028 that survives firm×year fixed effects, and the carbon price has no identified installation-level emission effect. The same position is strongly informative about which plants close. An exhausted balance raises the closure hazard by a fifth, and within a multi-plant firm the plant with the thinnest buffer relative to its own throughput closes first. Because the exposure measure loads three times more heavily on plants that eventually close than on survivors, part of what would read as abatement is capacity being run down on its way out. Retired capacity is only partly replaced, and 88.9 per cent of the non-surrendered stock of closing accounts returns to circulation rather than being cancelled. The scheme has worked through the extensive margin more than the intensive one, a distinction the Total Number of Allowances in Circulation cannot make.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the paradigm shift in the legal services industry as technology reshapes legal products, processes and service delivery. It considers how regulatory liberalisation, alternative legal service providers, artificial intelligence and changing client expectations altered competitive pressures on traditional law firms. Using Porter’s competitive framework, it evaluates strategic responses including legal technology adoption, outsourcing, service diversification, unbundling and alternative fee arrangements, alongside ethical issues of transparency, competence, confidentiality, data protection and human oversight. The paper argues that technological adaptation can create substantial operational and client-service benefits where firms implement appropriate governance and risk controls, and concludes by considering implications for ethical, regulatory and legal frameworks.

detail.abstract: We propose a distribution-free test of whether a systematic trading strategy generates a structural edge-one invariant across instruments, volatility regimes, and time-as opposed to regimecontingent returns, using only the trade-level R-multiple output and no access to the signal. Because a strategy with no edge can be distributionally invariant by construction, an invariance score alone is insufficient; we combine two orthogonal gates, one for the significance of the mean return and one for distributional invariance tested component by component against a Monte-Carlo null. We measure the edge on the raw directional return, which is free of any stop or target parameter, and show that judging it on a fixed reward-to-risk payoff instead would make the verdict depend on an arbitrary stop. The empirical application is built entirely on free, publicly available data: fourteen publicly specified trading strategies are reconstructed over 2008-2025, and none clears the edge gate. A proprietary FX strategy, regenerated on the same public price series and entering the test through its trade-level output alone, clears both gates (t = 3.64, N = 582). A placebo permutation, a graded sensitivity experiment and a Monte-Carlo power study calibrate the invariance gate and establish the sample size it requires. The framework is complementary to backtest-overfitting diagnostics and to factor attribution.

detail.abstract: Federal acquisition reform has repeatedly changed the practitioner and left unchanged the chain of review, audit, protest, and appropriation the practitioner works inside; the chain has prevailed each time. This note proposes Corridor Management as the concept that addresses the chain: the deliberate, category-by-category adjustment of guardian intervention to the rate at which capability and business models are changing in that category. It extends Acemoglu and Robinson's corridor to the guardian-commercial boundary inside the state's purchasing function, with the contracting officer's warrant as the boundary; argues from the Red Queen dynamic that the object of management is cogrowth of guardian and commercial capacity at matched rates, not a balance of power; derives from Ashby's law of requisite variety and Holling's panarchy the principle that a slow guardian must supervise a fast commercial layer by outcome feedback rather than by procedure; states six institutional design principles, each with the wall it guards and an operational test; identifies four vectors of institutional contest, two of which do not yet exist; and introduces a vocabulary-governance profile, trim, adaptive governance-for operationalization. Corridor Management is proposed as the complement to Category Management: the latter scales what is common; the former adapts what is not.

detail.abstract: Brazil's anti-money laundering framework presents limitations in addressing corporate structures that are formally lawful but informationally opaque. This theoretical-conceptual essay examines the dissociation between effective economic control and formal legal responsibility as an autonomous source of institutional risk that is insufficiently captured by transaction-based models and declaratory beneficial ownership registers. Drawing on the economics of information, law and economics, risk-based regulation, and accounting research on information quality, the study develops the concept of structural risk of asset concealment. Through a comparative documentary analysis of the regulatory frameworks of the United Kingdom, the European Union, the United States, and Brazil, the study identifies limitations related to the fragmentation, updating, and verification of corporate information. As an institutional response, it proposes the National System for Structural Transparency and Prevention of Asset Concealment (SINTREP). The article contributes by treating corporate structure as an autonomous dimension of risk and by bringing together anti-money laundering, information governance, and the quality of economic and financial information.

detail.abstract: A ledger that lets a claim grow in real terms without limit and promises to redeem it in full within a bounded delay makes a promise that cannot be kept in a bounded world. We prove this without behavioural assumptions: for any such holder there is a finite date after which a permitted request cannot be met, and lossless storage of all output postpones that date only logarithmically. Paid-out interest and offsetting claims survive; what fails is the joint grant of accumulation and redemption; if the cost of carry rises fast enough with the shortfall, the ratio diverges at a finite date. Redemptions conserve the shortfall and worsen coverage for those who remain. Every restoration of feasibility must lower exercise, lower the unit delivered, cut the claims, enlarge the resource envelope, or extend time, and extending time fails when claims keep accruing. Under Bretton Woods, foreign official dollar claims relative to US gold rose log-linearly for twenty years (slope 0.120 per year, R²=0.983); pseudo-real-time forecasts using data through 1957–1963 placed the crossing in 1963–1965 (realized: 1964); by 1969 all foreign liquid claims exceeded the world's official gold. Under convertibility, narrow money stayed within 1.8–2.3 times monetary gold for six decades; once domestic redemption ended, it rose 6.2% a year. A pre-declared test shows that the ratio's level did not date suspensions. Over 1871–2020 real bill returns fell below growth in 15 of 16 economies, and large shortfalls came through inflation, not lower nominal yields.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the legal treatment of a person's photographic likeness under Nigerian law. It argues that Nigeria does not recognise a unified right of image or publicity, and that protection against the unauthorised use of a person's likeness is instead distributed across several distinct legal regimes: copyright, contract, the tort of passing off, constitutional privacy, and data protection. Drawing on four judicial decisions, Ubom v Globacom Nigeria Ltd, Banire v NTA-Star TV Network Ltd, Portland Paints & Products Nig. Ltd v Olaghare, and Nwabueze v Nigerian Breweries Plc, the paper demonstrates that each regime protects a different interest in the same photograph, and that the correct outcome of any dispute depends on identifying which interest is actually engaged. The paper closes by considering the doctrinal gap exposed by AI generated derivative images, an area in which no Nigerian court has yet ruled.

title: Predicting Order-processing Demand and Per-order AGV Delivery Time for Responsive Operations at Robotic Fulfillment Centers

detail.title: Predicting Order-processing Demand and Per-order AGV Delivery Time for Responsive Operations at Robotic Fulfillment Centers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China Grant (No.72261008), Hainan Provincial Natural Science Foundation of China (No.625MS048), and ‘Nanhai New Star' Philosophy and Social Science Talent Project of Hainan Province.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: E-commerce giants scale order-picking operations through robotic fulfillment centers (RFCs), where automated guided vehicles (AGVs) are dispatched according to real-time order-processing demand for transporting movable shelf racks to pickers' workstations. However, external factors (including weather conditions and promotional campaigns) may lead to sudden fluctuations in order inflows and RFC operational adjustments (including AGV system upgrades and changes in dispatching policies), which may induce complicated AGV scheduling and congestion and then significantly affect AGV performance of transporting orders. This interplay of dynamic, heterogeneous and multi-sourced impacts poses dual challenges: ensuring timely order fulfillment while maintaining high-throughput and low-latency AGV scheduling. Importantly, forecasting methods should adapt continuously under high-dimensional streaming data conditions to track structural changes in order-processing demand and AGV performance. Methodology/results: To address these challenges, we collaborate with a major e-commerce firm (JD.com) to propose a novel Incremental Sparse Forecasting method based on Informative Observations (ISF-IO) for predicting two critical real-time metrics in RFCs: order-processing demand and per-order AGV delivery time. This method first combines quadratic least square forecasting model with Lp-norm regularization for efficient nonlinear prediction by directly using a quadratic surface, to well handle high-dimensional and heterogeneous features in RFC data. The Lp-norm regularization is applied to intercept, single and quadratic features to reduce the impact of redundant features, leading to a sparse solution with automatically-selected features. We prove that the proposed model can be equivalently reformulated as a smaller-sized nonconvex problem, which is strongly NP-hard. For efficient implementation, we then develop a novel algorithm which converges to a sparse epsilon-KKT solution of this nonconvex model in tractable computational steps. Finally, we develop an adaptive pruning strategy to dynamically select the most informative observations under newly-inflowed data streams, supported by objective-sensitivity and forecast-stability analysis, for efficient incremental forecasting with theoretical analysis. Managerial implications: Our computational study, based on real data from a large RFC and additional public datasets, demonstrates that the ISF-IO method dominates state-of-the-art incremental forecasting methods in terms of forecasting accuracy and efficiency. By leveraging incremental learning and adaptive pruning, the proposed method dynamically updates predictive relationships under non-stationary streaming data, enabling robust and computationally efficient adaptation to evolving demand patterns and operational conditions. In summary, our study provides a critical foundation for generating real-time accurate forecasts and supporting responsive optimization-driven decision-making in large-scale RFCs, thereby enhancing AGV utilization rates, congestion management, workforce assignment, and overall intralogistics performance. Our method showcases a new perspective on addressing AI problems using operations research theory, enhancing the interpretability and practical acceptance of real-time predicted results for responsive RFC operations.

detail.abstract: Quantitative easing has become one of the defining monetary policy tools of the past decade. However, its role in shaping the structure of the financial system beyond its immediate impact on yields and asset prices remains unexplored, particularly as the ECB's Asset Purchase Programme is coming to an end. The PSPP portfolio is declining as securities mature and the ECB's policy framework after 2022 shifts towards more targeted instruments, such as the Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI). This paper examines the effect of the PSPP on financial development using the IMF's Composite Financial Development Indices, which capture depth, access and efficiency across financial institutions and markets, for a panel of 19 euro area countries from 2010 to 2021. Two original PSPP intensity indicators are constructed, relating cumulative purchases to public debt and to GDP. A System GMM model is then used to estimate the dynamic persistence of financial development, the potential endogeneity of asset purchases, and unobserved crosscountry heterogeneity. The results reveal a pronounced asymmetry: PSPP intensity is positively and significantly associated with financial market development, whereas its effect on financial institutions is negative and statistically insignificant. Disaggregating by sub-dimension shows that the market effect operates mainly through access and depth rather than efficiency. Extensive robustness checks confirm that, in the euro area, capital markets rather than financial institutions represent the dominant transmission channel of unconventional monetary policy to financial development.
