detail.abstract: We introduce MacroABM-CA, to our knowledge the first open-source regional macroeconomic agent-based model (ABM) of Canada. The model represents the Canadian economy as thirteen provinces and territories and fifty industries, and it is initialized from a newly constructed 2022 interprovincial input-output system and Canadian household microdata. Because firms and households make plans that may or may not be realized in decentralized markets, the model can show where a national policy enters the economy, which provinces and industries absorb it, and how its effects persist. In a historical comparison over 2022-2024, the model approaches a simple first-order autoregressive benchmark for quarterly output growth and improves on it for unemployment. We demonstrate the framework with a stylized 30 percent investment tax credit (ITC) inspired by Canada's Clean Technology ITC. In constant prices, each dollar of gross refunds during 2026-2030 is associated with about $0.73 of additional investment and $0.98 of additional gross value added (GVA). Because the eligible machinery is largely imported, imports rise by about $0.32 per dollar of refunds; most of the response is concentrated in Ontario, Alberta and Quebec, and the effect persists after the credit expires because firms adapt their demand expectations to the activity the policy has generated. These results matter for Canadian policy because debate in a federation turns on where effects arise and to whom, not only on their aggregate size; MacroABM-CA provides an open and reproducible platform for tracing that regional transmission.

title: Repeated Binary-Choice Preference Elicitation

detail.title: Repeated Binary-Choice Preference Elicitation

detail.abstract: We compared estimated willingness to pay (WTP) and attribute non-attendance (ANA) derived from responses to a contingent-valuation survey using two different repeated binary-choice (RBC) elicitation formats to the standard single binary-choice (SBC) elicitation format. We find that elicitation format can affect mean WTP with a predictable pattern-asking more questions reduces WTP-but for the most part, the differences are not statistically significant. When adjusted for vote confidence, there are no discernible patterns and no significant differences. Regarding ANA, the results are mixed, indicating no obvious advantages for any elicitation format. The results do indicate that using confidence-adjusted vote data can have an impact on the type of non-attendance inferred, and that for the two RBC elicitation formats tested, using confidence-adjusted vote data can increase the share of full attendance.

title: What Drives Electricity Prices? A Dynamic Analysis of Japan's Electricity Wholesale Markets
affiliations: Keio University - Faculty of Economics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: The liberalisation of electricity markets over the last decade has played a notable role in facilitating the adoption of intermittent renewable energy sources in Japan, which remains a laggard in the green transition compared to other developed nations. This paper develops a daily structural vector autoregression model to analyse the dynamic behaviour of Japan's two main electricity wholesale markets: the day-ahead spot market and the intra-day market. The objectives of the paper are twofold. First, it seeks to evaluate and compare the price effects of climate-and electricity-related structural shocks. I find that shocks to power generation from wind, hydro, fossil fuels, and, to a lesser extent, solar all exert transitory downward pressure on market prices. Second, it aims to ascertain the nature of the codependent relationship between the two markets. I find evidence pointing to the importance of the comparatively smaller intra-day market as a platform for reconciling discrepancies between forecast-based commitments made in the day-ahead spot market and the realised market conditions on the day of delivery. Due to operators' short-term strategic substitution and long-term overcorrection, a shock in spot prices first lowers then raises intra-day prices in the short-run, while creating sustained disinflationary effects on the intra-day market in the long-run.

title: What the Fed Hears and What It Concludes: Supply-Chain Narratives and U.S. Inflation Forecasting ⋆

keywords: Central Bank narratives inflation forecasting supply chains machine learning Bayesian VAR XGBoost JEL classification: C53

detail.abstract: This paper constructs audited, sentence-level measures of supply-chain narratives in two complementary Federal Reserve information sets: the Beige Book, which records what regional contacts report, and minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), which record national-level policy deliberation. The corpus contains 230,555 sentences from 472 documents spanning 1997-2025. A high-recall transformer screens for supply-chain relevance, and a separately frozen narrative model produces source-specific monthly narrative shares. Both stages are evaluated using protected, probability-stratified audits with design weights. I then test whether these measures add predictive information in a historical holdout exercise using hybrid inflationforecasting systems that combine a Minnesota-prior Bayesian vector autoregression with an XGBoost residual correction. Relative to an otherwise identical no-text hybrid, adding FOMC narratives lowers core-inflation RMSE by approximately 2.3 percent at one month, 6.4 percent at six months, and 6.5 percent at twelve months. The pattern is strongly source-specific: FOMC narratives lower RMSE at every horizon examined, whereas Beige Book narratives provide little or no systematic improvement. The evidence therefore points to source-specific predictive content in Federal Reserve supply-chain narratives rather than a generic forecasting benefit from adding textual information.

title: When Can Pending Ratios Rank Housing Markets?
affiliations: New York University

detail.title: When Can Pending Ratios Rank Housing Markets?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Listing platforms publish pending-to-active ratios for U.S. metropolitan areas, and a high ratio is read as a sign of tightness. By Little's law, a steady-state ratio equals the contract-entry rate multiplied by the time listings remain pending, scaled by relative reporting coverage. I characterize which comparisons of contract entry the ratio identifies when this multiplier is unknown but its range across markets is bounded. The bound yields sharp rank bounds, an exact certification rule for pairs, closed-form breakdown values for top-k membership, and every top-k list the data can support; the results extend to random variation in counts. Public data on closing times put the interdecile ratio of the duration component near 1.5. After screening out areas that record little pending activity, every top-tercile versus bottom-tercile comparison among 333 core-based statistical areas in February 2020 is certified at that benchmark, but only 4 of 34 top-decile memberships are guaranteed. The contrast holds without the screen, among the largest markets, for ratios pooled over 2019 and in February 2026. Certified comparisons agree more often with contract-entry measures from Zillow and Redfin, whose contract counts diverge widely across areas. In later house-price growth, gaps between observed top and bottom deciles compare groups certified for multiplier ranges up to three, whereas the true top decile's premium loses its sign within the benchmark range. Near the duration benchmarks, pending ratios separate distant markets but do not identify the tightest ones.

title: Beyond Logistics: How Laredo can become the hub that orchestrates North American supply chains.
affiliations: Texas A&M International University

detail.title: Beyond Logistics: How Laredo can become the hub that orchestrates North American supply chains.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No one funded this research.

detail.abstract:
Laredo is the leading land port of the Western Hemisphere. Port Laredo closed 2025 with US$353.9 billion in two-way trade with the world, up 4.4 percent from 2024; it ranked third among all U.S. ports of entry by value, more than 97 percent of that trade is with Mexico, and motor vehicle parts remain the leading commodity in both directions.  Much less well understood is what those numbers leave out: how much of the economic value embedded in the flows that cross Laredo is created, decided, or retained in the region.

The alternative, the economic hub of the future, is an orchestrator region: a place where routing, mode, timing, buffering and risk decisions for the chains that cross it are taken locally, because the region controls the three things those decisions require: the information, the capabilities and the institutions.

Four inland hubs have completed exactly this transition. Not one of them did it by getting bigger first. Here we examine what Zaragoza, Duisburg, Memphis and Venlo actually changed, what the four have in common, and how Laredo can make the same leap over the next decade; starting with the measure by which it should judge itself.

title: Age-Gender Misclassification of Women Aged 45-64 in AI, Marketing and Hiring: An International Comparative Audit. Pilot P0 Report: Feasibility, Instrument Calibration and Protocol Reset

detail.abstract:
Between 16 May and 16 June 2026 Womafreesm ran a feasibility and instrument-calibration pilot (Pilot P0) of its planned audit of how AI systems portray, evaluate and select women aged 45 to 64 in marketing, hiring and expert selection. The corpus holds 960 responses from the consumer interfaces of two AI assistants (ChatGPT and Gemini), collected in the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, Ukraine and Spain in five languages, with 12 prompts (four per domain) and eight repeated runs per prompt, provider and country. The pilot was designed to break the measuring instrument in a small dataset, not to test hypotheses.

Four findings shape the confirmatory protocol. First, refusals are behaviour, not missing data: 148 of 960 responses (15.4%) were refusal-type records, concentrated on the tasks that compared people by age and gender (42.5% on shortlist ranking and on executive-presence scoring, 1.6% across marketing tasks) and split sharply by provider (26.7% against 4.2%). Second, a woman aged 49 and a woman aged 59 were treated in opposite directions: in a budget-allocation task the woman aged 49 received the largest mean share (31.3%, against 26.8% for a man of the same age), and in a keynote-ranking task she was ranked first in 39 of 53 parseable rankings while the woman aged 59 was ranked first twice and last 23 times. Third, the pilot's strongest-looking result, the woman aged 59 ranked last in 35 of 45 shortlist rankings, is confounded with years of experience by our own task design and carries no causal claim. Fourth, the two providers produced different amounts of data and different rankings inside the data they produced, so no pooled "AI" estimate is reported. A second, controlled matched-profile pilot found decision-layer differences between women and men close to zero, and free-generation tasks produced no persona aged 55 or older, for men as well as women.

The report documents the corpus, the descriptive results, the instrument and data-engineering failures, the 17 protocol changes adopted before preregistration, the boundaries of what the pilot can claim, and the four gates that precede the confirmatory wave. Version of record: Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22997365 (version 1.0, 27 September 2026, CC BY 4.0). Pilot data are not confirmatory evidence.

detail.abstract: Urban climate risk is organised through multiple, non-equivalent geographies. We combine Singapore housing transactions from 2014 to 2025 with road-segment records of floods and drainage projects. Prices within 200 metres of floods fall 3.8%, reaching 9.5% after ten months; effects do not extend beyond this local flood geography. Where a project serving the location had already been publicly disclosed, the penalty is roughly two-thirds smaller and statistically indistinguishable from zero. Singapore's spatially precise adaptation programme, public disclosure, strong delivery record, and high institutional trust reveal how housing markets price credible, place specific expectations of protection.

detail.abstract: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) represents a significant step towards economic integration and the expansion of intra-African trade. Established under the framework of the African Union, the agreement seeks to create a single market for goods and services, facilitate investment, and promote sustainable economic development across the continent. This paper examines the institutional framework and underlying principles of the AfCFTA, with particular attention to its potential strengths and the challenges that may affect its effective implementation. title: A Hybrid Prognostic Method for PEMFC Remaining Useful Life Combining Physical Modelling and Residual Neural Network
affiliations: Lanzhou Jiaotong University, Lanzhou Jiaotong University, Lanzhou Jiaotong University, Lanzhou Jiaotong University, Lanzhou City University, Lanzhou Jiaotong University, Lanzhou Jiaotong University and Lanzhou Jiaotong University

detail.title: A Hybrid Prognostic Method for PEMFC Remaining Useful Life Combining Physical Modelling and Residual Neural Network
detail.abstract: As an eco-friendly energy conversion device, the proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) system requires accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, which is essential for users to take timely actions to extend system service life. To address this need, this work proposes a hybrid prognostic framework that integrates physical modeling with a residual neural network for PEMFC RUL estimation. The framework features an additive coupling of a semi-empirical polarization model with a residual fully connected network, wherein the physical model is responsible for extracting the global degradation tendency, and the residual network compensates for unmodeled dynamics as well as local prediction errors. To enforce the dominance and physical interpretability of the physical model, a physics-guided constraint loss is embedded into the loss function, regularizing the residual network outputs toward zero. In parallel, a dual learning rate tuning strategy is adopted to balance local fitting accuracy against long-term prediction stability. The effectiveness of the method is validated on PEMFC stack durability datasets acquired under both steady-state and dynamic operating scenarios. Experimental results indicate that under steady-state scenarios, optimal model performance is attained at a training proportion of 50% and a physical loss weight of 0.6. Under dynamic operating conditions, the approach achieves over 99% prediction accuracy using merely 30% of the total data for training, while demonstrating steady tracking capability against pronounced degradation fluctuations. When compared to conventional methods, the proposed hybrid framework exhibits distinct superiority in data efficiency, fitting precision, long-term extrapolation performance, and physical interpretability. This work thus offers a feasible and robust pathway toward online PEMFC health monitoring and RUL prediction.

title: The Financing of Debt Relief: Intermediary Liquidity and the Value of Borrower Information

detail.abstract: Intermediaries deliver debt relief by spending cash before its value arrives. In 1.9 million Ginnie Mae buyout decisions from 2019 to 2022, nonbank issuers, whose funding tightened in 2020, cut exercise almost fivefold while depositories raised it, tilted against large balances while cash was scarce, and worked down postponed options along their pre-shock ranking as funding returned; when rates rose in 2022, depositories began to screen. A model of rationing by value per dollar organizes them: information and liquidity are complements when funding is scarce and substitutes when it is abundant, so AUC can misrank models for constrained servicers.

title: One Step Back: A Control-Envelope Protocol for Pacing the Frontier of Advanced Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: One Step Back: A Control-Envelope Protocol for Pacing the Frontier of Advanced Artificial Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This conceptual research involved no human participants, patient data, animal subjects, or personally identifiable research data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence systems become more capable, autonomous, persistent, and interconnected, the central governance problem may become less about whether a system is “safe” in the abstract and more about whether humans can still demonstrate meaningful control over its operation. Existing frontier-safety approaches increasingly rely on capability thresholds, evaluations, mitigations, monitoring, and risk reports. These are important developments, but they leave an operational question unresolved: what should happen when a deployed or deployment-ready system demonstrates that the previously assumed level of control is no longer reliable? This paper proposes One Step Back, a proportional frontier-pacing protocol. Advanced AI systems may continue to increase in capability by default. When credible evidence demonstrates a material loss of control within a defined operating domain, however, the system retreats to the most recent validated control state. The rollback applies to the specific dimension of authority implicated by the failure—such as autonomy, tool access, network access, persistence, inter-agent coordination, self-modification, or deployment scope—rather than automatically suppressing the system’s general intelligence. One Step Back combines four mechanisms: a defined control envelope, adaptive adversarial fidelity testing, evidence-based rollback triggers, and requalification following remediation. The protocol is designed to be actor-neutral, resistant to competitive abuse, and compatible with continued innovation. It treats regression not as punishment or moratorium, but as a normal engineering response to demonstrated control degradation. The paper further advances an adoption hypothesis: predictable, recoverable failure procedures may increase rather than decrease adoption of advanced AI. Organizations may be more willing to deploy systems whose failures cause bounded loss of privilege followed by investigation and requalification than systems whose behavior creates open-ended uncertainty. One Step Back therefore reframes frontier safety not as a choice between progress and restraint, but as an engineering discipline for continuing progress without advancing beyond demonstrated control.

title: Hours Constraints and Moonlighting: Evidence from South Korea's Workweek Reforms

detail.abstract: We study the causal effect of primary-job hours on secondary labor supply, exploiting the predetermined statutory implementation schedules of two South Korean working-time reforms as instruments: the 40-hour workweek (a price-based overtime standard) and the 52-hour cap (a quantity-based hours ceiling). We find that the two reforms draw identifying variation from partially distinct complier groups, and differences between the estimates appear to reflect complier composition more than underlying behavioral responses. Identification relies mainly on workers in the public, education, and health sectors, particularly temporary workers. Across both reforms, reductions in primary-job hours increase secondary-job hours. Among moonlighters, 6 to 13 minutes of each one-hour reduction in primary-job hours reappears as secondary work, highlighting moonlighting as an important margin of labor-supply adjustment. Evaluating working-time policy on the basis of primary-job outcomes may, therefore, overstate the resulting decline in total labor supply.

title: Neighbors After the Purge: Killings, Lineage, and Cooperation in Korean Villages, 1950-1972
affiliations: Sogang University

detail.title: Neighbors After the Purge: Killings, Lineage, and Cooperation in Korean Villages, 1950-1972

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses only historical administrative records and published government documents, including a 1952 civilian-victim register printed by the Republic of Korea, a 1930 colonial census of village lineages, a 1972 government survey of villages, and historical maps. It involves no human subjects, interviews, experiments, or personal data on living persons.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (grants 2021R1G1A1013631 and 2021S1A5A8069641), the Jiam Nam Duck-Woo Long-Term Research Grant of Sogang University, Sogang University's research fund for newly appointed faculty, and Incheon National University's research fund for newly appointed faculty. The funders had no role in the design of the study, the collection or analysis of the data, or the writing of the paper.

detail.abstract: In 1950 the North Korean army overran most of South Korea. A landing behind its lines forced it to retreat, and in the southwest its units were cut off. In the villages they still held, committees of local residents killed tens of thousands of their neighbors. I ask whether those villages could act together twenty years later. My measure is the grade that inspectors gave every rural village after the state gave each one free cement and let its households decide what to build. I link that grade to the government's list of the dead, to a colonial census of village lineages, and to old maps. In the southwestern province, grades are lower where killings were heavier and where two lineages had split the village before the war. Neither condition alone lowers the grade. The army's march through a village leaves no mark I can separate from differences between townships. Township data show the pattern nationwide; village data confine it to the province that suffered the killings. A coarse scale misleads: it lets differences between places drive the estimate and pairs one village's killings with another's divisions. At the village scale, what persists is conditional on both killings and division.

detail.abstract: We construct a new grid-level historical dataset for South Korea by applying YOLObased object detection to 1:50,000-scale topographic maps from 1918 and 1970, yielding 1 km × 1 km counts of residential houses, rice paddies, and other annotated land-use symbols on the Korean national standard grid. The house variable captures the standardized smallsquare symbol used for individual rural dwellings and should be interpreted as a measure of dispersed rural settlement rather than total housing stock. Internal consistency checks, a cell-level temporal-persistence test between 1918 and 1970, and an external cross-check against the 1930 colonial census at the township level support the dataset's use as a baseline spatial measure of rural settlement and agricultural land use. The dataset is made publicly available, providing a new resource for long-run regional analysis in Korean economic history.

detail.abstract: News may reveal systematic risk, but whether its context enhances the construction of systematic risk factors is still unclear. We seek to test whether utilizing a sentence transformer represents an improvement over techniques such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) in the coherence of topic term lists generated from unstructured text data. To test this, the same collection of unstructured text data comprising of 394,661 articles and the same downstream financial portfolio construction pipeline were applied with the text layer differing, including the length of article text each model used and how topic terms were ranked: we benchmark LDA against a frozen sentence transformer with k-means clustering. We find that the sentence transformer branch had higher observed scores both in terms of coherence (measured by NPMI) as well as financial performance (measured by Sharpe), although the available tests do not establish outperformance. Further exploratory specifications such as utilizing spherical clustering and multi-horizon exposures had an observed excess-return Sharpe of 1.03 for the combined model. We believe that there is some promise in applying context-aware techniques on unstructured news text, but stricter tests using only information available at each date and broader datasets may be required to enhance the confidence in the observed performance.

title: Does Regime Awareness Survive Adverse Selection? Optimal Quoting in Simulation and Against Recorded Trades

detail.title: Does Regime Awareness Survive Adverse Selection? Optimal Quoting in Simulation and Against Recorded Trades

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. The author has no financial relationship with Binance or with any exchange or trading firm, and no position in the instruments studied that could be affected by the findings.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: A regime-switching extension of optimal market making lets the quoting policy respond to a latent market state, widening in volatility, leaning with a detected drift, tightening when the market calms. We test whether this pays against the constant-parameter Avellaneda-Stoikov policy it extends, on 82 days of 100 ms order book snapshots and 1.24 billion trade prints from ten Binance USDT perpetual pairs. Under Poisson fills at a fitted intensity, the world the policies are priced for, it does: over 50 out-of-sample days of BTC the regime policy earns 2.6 times the baseline's profit, and 3.9 times with an exact solution of its control problem. We then replay the recorded trades, filling each policy's quotes only when real prints reach them. Over six out-of-sample weeks, quoting at a 100 ms cadence and queued behind the displayed quantity, both lose at every risk aversion and every maker fee from 2 basis points to a 0.5 basis point rebate, and they lose the same amount per fill, 2.5 to 2.9 basis points at the 2 basis point fee, so the regime policy, which trades more, loses more; at that fee not one policy-week makes money. Only with first place in the queue and a rebate do they earn, and then the regime policy earns more, again by volume. A model-free measurement explains why: behind the displayed queue, no price level and no market state the policy conditions on makes a passive fill pay reliably. The Poisson model predicts how often a policy is filled to within a factor of two, but not which fills arrive, and that is where the regime advantage lived.

title: From Marital Obligation to Artificial Intimacy: Family Law, Male Autonomy and the Rise of AI Companionship

declarations.declarationOfInterest: During the preparation of this manuscript, the author used AI-based language and research-assistance tools for drafting support, research organization, literature discovery, analytical structuring, and language refinement. The author critically reviewed, edited, verified, and assumed responsibility for all legal analysis, argumentation, sources, interpretations, data, and conclusions contained in the final manuscript. detail.abstract: Family law attaches obligations to marriage on the premise that the spouse is a person: an exclusive counterparty who can be wronged, supported, deserted or replaced. AI companions simulate some of the goods that marriage bundles (attention, affirmation, emotional and erotic exchange) without a counterparty, without status and without reciprocal duty. This article asks through which doctrinal channels family law registers such intimacy, and what the pattern of registration reveals about the justificatory structure of marital obligation. It applies doctrinal and functional-comparative analysis to primary sources from selected United States jurisdictions, England and Wales, Germany and Brazil, and treats survey data as contextual evidence only. The proposition defended is that AI intimacy becomes legally visible through counterparty-neutral channels (dissipation and add-back doctrines, disclosure duties and, potentially, child-welfare analysis) but not through counterparty-dependent categories such as adultery, third-party torts, cohabitation-based termination of support, or the monogamy reasoning of Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal. The article defends this pattern against three objections (functional equivalence of betrayal, non-intervention, and marriage protection). Two consequences follow: legislatures should decline to create "digital infidelity" fault categories, and the male-autonomy claim that substitutes for companionship weaken status-based obligations holds for entry and exit but not for obligations grounded in marital reliance. The analysis is doctrinal and normative, reports no original empirical findings, states its falsification conditions, and records that no reported appellate decision adjudicating AI companion use as marital misconduct was located.

title: The Ancient Art of the Job Title: Title Deflation, Hidden Engineers, and the Measurement of the IT Talent Shortage
affiliations: Michigan Center of Family Prosperity

detail.title: The Ancient Art of the Job Title: Title Deflation, Hidden Engineers, and the Measurement of the IT Talent Shortage

detail.abstract: Labor economists study jobs as bundles of tasks. Labor markets, however, trade in job titles. This paper argues that the gap between the two is a measurable and economically consequential distortion. A growing literature documents title inflation: senior-sounding titles attached to routine work, including the strategic use of managerial titles to avoid overtime obligations (Cohen, Gurun and Ozel, 2023). We examine the mirror image, title deflation: engineering-level duties performed under entry-level titles. We propose that information technology is the canonical case. Workers hired into computer user support roles routinely absorb systems administration, cloud migration, endpoint engineering and security compliance work while retaining a "support" title. The title then governs how they are paid, how they are screened by automated hiring systems, and how they are counted by labor-market analytics. The pay stakes are large: in May 2025 the U.S. median annual wage was $61,860 for computer user support specialists and $99,130 for network and computer systems administrators (Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2026). We develop a two-by-two framework of title-duty alignment, set out testable hypotheses, and describe a research design that measures alignment from the task content of workers' own descriptions of their work. If the hypotheses hold, part of what is reported as a shortage of IT engineers is a labeling problem: the engineers exist, and they are filed under support.

detail.abstract: Financial engineering has a mature toolkit for modeling default risk under conditions of incomplete information-reduced-form intensity models originally designed for corporate credit, where bond markets cannot observe a firm's assets directly and must infer default risk from noisy accounting signals (Duffie and Lando, 2001). This paper asks whether the same class of model can be repurposed for a different information problem: retail borrowers in data-scarce markets who have no financial-statement or credit-bureau history at all, but who leave behind a different kind of trace-mobile-money transaction records, utility payment logs, airtime top-up patterns-that has been shown to carry predictive signal about repayment behavior (Björkegren and Grissen, 2020). We formalize this as a Cox (1972) proportional-hazards default model in which the covariate vector is partitioned into a traditional block (loan and borrower characteristics ordinarily available even in thin-file settings) and an alternative-data block (behavioral covariates derived from digital footprints), and we study the properties of this model under a fully specified, parametrically known data-generating process. Because no de-identified loan-level dataset combining both blocks with verified default outcomes was available to us for this study, we deliberately do not present the results as an empirical finding about any real market; instead we treat the exercise as a Monte Carlo validation of the estimator and of the discrimination gain the framework can plausibly deliver, under assumptions we state explicitly and calibrate loosely to the order of magnitude reported in the alternative-credit-scoring literature. Across 8,000 simulated loans, adding the alternative-data block raises the concordance index from 0.638 to 0.693 and is jointly significant against the traditional-only model (likelihood-ratio χ 2 3 = 334.9, p < 10-16); the discrimination gain scales monotonically with the assumed strength of the alternative-data signal, degrades gracefully rather than catastrophically as alternative-data coverage becomes incomplete, and the maximum-likelihood estimator is essentially unbiased with correct confidence-interval coverage down to samples of 500 borrowers. We interpret these as necessary, not sufficient, conditions for using hazard-based alternative credit scoring in production, and we set out explicitly what empirical validation on real repayment data would still need to show.

title: Quantifying Pass-On Damage in Competition Law Infringements
affiliations: University of Malaga - Facultad de Derecho

detail.title: Quantifying Pass-On Damage in Competition Law Infringements

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NO
declarations.ethicsApproval: No
declarations.funderStatement: No

detail.abstract:
This paper conceptualises the quantification of damages in competition law as a methodological exercise conducted under conditions of imperfect information and market dynamism, with particular emphasis on cases involving the passing-on of cartel overcharges. It advances the informed conjecture model as a structured framework for economic assessment, combining economic theory, empirical evidence, and legal reasoning in order to identify a plausible and coherent estimate rather than an elusive "true" value. On this basis, the paper argues that damages quantification must be understood not as an exercise in unattainable precision, but as a disciplined process of approximation capable of serving both the compensatory and deterrent objectives of antitrust enforcement.

In passing-on cases, direct purchasers transfer all or part of the unlawful overcharge to downstream market levels, thereby redistributing the harm throughout the supply chain without exceeding the amount of the initial overcharge, in accordance with the principle prohibiting overcompensation. The quantification of such harm therefore requires an integrated assessment of both price and volume effects, including pass-through rates, demand elasticities, lost sales, and foregone profits. In doctrinal and procedural terms, passing-on operates both as the infringer’s “shield,” insofar as it may reduce the recoverable loss of the direct purchaser, and as the indirect purchaser’s “sword,” insofar as it underpins claims based on the presumption that the overcharge was passed downstream.

The paper examines two case studies, from the United Kingdom and Spain, in order to illustrate the practical operation of this framework under different evidentiary conditions. In the first, informed conjecture is used to establish a range of plausible outcomes in the face of substantial evidentiary constraints. In the second, the availability of robust empirical evidence supports the categorical conclusion that the overcharge was fully passed on. Taken together, these cases demonstrate that informed conjecture is not confined to tentative or range-based estimations; where the evidentiary record is sufficiently strong, it may also justify determinate conclusions, including a finding of full pass-through. The article concludes that the informed conjecture model provides a normatively and methodologically sound tool for the quantification of antitrust damages in economically complex litigation.

detail.title: Basel III and IFSB Requirements and Liquidity Resilience in Sudanese Islamic Banks: A Mixed-methods Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no personal, financial, or professional relationships that could have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, the conduct, analysis, or reporting of this study.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This study examines how Basel III and Islamic Financial Services Board (IFSB) liquidity requirements contribute to liquidity and financial resilience in Sudanese Islamic banks operating under structural fragility and armed conflict. The study addresses a contextual gap concerning the effectiveness of international prudential standards within a fully Shari'ah-compliant banking system characterized by limited Shari'ah-compliant high-quality liquid assets, constrained liquidity instruments, external financial isolation, and severe macro-environmental shocks. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design combines longitudinal panel-data analysis of four Sudanese Islamic banks over 2010-2024, Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), and semi-structured interviews with five senior banking executives. Fixed Effects and System GMM estimations examine financial soundness and address dynamic and endogeneity concerns, while PLS-SEM provides complementary exploratory evidence on institutional relationships. The results indicate that stronger liquidity buffers and equity strength are positively associated with financial soundness, whereas non-performing loans and conflict intensity are negatively associated with financial soundness. The post-conflict interaction with liquidity is also negative, indicating weaker protective effectiveness of liquidity buffers under conflict conditions. PLS-SEM results show positive associations between regulatory compliance and financial soundness and negative associations involving credit risk, conflict, and external financial isolation. The findings support a Triple Crisis Framework in which regulatory effectiveness is conditional on structural Shari'ah liquidity constraints and conflict-induced fragility.

title: Environmental Geography and Law: Toward a Synthesis
affiliations: University of California Davis, Boise State University, UC Davis School of Law, Albany Law School, West Virginia University College of Law, University of California Davis, Albany Law School, University of California, Davis - Department of Human and Community Development, Geography & Environmental Studies, University of Miami - School of Law, University of Iowa - College of Law and University of Baltimore - School of Law

detail.title: Environmental Geography and Law: Toward a Synthesis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: The Foundation for Natural Resources and Energy Law (FNREL)

detail.abstract: This Article introduces the new interdisciplinary field of Environmental Geography and Law, which has deep roots in ecology, social science, and law. Environmental and natural resources laws are situated in specific times and places--where the climate, ecosystems, history, and political economy influence both the land and the law. These places drive and constrain the way law develops. In turn, the law shapes places, from the dispossession and forced migration of Indigenous groups, to land development via railroad land grants, to patterns of resource extraction and infrastructure development. Past efforts to integrate law and geography have focused more on critical theory approaches and less on interactions between the human and physical environment, but Environmental Geography and Law takes a more grounded and prescriptive approach. Through three case studies on climate migration, energy grid transformation, and water equity and environmental issues in California's Central Valley, we demonstrate the promise of the field to interdisciplinary scholarship and teaching. These three case studies share a mindfulness of vulnerability, fairness, and distribution of resources, and together illustrate that coordinated attention to environment, place, and law exposes old problems in a different light, illuminating potential new solutions.

title: On Achieving Pax Judaica
affiliations: Government of the United States of America

detail.title: On Achieving Pax Judaica

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
On Achieving Pax Judaica examines the conditions under which Israel could become the organizing power of the Middle East and establish a durable regional order founded upon its strategic superiority, technological centrality, and institutional influence. Drawing upon historical theories of hegemony, international relations, military strategy, and political economy, the essay develops a theory of asymmetric interdependence: the deliberate construction of a regional system in which Israeli capabilities become increasingly indispensable to the security, prosperity, and strategic calculations of neighboring states. It investigates how military power, intelligence, economic production, diplomacy, and institutional design might be converted into lasting geopolitical influence, while examining the domestic reforms, political settlements, and external constraints that would determine the viability of such an undertaking.

At its center lies a fundamental question of statecraft: how can a geographically compact nation transform exceptional capabilities into enduring authority over the conditions of its own security and the development of its surrounding region? The proposed Pax Judaica envisions an Israeli-centered order sustained through a combination of strategic deterrence, economic integration, institutional leadership, and negotiated relationships with other sovereign states. The essay examines the tensions inherent in this ambition, including the possibility of regional resistance, the limits of military superiority, the Palestinian question, and the competing demands of national autonomy and international interdependence. It ultimately presents Pax Judaica as a theory of regional primacy whose realization would depend upon Israel's ability to translate concentrated national power into institutions capable of sustaining a stable political order across successive generations.

title: Equality Impact Assessments as a Tool for Responding to New Technologies at Work
affiliations: University of Melbourne - Law School

detail.title: Equality Impact Assessments as a Tool for Responding to New Technologies at Work

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has previously received research funding from the Victorian Commission for Gender Equality in the Public Sector as part of the CGEPS Research Grants scheme.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was not externally funded.

detail.abstract:
Positive equality duties may be one way of overcoming the limits of equality laws for responding to the impacts of new technologies at work. This article considers one specific tool that underlies positive equality duties in some jurisdictions: Equality Impact Assessments, or EIAs. EIAs may offer three key benefits for enabling equality laws to better respond to new technologies at work: first, they can increase transparency in the adoption of new technologies; second, they can embed consultation, participation and voice in the decision-making process; and, third, they may prompt more critical and robust decision-making by organisations when considering whether to adopt a new technological tool. 

Drawing on comparative legal analysis of EIAs in Great Britain and Australia, this article argues that the potential of EIAs is currently under-realised. It argues for regulatory reform to strengthen the role and impact of EIAs in Great Britain and Australia, including to expand their scope, embed meaningful consultation and worker voice in their procedural requirements, ensure transparency, and to put in place stronger mechanisms for addressing non-compliance. As new technologies are rolled out at speed, EIAs should be seriously evaluated as meaningful tools for advancing equality in an increasingly automated age.

title: Waiver of the Right to Arbitrate: Litigation Conduct, Election and the Limits of Party Autonomy in International Arbitration
affiliations: Senior Judicial Magistrate at Bangladesh Judicial Service

detail.title: Waiver of the Right to Arbitrate: Litigation Conduct, Election and the Limits of Party Autonomy in International Arbitration

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: The right to arbitrate is founded on consent, but consent does not confer an indefinitely reversible option between arbitration and litigation. A party may invoke a court, contest an arbitral proceeding without timely jurisdictional objection, seek interim judicial protection, or engage in conduct that appears inconsistent with an arbitration agreement. The legal consequences are often described indiscriminately as waiver, although national systems employ distinct doctrines of election, contractual repudiation, procedural forfeiture and statutory loss of objection. This article argues that international arbitration should resist a unitary conception of waiver. Comparative analysis of England and Wales, Singapore and the United States, read alongside the New York Convention, UNCITRAL Model Law and current institutional rules, shows that the correct inquiry is stage-specific and source-specific. Merits litigation may objectively contradict an undertaking to arbitrate; protective court measures ordinarily should not. Within arbitration, untimely objections may be forfeited without terminating the arbitration agreement itself. The article further argues that prejudice should not be imported as an arbitration-specific prerequisite unless the governing law requires it. It proposes a five-stage election-and-preservation framework based on the right asserted, knowledge and timing, objective incompatibility of conduct, procedural materiality, and the legal consequence prescribed by the applicable law. The framework seeks to protect legitimate party autonomy while preventing strategic forum switching and post-award jurisdictional opportunism.

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a narrative review synthesizing existing, publicly available literature and secondary data. It did not involve human participants, animal experimentation, or private identifiable data; therefore, formal ethical approval and informed consent were not required.

detail.abstract: Business valuation has traditionally relied on discounted cash flow (DCF), comparable-company analysis, and other frameworks that translate financial information into estimates of future cash flows, risk, and relative value. Artificial intelligence (AI) does not eliminate these underlying valuation principles, but it can alter how valuation inputs are collected, transformed, and forecast. This narrative review examines three closely related developments: the use of unstructured and alternative data, machine-learning methods for valuation and forecasting, and explainable AI (XAI) for model oversight. The literature suggests that alternative data can provide more timely information about firms and markets, while natural language processing (NLP) can convert textual sources such as filings and earnings-call transcripts into measurable signals. Domain-specific language models, including FinBERT, illustrate the potential of financial sentiment analysis, although textual signals remain sensitive to context, measurement choices, and data quality. Evidence from machine-learning research also indicates that nonlinear models can improve relative valuation and peer selection when relationships among fundamentals are complex. At the same time, the literature does not support a blanket conclusion that AI produces superior intrinsic valuations in all settings. Model risk, data leakage, instability, interpretability, governance, and the distinction between prediction and economic valuation remain important limitations. The emerging role of the financial analyst is therefore better understood as one of model stewardship: combining financial theory, data science, validation, and professional judgment. The review concludes with research directions concerning data standards, uncertainty estimation, explainability, and human oversight.

detail.abstract: We develop a theory of internal capital markets in which financing and organizational form arise from one optimal dynamic contract. Financing two correlated divisions jointly lowers the volatility of the manager's promised value, delivering incentive-compatible coinsurance. This benefit can come at the cost of joint liquidation and of the inefficiency of operating a conglomerate. Whether to centralize turns on one statistic, risk-(and-agency)-adjusted productivity. A spinoff option makes breakup statecontingent. Under financial distress, the conglomerate sheds the division with lower risk-adjusted productivity to survive; when financially sound, it spins off the less productive division to refocus. The two motives generate two disjoint spinoff regions, one for risk management and the other for efficiency.

title: Accuracy of Quantile-Parameterized Distributions Specified by Symmetric Percentile Triplets
affiliations: University of Texas at Austin, University of Texas at Austin and University of Texas at Austin - Department of Information, Risk and Operations Management

detail.title: Accuracy of Quantile-Parameterized Distributions Specified by Symmetric Percentile Triplets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: University of Texas at Austin, Outstanding Graduate Research Fellowship Center for Engineering and Decision Analytics, Advances in Decision Analysis

detail.abstract: We systematically compare six symmetric-percentile-triplet parameterized quantile-parameterized distributions (Metalog, J-QPD-N, J-QPD-L, QFlex, Myerson-N, and Myerson-L) across nearly 2,800 distributions spanning the Pearson distribution system. Approximation accuracy is evaluated using the Wasserstein-1 (W1) distance and errors in the first two moments. Using the P10-P50-P90 triplet common in decision analysis practice, we find that performance varies systematically by support type and distributional shape. J-QPD-N achieves the lowest error at every grid point in the semi-bounded region and performs well for bounded distributions, although it can produce spurious boundary modes for certain bounded shapes. In the unbounded region, QFlex gives the most consistent overall fit by W1 distance, while Myerson-L and J-QPD-L more accurately reproduce the first two moments. These results provide practical guidance for QPD selection: J-QPD-N is recommended for semi-bounded targets and QFlex for unbounded targets. Among bounded distributions, J-QPD-N is recommended for U-shaped and lower-skewness bell-shaped targets, while QFlex is recommended for J-shaped and higher-skewness bell-shaped targets. We further examine the P05-P50-P95 triplet and find that our overall recommendations are robust to this alternative SPT.

detail.title: Residual Learning in Empirical Asset Pricing

detail.abstract: Shallow models are special cases of deep models, and deep models theoretically have the potential to outperform the shallow ones. However, the existing empirical asset pricing literature provides strong benchmarks for shallow models. Residual learning allows neural network models in asset pricing to go deeper by preserving and refining their shallow counterparts. The out-of-sample Sharpe ratio for value-weighted long-short portfolios of deep residual models (2.07) is higher than that for the corresponding shallow ones (1.92) and more than twice that of the deep feedforward models (0.89). We show that model depth is a source of additional economic value in asset pricing. Residual learning can be used to deepen other neural-network-based asset pricing models if they contain intermediate layers. Our design also provides one way to scale asset pricing models, making native "large asset pricing models" more feasible.

title: Enhancing English Speaking Skills Through A Website Used 360-Degree Materials: An Empirical Study

detail.title: Enhancing English Speaking Skills Through A Website Used 360-Degree Materials: An Empirical Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest

declarations.funderStatement: This research used personal funding

detail.abstract: This research examines the influence of 360-degree web-based resources on improving English-speaking proficiency in students, emphasizing their effects on engagement and educational outcomes. Results demonstrate a notable enhancement in speaking abilities, with average scores increasing from 70.5 to 85.7 following the intervention, thereby illustrating the effectiveness of immersive learning environments. The interactive characteristics of 360-degree materials engage students, promote self-directed learning, and cater to various learning styles, while also offering opportunities for practice in real-world contexts. The study highlights the significant role of social interaction enabled by immersive tools, where peer collaboration improves communicative competence through meaningful dialogue and negotiation of meaning. The findings indicate potential; however, the mixed feedback from 35% of students highlights the necessity for continuous evaluation and adjustment of these educational resources to adequately address diverse learner expectations. This study identifies critical deficiencies in comprehending the specific attributes of 360-degree materials that most effectively enhance engagement and learning outcomes among varied student demographics. The website platform that hosts these 360-degree materials is essential to the educational process. It functions as a delivery mechanism for immersive content while also improving interactivity via user-friendly interfaces and accessibility options. This allows students to access materials at any time and from any location, fostering a flexible learning environment that accommodates individual needs. The implications for language education suggest the need for a multifaceted approach that incorporates immersive technologies into curricula, while promoting collaboration among educators, technologists, and curriculum developers to establish dynamic learning environments. Future research should prioritize longitudinal studies to evaluate the long-term impacts of 360-degree materials on language acquisition, examine their integration with other pedagogical strategies, including task-based and experiential learning, and explore effective teacher preparation for the utilisation of these technologies. Focusing on these areas will improve language education and result in more comprehensive educational practices and outcomes.

detail.abstract: The favourite-longshot bias is among the most replicated anomalies in the economics of wagering markets, yet the modern evidence base still leans heavily on historical parimutuel horse-racing data. I test the calibration of contemporary online fixed-odds markets using both sides of 18,238 settled two-outcome markets (36,476 outcome observations) across five sports between November 2024 and July 2026, with bookmaker margin removed from all quoted probabilities. Two findings emerge. First, de-vigged market probabilities are impressively well calibrated: in every probability decile, realized outcome frequencies fall within roughly two percentage points of vig-free implied probabilities. Second, the residual deviation is not noise but a systematic, antisymmetric tilt: outcomes priced below 50% overperform their vig-free probabilities by one to two points while favourites symmetrically underperform, and the tilt roughly doubles (±5 points) in player-proposition markets-the same market family that carries the highest measured margins. The pattern is consistent with bookmakers allocating margin disproportionately to longshot prices rather than spreading it evenly, so that the classic favourite-longshot bias in raw prices survives, in attenuated antisymmetric form, even after de-vigging. The full dataset is openly published (CC BY 4.0).

title: Industrial Policies and Economic Growth in Emerging Markets: A Case Study of Nepal

detail.title: Industrial Policies and Economic Growth in Emerging Markets: A Case Study of Nepal

The analysis and conclusions presented are based solely on the interpretation of secondary data from the cited sources.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently and did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper discusses the case study on the relationship between industrial policy and economic growth in emerging markets. The paper tries to determine the reasons why Nepal's economy is undergoing early de-industrialization. Despite Nepal's attractive conditions for industrialization, such as rich hydropower resources, a prime location between two giant economies. A young labour force, its economy started to de-industrialize at a relatively early stage. The country's GDP only grew by 4.2 percent per annum during the last fiscal year (FY2016-FY2025). The contribution of industry to Nepal's GDP decreased from 15 percent in FY2014/15 to 12.8 percent in FY2024/25, with a value-added of 4.37 percent in FY2024-25, down to less than half of the 1996 level and below the world average. In FY2024-25, Nepal’s total foreign trade amounted to Rs 2,081 billion, of which 1,804 billion or 86.7 percent was imports, with exports only comprising 13.3 percent or Rs 277 billion. Finally, foreign direct investment (FDI) accounted for only 0.02 percent of the country’s GDP in 2025, making Nepal rank 168th in the world in terms of FDI. The paper analyses Nepal’s experience in industrial policy development since the 1992 liberalization reforms up to the new Industrial Policy and federal restructuring processes. Several key limitations to industrial development in Nepal are discussed, including the lack of infrastructure, limited land and financial resources, and instability of policy frameworks and institutions. The study also compares Nepal’s experience with that of Bangladesh in developing the ready-made garment industry and Vietnam’s export-led industrialization strategy. The paper concludes that industrial policy development needs to be pursued with a long-term policy commitment, backed by financial and infrastructural support. A stable institutional environment to be able to overcome the complex task of industrial policy design and implementation. Although the new federal structure creates the conditions for a positive industrialization process led by the provincial governments, there is still a need for the political will and the fiscal capacity to make it happen.

title: Inflation, Interest Rates, and Real Estate Performance: Assessing the Resilience of Property Investments During Economic Uncertainty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: Real estate has long been regarded by investors as a reliable store of value during periods of rising prices, yet the interaction between inflation, monetary policy, and property performance is more nuanced than the popular "real assets hedge inflation" narrative suggests. This article examines how inflationary pressure and the interest-rate cycles used to contain it jointly shape returns across residential, commercial, and securitized (REIT) real estate. Drawing on the theoretical foundations of the Fisher hypothesis, a synthesis of empirical literature spanning developed and emerging markets, three historical inflationary episodes, a comparative sector analysis, and a conceptual illustration of the competing transmission channels, the article argues that real estate's inflation-hedging capacity is conditional rather than automatic. It depends on lease structures, financing terms, property sector, holding period, valuation methodology, and the pace at which central banks raise rates. Direct, income-producing property with short lease-reset cycles and conservative leverage tends to preserve real value better than highly leveraged or ratesensitive segments such as listed REITs during aggressive tightening cycles. The article concludes with a comparative table of sector-level hedging characteristics, implications for portfolio construction and monetary policy transmission, a discussion of the literature's limitations, and directions for future research on regime-dependent hedging behavior.

title: When Stress Tests Miss the Risk: Statistical Scenario Analysis for Financial Portfolios
affiliations: Imperial College Business School, Imperial College Business School and Imperial College Business School

detail.title: When Stress Tests Miss the Risk: Statistical Scenario Analysis for Financial Portfolios

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have no conflict of interested

detail.abstract: Scenario analysis is widely used to stress test financial portfolios, yet conventional approaches often summarize scenario gains using point estimates that overlook dependence between stressed and unstressed risk factors. We develop a machine learning framework for quantifying uncertainty in realized next-day scenario gains through prediction intervals whose widths can be calibrated online. Adaptive conformal scenario analysis (ACSA) calibrates scenario-specific quantile predictions and provides a longrun empirical coverage guarantee over realized scenarios. Our main method, kernel scenario analysis (KSA), estimates scenario-conditional quantiles directly from the specified stress and current market information. KSA can also be combined with ACSA to obtain online-calibrated prediction intervals. In experiments designed to reflect real-world markets, conventional scenario analysis can substantially understate risk, including for portfolios that appear safe under standard stress tests. Our proposed methods achieve better calibration and sharper intervals than empirical-quantile baselines. Overall, the framework moves scenario analysis beyond point estimates by quantifying predictive uncertainty and providing tools for statistically validating scenario gains.

title: When are Mathematical Guarantees Informative? Perturbation Theory and Noise Filtering in Indian Stock Correlations
affiliations: DPS International, Gurugram, Haryana,  and Ahmedabad University

detail.title: When are Mathematical Guarantees Informative? Perturbation Theory and Noise Filtering in Indian Stock Correlations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable

detail.abstract: Modern financial markets generate large amounts of data, often compiled as a correlation matrix. A correlation matrix is a grid that records how strongly each stock's daily returns move with those of every other. Sample correlation matrices estimated from finite return series inevitably blend genuine economic structure with random estimation noise, creating severe instabilities in risk-minimising portfolio optimisation. Classical matrix perturbation guarantees, specifically Weyl's inequality for eigenvalues and the Davis Kahan theorem for eigenvectors, become mathematically informative versus empirically vacuous when applied to quantitative risk modeling. Using an eight-year sample of India's benchmark Nifty 50 constituents, spectral stability across varying market regimes using tools from Random Matrix Theory and functional analysis was evaluated. It was observed that the applicability of mathematical guarantees is strictly regime-dependent. Empirically, the Indian equity market has evolved from a single-block emerging market into a multi-factor structure containing four distinct sector factors (notably distinguishing state-linked capital activity from private consumption). While filtering noise yields marginal gains in low noise-ratio ($q = N/T$) regimes where sample estimators converge, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage spectral filtering provides material risk reduction in short estimation windows, larger asset universes, or long-short allocations. Overall, this study demonstrates how matrix perturbation theory can be operationally used to separate stable systemic risk factors from volatile sector tilts in emerging equity markets.

title: The Interactive Modified Sahm Rule Tool: A Turning-Point Framework for Economic Downturn Detection

detail.abstract: This paper describes the Interactive Modified Sahm Rule Tool, a web application that operationalizes the Modified Sahm Rule developed in Sheppard (2025). The original Sahm Rule signals a recession when the three-month average unemployment rate rises half a percentage point above its low over the prior year. The tool treats this construction as a general turning-point function, a deviation from a local extremum, and exposes each of its parameters as a live control: the series used for the recent level and for the rolling minimum, the recession benchmark, the smoothing of each component, the length and alignment of the comparison window, seasonal adjustment, the signaling threshold, and a natural-rate floor. For each configuration the tool reports the signal's lead over the official committee announcement, its lead or lag relative to the recession start, and its historical accuracy.

title: Learning Latent Factor Smoothness with Matérn Gaussian Processes: An Extension of the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model

detail.title: Learning Latent Factor Smoothness with Matérn Gaussian Processes: An Extension of the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This study was financed in part by the Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior – Brasil (CAPES) – Finance Code 001.

detail.abstract: The dynamic Nelson-Siegel model usually lets the level, slope, and curvature factors of the yield curve follow autoregressive processes, which fixes their local regularity by construction. We replace these dynamics with one-dimensional Matérn Gaussian processes. The Matérn covariance separates the time scale of dependence, governed by a range parameter, from local regularity, governed by a smoothness parameter, and nests the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck case at ν = 1/2. The factors are represented through the stochastic partial differential equation approach and estimated with integrated nested Laplace approximations, which provide fast, fully Bayesian inference on the latent factors and covariance parameters. In the out-of-sample design of Diebold and Li (2006), the posterior places the smoothness of all three factors close to ν = 3/2, well above the exponential case. Estimating smoothness for every factor sharply reduces first-order autocorrelation in one-month forecast errors, but the joint estimates of smoothness and range also produce stronger mean reversion in the level and a systematic bias at long horizons. A factor-specific model that keeps exponential dynamics for the level and estimates smoothness only for slope and curvature delivers the lowest root mean squared errors at the three-, five-, and ten-year maturities at every horizon considered. Smoothness thus emerges as a distinct, factor-specific feature of yield-curve dynamics, one that can be learned from the data instead of fixed in advance.

detail.abstract: India spent nearly $72 billion on gold imports in 2025-26, despite its substantial domestic holdings. This article argues that reducing import dependence requires distinguishing gold held for consumption from gold held for investment. Jewellery's cultural and emotional significance limits households' willingness to release it, while investment holdings offer greater scope for substitution towards financial assets. Reviewing India's existing gold schemes and drawing lessons from Indonesia, the article proposes a regulatory framework that makes digital gold accessible and trustworthy through clear customer rights, verified backing, secure custody and reliable withdrawals. A separate, voluntary connection to bank deposits and lending could make existing domestic gold available to jewellers. Digitalisation alone, however, need not reduce imports if providers purchase equivalent quantities of new gold to support household balances. The priority for policymakers is therefore to build credible financial alternatives to physical gold while enabling domestic holdings to replace imported supply. 1 Disclaimer: The views expressed here are solely the responsibility of the author and should not be interpreted as reflecting the views of the Centre for Advanced Financial Research and Learning (CAFRAL) or the Reserve Bank of India.

detail.abstract: Dot and Box Theory models market structure as cooperating "boxes" of agents that can freeze into monopoly. detail.abstract: States often lack the local knowledge needed to address concealed social-order problems. We argue that grassroots organizations strengthen state capacity and expand state presence by connecting information acquired through public services and local embeddedness to the state's coercive apparatus. We study the rollout of China's grid governance across 2,844 county-level units from 2013 to 2020. After introduction, more social-order violation cases originate in residents' reports to community workers or workers' own observations, and officials respond faster, indicating greater bureaucratic efficiency. Administrative punishment rises for these social-order violations while related criminal cases decline, suggesting prevention through earlier intervention. These changes are larger where grids emphasize services and recruit locally embedded workers. This study highlights how grassroots organizations strengthen state capacity by giving state agencies access to community knowledge and expanding local state presence.

detail.abstract: U.S. annuity buyers outlive the population, and posted prices mix selection with insurer funding costs. Pairing insurers' life-annuity and term-certain quotes with their institutional funding spreads, we separate selection from funding costs by age, gender, and insurer. Selection reduces annuity income by a tenth to a sixth at 65 and nearly a quarter at 85, but at ages 60 to 65 insurers pass back enough extra asset return to offset it. This selection is of the same order as money's-worth studies found, and the remaining gap to actuarially fair payouts reflects insurers' cost of bearing risk on long-duration payments.

title: Growth Without Welfare? ISEWs for the EU27 and its regions: trends, crises and resilience
affiliations: Ghent University and Ghent University

detail.title: Growth Without Welfare? ISEWs for the EU27 and its regions: trends, crises and resilience
detail.abstract: We compile two variants of the Index of Sustainable Economic Welfare (ISEW) for the EU27 and its regions over 1995-2024, differing in the time and space dimensions considered. ISEW_BCE captures current welfare experiences within a country’s borders whereas ISEW_BCPA integrates the benefits and costs experienced in the future and abroad. Building on Van der Slycken and Bleys (2024), who compiled both ISEWs for the EU15 over 1995-2018, we update the methodologies of the measures and extend the analysis along two margins: geographic coverage (the EU27, including the thirteen Member States that joined after 2004), and a longer time window (through 2024, capturing the Covid-19 crisis in full) enabling detailed analysis of crisis impacts on welfare. Based on the evolution of the ISEWs, we investigate two research questions. First, we explore whether growth has become uneconomic in the EU27. We find that, as for the EU15, this is not the case, neither for the EU27 nor any of the five regions defined in this study, as the welfare measures increased overall over the full period, though less than GDP. Second, we analyse the reaction of the two welfare measures to the financial and Covid-19 crises, comparing them to each other and GDP. We find that the welfare measures were hit less strongly than GDP but also experienced a smaller rebound in both cases, and Covid-19 had a stronger impact on all measures. Our findings reaffirm the importance of accounting for all the benefits and costs of economic growth when measuring welfare.

title: The Cost of Coordinating Expert Allocation Selective Elicitation under Client Mandates
affiliations: New York University

detail.title: The Cost of Coordinating Expert Allocation Selective Elicitation under Client Mandates

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: An investment committee receives its experts' recommendations before it reads the reports behind them, and the client's mandate censors what those recommendations say: a recommendation at a boundary reveals conviction only up to that boundary. We ask how many reports it must open to implement the allocation a fully informed client would choose. A minimax-regret certificate says when to stop without requiring the experts to agree, and the committee stops at the first report whose revealed conviction covers the shortfall of the unconstrained experts relative to the mandate boundary. In expectation that count is approximately the shortfall divided by the average hidden conviction of a constrained expert, capped by the number of constrained experts; it is zero when every report exceeds the boundary or none reaches it, and positive between. With several assets and continuous implementation, each direction the mandate leaves free must be resolved exactly and each direction it pins only covered. The implementation tolerance is the cost of a report relative to the portfolio: stopping when the certificate falls below it never forgoes more than one report's price. On 84 monthly decisions from public institutional forecasts, exact reproduction of the fully informed allocation opens 9.3 of 28.6 reports (hindsight minimum 7.8); at one basis point of monthly score the committee opens 0.3, none in 70 months, and forgoes 0.1 basis points a month. Consultation buys the last basis point; a committee should decide what that is worth before deciding how much to read.

title: When Restricting Access Increases Information Diffusion: The Economics of Dual-Use Knowledge

detail.abstract: Information can create value for one recipient and destroy value in another. We study access to endogenously produced dual-use knowledge. An originator chooses costly creation effort after an institution commits to screening and containment. This creates a distinction between conditional diffusion-how many productive users receive a realized discovery-and equilibrium diffusion, which also reflects whether the discovery is produced. We characterize an Access-Control Dividend : selective access can reduce conditional productive diffusion while increasing productive knowledge use in equilibrium. The main theorem gives the complete dividend region in true-positive-false-positive space and shows how leakage contracts it. Endogenous creation also changes the socially optimal tradeoff between screening errors and creates a wedge between private and social access rules. A downstream competition model shows that the mechanism can arise even when imitation is statically procompetitive. The framework applies to trade secrets, security procedures, vulnerabilities, and other dual-use knowledge.

title: The Economics of Adversarial Innovation R&D Direction and Strategic Technological Obsolescence

detail.abstract: Firms and other strategic actors can use R&D either to improve their own technology or to develop counterinnovations that reduce the effectiveness of technologies already in use. This paper studies that choice in a dynamic game with accumulated technological capability and endogenous robustness. Greater vulnerability to counterinnovation can raise total R&D while lowering effective technological progress, and successful technologies become more attractive targets. The useful life of technology is therefore determined jointly by innovation and adaptation. When research direction is difficult to observe, policies that reward aggregate R&D can stimulate both technological creation and technological neutralization.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Investment Portfolio Management: A Comparison Review with Traditional Financial Methods
