detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping investment portfolio management by enabling nonlinear learning, dynamic allocation and the processing of high-dimensional market information. Yet greater model complexity does not necessarily produce superior investable performance. This study conducts a structured comparative review of traditional portfolio methods and recent AI-based approaches, focusing on return, risk-adjusted performance, transaction costs and turnover, market-regime robustness, explainability and implementation feasibility. The review combines foundational portfolio theory with recent peer-reviewed evidence on machine learning, deep learning, deep reinforcement learning, automated model selection and cost-aware optimization. The synthesis shows that AI can improve representation, forecasting and adaptive allocation, especially in dynamic and high-dimensional settings, but apparent gains can disappear after realistic trading frictions, unstable training or regime shifts. Traditional methods therefore remain important benchmarks and portfolio-control mechanisms. Building on the evidence, the study proposes a six-dimensional evaluation framework and an evidence-derived hybrid architecture in which AI supports signal generation and regime detection while constrained financial optimization governs allocation, risk and implementation. The main contribution is an integrated decision protocol that shifts comparison from isolated predictive or gross-return performance toward investable decision quality. Future research should validate the framework and architecture on common datasets, multiple market regimes and harmonized transaction-cost assumptions, reporting both gross and net-of-cost performance

title: Rotation-Robust Skin Lesion Classification Using Gated EfficientNet–Vision Transformer Fusion
affiliations: The University of the South Pacific, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Rotation-Robust Skin Lesion Classification Using Gated EfficientNet–Vision Transformer Fusion
detail.abstract: Dermoscopic skin-lesion classifiers are typically evaluated at a single fixed orientation, yet clinical images arrive at arbitrary rotations whose performance impact is rarely characterized. This paper presents a rotation-robust classification pipeline and subjects its robustness claim to a controlled test. A shared spatial transformer network (STN) preprocesses both encoder inputs, and a learned per-sample scalar gate fuses local EfficientNet-B0 features with global Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) features. On HAM10000 (10,015 images, seven lesion classes) the reported single-seed model reaches 91.16% validation accuracy with maximum relative rotation degradation (RRD_max) of 0.89% over a complete 24-angle protocol. A 2×2 factorial then isolates the source: rotation robustness comes primarily from training-time rotation augmentation, not from the STN—removing rotation augmentation inflates RRD_max from under 1.3% to 11–18% regardless of the STN. One-factor and multi-seed experiments further show that the STN, scalar gate, and pooling choices lie within run-to-run variation (n=3 seeds), leaving the full model statistically indistinguishable from a simpler no-STN gated fusion; interpolation-label augmentation (MixUp), by contrast, leaves clean accuracy unchanged yet inflates RRD_max above 50% by making the model brittle to test-time interpolation. A held-out partition (87.87%, RRD_max 1.14%) and external validation on three datasets (ISIC 2019, ISIC 2020, out-of-archive PH2) confirms robustness transfers zero-shot (RRD_max≤1.67%), while target-domain fine-tuning recovers ISIC 2019 accuracy to 85.55%. Temperature scaling reduced expected calibration error from 0.2301 to 0.1880. The contribution is a calibrated, externally-validated rotation-robust pipeline and a controlled, multi-seed attribution of its orientation stability to the training regime rather than the architecture.

title: Central Banks and Republican Liberty: The Case Against Independence

detail.title: Central Banks and Republican Liberty: The Case Against Independence

detail.abstract: Central banks present a prima facie problem for republican political theory: they wield substantial power over citizens' economic lives while remaining insulated from democratic control. This paper develops a republican framework for evaluating monetary institutions, grounded in the conception of liberty as non-domination, and applies it to central banking. We argue that central banks are justifiable in principle on republican grounds, since monetary instability and financial panics themselves threaten nondomination. But this justification holds only under demanding conditions: a single mandate focused on price stability; strict Bagehot-style emergency lending rules; and simple, legible regulatory standards that resist the "expert trap" of technical complexity. The empirical record of the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank suggests these conditions are chronically unmet, with mission creep and accountability gaps producing structural domination rather than incidental inefficiency. Our demanding conditions thus point to necessary institutional revisions for central banks. These preclude central bank independence, since all changes entail an active role for political authorities who are themselves directly democratically accountable. The paper contributes to an underdeveloped republican analysis of monetary institutions, which existing scholarship has treated in primarily technocratic or libertarian terms.

detail.abstract: Economic theory and observational data suggest that a college student's choice of major is an important causal determinant of their future income. While identifying the causal effect of a college major on income is difficult since major choice is endogenous, Bleemer and Mehta (2022) plausibly identify the return to an economics degree using a regression discontinuity design. However, they do not provide returns in the form of an hourly wage, instead providing them as an effect on overall earnings with no adjustment for hours worked. This omission might make it difficult for prospective students to tell whether an economics degree will raise their hourly earnings or merely funnel them into careers that require higher hours. Using American Community Survey (ACS) data, I estimate the hourly returns to the economics major by adjusting Bleemer and Mehta's estimate for hours worked. I find an estimated effect on hours worked of 11.48% and an estimated hourly return of 30.97%, 15.03 percentage points smaller than their estimated return to earnings of 46%.

detail.abstract: During the long economic expansion of the 2010s, employment growth in Massachusetts ran well above historic rates, ahead of the rest of New England, and on par with the national rate. Much of the job growth was in highly productive, high-paying sectors. The expansion ended with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in early 2020, and the Massachusetts economy that has emerged in the aftermath of the crisis looks different from the state’s pre-pandemic economy. In particular, job growth trails the rest of the region and the nation. Changes in the handful of sectors that were largely responsible for the strong growth in the preceding decade have driven this shift in fortunes.

title: Appropriate Entrepreneurship? The Rise of China and the Developing World
affiliations: Harvard Business School - Finance Unit, University of Warwick - Department of Economics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Harvard University

detail.title: Appropriate Entrepreneurship? The Rise of China and the Developing World
detail.abstract: Global innovation and entrepreneurship has traditionally been dominated by a handful of highincome countries, especially the US. This paper investigates the international consequences of the rise of a new hub for innovation, focusing on the dramatic growth of high-potential entrepreneurship and venture capital in China. First, using comprehensive data on global venture activities, we show that as the Chinese venture industry rose in importance, entrepreneurship increased substantially in other emerging markets, particularly in sectors dominated by Chinese companies. Using a broad set of country-level economic indicators, we find that this effect was driven by country-sector pairs most similar to their counterparts in China. Second, turning to mechanisms, we show that the baseline findings are driven by local investors and by new firms that more closely resemble existing Chinese companies. Third, we find that this growth in emerging-market investment had wide-ranging positive consequences, including a rise in serial entrepreneurship, cross-sector spillovers, innovation, and broader measures of socioeconomic well-being. Together, our findings suggest that developing countries benefited from more “appropriate” businesses and technology pioneered by China, and that a system where only rich countries lead in innovation could limit entrepreneurial activity in large parts of the world.

title: "They Caught us without any Reason": Waste Pickers' Encounters with Police, Crime and the State in Rawalpindi-Islamabad, Pakistan
affiliations: National Defence University

detail.title: "They Caught us without any Reason": Waste Pickers' Encounters with Police, Crime and the State in Rawalpindi-Islamabad, Pakistan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study was conducted as part of the author's MPhil thesis at the National Defence University, Islamabad, under the supervisor's approval.

detail.abstract:
Purpose. Informal waste pickers are routinely portrayed as a source of urban crime, yet little research asks how they themselves experience the police, the state and the illicit economies around them. This article examines the lived experiences of waste pickers in the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad, Pakistan, focusing on their encounters with law-enforcement bodies, their involvement in and victimisation by crime, and their access to government and NGO support. 

Design. Semi-structured interviews were conducted in Urdu with 25 waste pickers, aged roughly 10 to 50, living in informal settlements (katchi abadis) along the railway line near Mareer Chowk, along IJP Road, in the Afghan Basti in sector I-10/3, and in Pirwadhai. Participants were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling. Transcripts and field notes were analysed thematically, drawing on street-level bureaucracy and general strain theory. 

Findings. Four themes emerged. (1) Extractive policing: participants described arbitrary detention, bribes as the price of release or of being left alone, and police ties to the employers and dealers around them. (2) Crime as coerced and relational: most participants denied offending. Those who reported drug use or sex work described being drawn in by peers, clients, gangs or their own families, often while being victimised. (3) The absent state: no participant had received government or NGO assistance; BISP applications went unanswered, and the only NGO contact described followed an arrest. (4) Constrained pathways: waste picking was a response to family need, orphanhood, homelessness, physical incapacity or a family trade. Most participants said they would leave it if given financial support. 

Originality and implications. The findings reverse the usual framing of waste pickers as a crime problem. The police are experienced as a source of extraction rather than protection, and illicit activity is mostly entangled with exploitation. The article calls for protective, nonextractive policing, safeguarding responses to children in sex work and drug use, and outreach that makes social protection reachable for people without documents or fixed addresses.

detail.abstract: A supervisor observes a population of institutions at one date; a chief risk officer observes one institution over time. Each computes an average — one across institutions, one along a history — and the two are read as the same quantity. Worked out in full for an elementary process, they are not: they answer different questions, they part as consequences accumulate, and no amount of data brings them together. The supervisor's own average is also hard to measure: the dispersion across institutions can be so wide that no realistic number of them gives a reliable figure. That is true of the position and not of the growth rate, which — absent shared models — a cross-section and a history read equally well. Agentic workflows compound faster, so each effect is stronger. The process used here is the most favourable one a cross-section could have — institutions identical and independent — so the results are a floor rather than a worst case. The frameworks now being finalised for artificial intelligence ask for assessment without stating which of the two averages the resulting figures are. An institution should ask, of any figure put in front of it, which of the two averages it is, and gate the actions it cannot reverse rather than score them; a supervisor should collect what governs the outcome rather than scores returned by firms.

detail.abstract: This study examines structural and pragmatic features of dissertation titles in German and Russian language teaching methodology. Despite growing comparative research on academic discourse, the conventions governing dissertation titles in these two traditions remain insufficiently systematised. The research identifies structural characteristics (syntactic models, compositional schemes, length) and pragmatic features (selfpresentation strategies, rhetorical devices, addressivity) of titles defended in Germany and Russia. The material comprises dissertation titles analysed through structuralsyntactic, frequency, co-occurrence, and discourse-pragmatic methods. Results reveal that Russian titles are highly standardised, built predominantly on one-member verbalnoun constructions with predictable lexical co-occurrence, whereas German titles favour two-member colon constructions, demonstrating greater variability, interdisciplinarity, and methodological reflexivity. German authors position themselves as problematisers and empiricists addressing interdisciplinary audiences, whereas Russian authors act as methodology developers addressing a narrow expert community. Findings carry implications for intercultural rhetoric and academic writing pedagogy.

detail.abstract: Purpose: This article proposes a platform design for a university-industry-student job bank. The platform connects student research projects to real organizational problems through conditional employment. Existing job banks such as LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Handshake, Boss Zhipin, and Jobberman optimise the search for jobs but do not create them. The experience paradox persists because no platform internalises the training externality. Design/methodology/approach: The article is conceptual. It uses the platform design framework from Tura, Kutvonen, and Ritala (2018), which has four categories: architecture, value creation, governance, and competition. The article applies these categories to education-to-employment platforms. It analyses five existing job banks using the same framework. It draws on transaction cost economics to explain the market failure that the platform addresses. Findings: The analysis shows that existing job banks do not turn the research project into a job trial. They do not offer conditional employment during study. They do not internalise the training externality. The article proposes a design that addresses these gaps. The design has four components: a three-sided market structure, a value creation logic based on conditional appointments, a governance model with failed trial safeguards, and a launch strategy based on university partnerships. Research limitations/implications: The design is conceptual and has not been tested empirically. Future research should pilot the design with a university and a small number of organizations. Practical implications: The design offers universities, organizations, and policymakers a practical model for connecting academic research to employment. It addresses the experience paradox and the decline of entry-level jobs. Originality/value: The article extends the Tura et al. (2018) framework to a new context. It provides the first analysis of existing job banks using a platform design framework. It proposes a design for a multi-sided platform that creates employment by turning research into a job trial.

detail.abstract: We propose a framework that, while eliminating the endowment effect, accounts for the two leading explanations of the disparity between willingness to accept (WTA) and willingness to pay (WTP): loss aversion and preference imprecision. We illustrate the usefulness of this decomposition by reporting results from a simple experiment. Our setting is general and encompasses several prominent models as special cases. Finally, we argue that the WTA-WTP gap is a monetary measure (i.e., a premium) of uncertainty aversion.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the contemporary civil war in Sudan through the lens of elite-driven hate speech and its catastrophic economic and social consequences. Departing from Samuel Huntington's Clash of Civilizations paradigm-which initially appears analytically compelling given Sudan's intersection of Arab and African, Islamic and Christian, nomadic and urban identities-this study argues that the conflict is more accurately characterized as a deliberate politicization of difference by political and military elites. Drawing on World Bank macroeconomic data, IPC famine classifications, UNHCR displacement statistics, and theoretical frameworks from social identity theory, this paper demonstrates how hate speech functions as a cost-effective mobilization strategy for elites lacking economic vision or electoral legitimacy. The findings reveal a 29.4% GDP contraction in 2023 and an additional 13.5% in 2024, extreme poverty rising from 23.3% to 57.0%, approximately 9.8 million internally displaced persons, and famine conditions confirmed in multiple locations with over 21 million people experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity. The paper concludes that Sudan's crisis is not a clash of civilizations but a civilizational suicide-a deliberate destruction of coexistence through the weaponization of ethnic, tribal, color, and regional identities.

detail.abstract: Strategic planning has progressively absorbed concepts and methods from knowledge management, strategic foresight, decision sciences, systems engineering, organisational learning, evaluation, and research on dynamic capabilities. Yet these contributions remain dispersed across several scientific traditions. This conceptual article examines whether their interfaces can be formalised within an integrative research field termed Strategic Planning Engineering. The proposal is grounded in a principle of scientific specialisation and integration: as knowledge expands and complexity increases, science tends to create more specialised subfields capable of producing greater analytical precision, while simultaneously creating a need for architectures that reconnect fragmented expertise. The paper adopts a thesis-antithesis-synthesis structure. The thesis argues that strategic planning has become sufficiently complex to be studied as an engineered architecture. The antithesis questions whether a new field is necessary when established disciplines already address its components. The synthesis positions Strategic Planning Engineering not as a replacement for existing fields, but as an integrative architecture focused on their interfaces.

detail.abstract: Intra-daily trading volume forecasts are a key input for algorithmic trade execution. We introduce a forecasting methodology for large panels of assets that combines factor models with sparse vector autoregressions. The approach captures both market-wide common factors driving trading activity and the sparse network of volume spillovers among individual assets, consistent with a framework where information diffuses sequentially from leader to lagger stocks. We apply the methodology to a panel of 600 constituents of the STOXX 600 index spanning 16 European countries. We assess both the statistical accuracy and the economic value of the forecasts through an out-of-sample prediction exercise and a VWAP trade execution analysis. Results show that our methodology delivers significant statistical and economic gains relative to standard univariate benchmarks. The improvements are heterogeneous: the largest gains accrue to stocks with high network connectivity, while firm size also plays a significant role, consistent with the information diffusion mechanism underlying our approach.

detail.abstract: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple in Andhra Pradesh, India, receives roughly 70,000 to 80,000 pilgrims on an ordinary day, yet visitors have no reliable way to anticipate crowd levels or waiting times when planning a trip. This paper introduces the Darshan Queue Pressure Index (Darshan-QPI™), a framework for forecasting daily pilgrim footfall and queue pressure from publicly available administrative data. Rather than treating the reported visitor count as a direct measure of demand, the framework models the queue as a flow: pressure carried over from the previous day, plus new arrivals, less the day's throughput. Served counts are bounded by throughput, so on the busiest days they understate true demand. Using 1,726 daily observations from January 2022 to September 2026, we evaluate a family of baseline forecasts in a rolling-origin backtest over 995 days (2024-2026). A level × weekday × year-over-year model forecasts daily footfall with a mean absolute error of about 4,200 pilgrims (5.9%) one day ahead and 4,600 (6.5%) thirty days ahead, 9-14% better than a plain weekday average, and its empirical 80% prediction bands achieve 79-81% coverage. Served-pilgrim counts rise only modestly with reported waiting time and fall on the longest-wait days, consistent with a throughput ceiling. A case study of the September 2026 Salakatla Brahmotsavam festival suggests that festival days are not uniformly busy: public procession days run at or above baseline, while ritual and interior festival days run 10-16% below it. The framework is designed to extend to other high-volume pilgrimage sites.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: A firm combines an inexpensive regular supplier subject to delivery failures with a faster, more expensive express supplier. Regular orders must respond to inventory and scheduled deliveries, although some outstanding orders will never arrive. We study how to use this information while guaranteeing performance relative to established sourcing policies. Methodology/results: We develop a projected-bias (PB) policy using the one-dimensional continuation cost of a tailored base-surge (TBS) policy. With reliable express supply and independent regular yields in [0, 1], PB has no higher expected average cost than its TBS benchmark at every finite lead time. Under only a finite positive demand mean, we also establish asymptotic optimality of the best TBS and PB policies as the regular lead time grows. All-or-nothing failures simplify the PB comparison to an evaluation conditional on delivery. For exponential demand, we characterize when a simple projection target implements PB; fractional yields require weighting outcomes by delivered quantities. A separate continuation-cost screen protects a capped dual-index benchmark. We further establish TBS asymptotic optimality with immediate Bernoulli express failures. Explicit cost comparisons and exact discrete-demand calculations illustrate the mechanisms. Managerial implications: Replacing uncertain receipts by their mean misses their inventory consequences. Greater receipt variability can lower the optimal express stock while raising cost, even at a fixed mean receipt rate. Confirming regular deliveries before expediting reduces inventory mismatch; we quantify its value in an exponential-demand setting. PB combines a guarantee at practical lead times with asymptotically optimal performance when its TBS reference is optimized.

detail.abstract: Is looking at a map sufficient to understand a geography? Political borders, administrative lines, coordinates, and physical barriers demonstrate the material order of space; however, the geography lived by human beings is far broader than this. Humans do not merely observe their surroundings; they name, narrate, remember, contextualize, and reconstruct space through relationships of belonging. For this reason, certain borders remain invisible on conventional maps, yet maintain their existence in language, place names, social memory, narratives, and spatial forms of belonging. In this study, the concept of the "invisible border" is proposed as a conceptual framework outside political or administrative boundaries. Operating through language, place names, social memory, narratives, belonging, and spatial perception, this framework shapes how spaces are differentiated, brought closer together, or given meaning within people's mental geographies. The core assumption of this study is that geography possesses not only a physical surface, but also a linguistic, historical, and mental layer. In this context, the relationship between philology and cultural geography is reexamined. It is argued that place names are not merely tools for orientation or identification, but can also be investigated as linguistic carriers of past experiences, cultural relations, and social memory. The study proposes a sequential process model extending from physical space to naming, linguistic representation, narrative and experience, memory, belonging, mental geography, and ultimately to the invisible border: physical space → naming → linguistic representation → narrative and experience → memory → belonging → mental geography → invisible border. Rather than proposing an alternative border system to replace political boundaries, this model aims to explain the linguistic and mental dimensions of the human-space relationship that extend beyond physical geography.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: An assembly manufacturer needs every component to fill a product order. A criticalset base-surge policy coordinates express purchases but fixes each component's regular order, even when inventories and scheduled deliveries change. We ask whether regular orders can adapt to that information while retaining a cost guarantee against the matched constant-order policy. Methodology/results: We construct a projected-bias score that evaluates staggered entries of regular orders into expedited inventory positions and the benchmark's continuation value after the last entry. A regular-order policy that never raises this exact score has no greater long-run average physical cost than its benchmark under independent and identically distributed demand with finite mean, positive component holding rates, unequal regular lead times, and a common express lead time. A finite-bias truncation bound certifies exact-expectation comparisons, and calibrated simulation retains the expected-cost guarantee. Under explicit computational bounds, coordinated candidate screening is polynomial in the number of components. Exact two-component examples yield strict savings; one shows that a coordinated order succeeds although either component's order alone fails the test. Under the published benchmark's additional assumptions, the improved policy class inherits its large-regular-lead performance bound. A serial extension admits exact polynomial action selection when total network stock and other structural bounds are fixed. Managerial implications: Scheduled component arrivals can guide regular orders without sacrificing the benchmark guarantee when action comparisons are certified. Joint evaluation matters because the value of one component depends on the availability of the others.

detail.abstract: Texas discharges young people from juvenile justice supervision on a date it knows from the day the case opens, into a day it has never priced and does not measure. The companion paper names that condition the post-jurisdictional gap and shows that it is unfunded rather than unchosen. This paper asks what the corrected design would be and holds every candidate component to the same evidentiary standard, including the components the author's own field prefers. The synthesis covers ten bodies of program evaluation: credible messenger mentoring, street outreach, transitional employment, extended foster care, intensive juvenile aftercare, a bundled transition program for young adults leaving state custody, Medicaid at release, family-based treatment, restorative justice, and a randomized Texas trial of court-anchored diversion for emerging adults. The record is not uniformly encouraging and the paper says so. The most rigorous test of relentless outreach standing alone produced no beneficial estimates. The one randomized trial of a calendared, relational transition delivered by the parole authority produced nothing. Transitional jobs work only at the exit and only for the higher-risk. Read as one record, the evidence orders three properties by what each one moves. A status that survives the case and timing calendared to the exit, held together, move stability and leave arrest untouched. A credible relationship moves arrest and violence. All three held together move both, and the only record that holds all three did so under a court. No evaluated program has held all three without one. The paper states that ordering as eight design propositions for a voluntary, calendared, former-status bridge, shows that no component requires invention in Texas, states which components federal and Texas law deliver and which the state would have to buy, and specifies an evaluation registered to expect a stability effect first and an arrest effect later or smaller. The author operates a program that prototypes two of the eight design components, an interest disclosed on the title page, and the design is written so that a null finding counts against the design rather than against the evaluation.

title: Decouple, Calibrate, and Compensate: Heterogeneous Mamba-Wavelet Representation Learning for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
affiliations: South China University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology and Guangzhou Medical University - Guangdong Women and Children Hospital

detail.title: Decouple, Calibrate, and Compensate: Heterogeneous Mamba-Wavelet Representation Learning for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
detail.abstract: Accurate 3D medical image segmentation requires fine boundary delineation, long-range anatomical consistency, and frequency-sensitive structural modeling. Existing CNN--Mamba hybrid models usually combine local convolutional features and global Mamba representations through serial stacking or naive fusion, which may lead to heterogeneous representation conflict and path dominance. Moreover, spatial-domain local features often entangle true anatomical boundaries with noise and artifact-related high-frequency responses. We propose DCC-MWNet, a Decouple-Calibrate-Compensate Mamba-Wavelet network for 3D medical image segmentation. DCC-MWNet first uses a Decoupled Parallel Block to separate CNN-based local modeling and Mamba-based global context modeling. It then introduces Bidirectional Calibration Fusion to align heterogeneous local-global representations through channel-wise and spatial cross-branch calibration. Finally, a Wavelet-guided Feature Disentanglement Module extracts input-derived low-frequency structural priors and high-frequency boundary cues via 3D DWT/IDWT, generating frequency-aware modulation maps to guide the calibrated fused representation.Experiments on FeTA2021, an in-house fetal brain dataset, BraTS2023, and BTCV demonstrate that DCC-MWNet achieves average Dice scores of 90.49%, 94.64%, 92.56%, and 88.61%, respectively, outperforming competitive CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based baselines across fetal brain tissue, brain tumor, and abdominal multi-organ segmentation tasks.

detail.abstract: This document applies the Ising model of ferromagnetism to understand social coordination in networked populations. The structure of the influence network plays a central role in determining whether coordination can emerge. The simplest case is a line network where each node interacts only with immediate neighbors, but even this case yields insights about the limits of peer influence, the role of randomness, and the conditions under which spontaneous coordination can (or cannot) appear. On a two-dimensional lattice network, both continuous and discontinuous phase transitions appear. Whether coordination is feasible depends on the level of extraneous uncertainty, the rationality of decision makers, the strength of peer influence, and any external policy instruments, such as subsidies or taxes. On a hierarchical Bethe lattice, where every node has the same number of neighbors, the chances of spontaneous coordination increase with that number. On a scale-free network, connectivity is heterogeneous. If the second moment of the degree distribution is large (heavy-tailed distributions), spontaneous coordination can become inevitable. The analysis also reveals a close connection between the cavity method of statistical mechanics and backward induction in game theory. The Ising model originates in statistical mechanics but has applications across many fields, including economics. Contents

detail.abstract: A crucial policy target to ensure the consumption of clean and affordable energy by everyone by the close of 2030 is enshrined in goal seven of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). While the role of credit access in facilitating the transition from unclean to clean fuels has received considerable attention, how credit access affects the choice of specific energy among Ghanaian households remains a literature gap. In closing this gap, the current study employed household-level data from the Ghana Statistical Service within a Control Function (CF) approach to analyze the impact of credit access on specific energy choice. The findings indicate that credit access reduces the probability of households opting for fuelwood, while it increases the chance of using LPG for cooking. Credit access, however, has no significant effect on the likelihood of households to opt for electricity and crop residue. Further, the heterogenous effects showed that the positive effect of credit access on clean energy transition is significant only for larger and richer households, emphasizing the sensitivity of energy choice to household size and income. The government of Ghana is advised to deepen policies that enhance credit access to households to promote clean energy transition. Also, given the importance of household income for clean energy transition, government policies must prioritize gainful jobs for Ghanaians.

detail.abstract: We study certification markets in which certifiers announce a quality standard and certify any client that meets it. When certifiers set their own fees, a monopolist chooses an inefficiently low standard, while, in the equilibria we characterize, any degree of competition induces the standard preferred by the typical client. When fees are instead fixed-as in higher-education accreditation-certifiers extract rents by requiring clients to adopt practices the certifier favors: a monopolist couples a low standard with substantial bias, and competition raises standards and reduces bias only gradually. Entry by a maverick certifier with an opposing agenda raises quality and lowers every certifier's bias, improving welfare far more than entry by another aligned certifier. Our results thus bear directly on the current policy debate over the merits of inducing competition among higher-education accreditors.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the macroeconomic and structural determinants of nonperforming loan (NPL) accumulation across 28 European economies during the post-crisis adjustment period (2008-2016). Employing a comprehensive panel econometric framework encompassing Pooled OLS, Entity Fixed Effects, Two-Way Fixed Effects, First-Difference, and Dynamic Instrumental Variable specifications, we identify unemployment as the dominant accelerator of credit risk, with a one percentage point increase generating a 1.47 percentage point rise in NPL ratios under the preferred Two-Way Fixed Effects specification (p < 0.001). Real GDP growth exhibits significant counter-cyclical effects, while bank capital ratios demonstrate complex bidirectional causality reflecting macroprudential recapitalization dynamics. Dynamic panel estimation reveals substantial NPL persistence (ρ = 0.4709), indicative of structural hysteresis in European distressed debt markets. Bank branch density exerts a marginally significant negative effect on default rates, supporting the monitoring efficiency hypothesis. ATM density effects are absorbed by timeinvariant country heterogeneity, reflecting the confounding influence of institutional development on financial infrastructure penetration. These findings yield critical implications for macroprudential policy design, labor market stabilization, and distressed asset resolution frameworks within the European Banking Union.

Pre-emptive treatment of cryptococcal antigenaemia with fluconazole monotherapy is associated with 25%-33% excess mortality, largely attributed to inadequate treatment. The EFFECT randomised controlled trial is designed to evaluate whether a combination oral regimen of fluconazole plus flucytosine reduces mortality compared to the standard of care. This paper describes the protocol for the economic evaluation conducted alongside the trial, with the primary hypothesis that a reduction in all-cause mortality offsets higher drug costs and yields a favourable incremental cost-effectiveness ratio.

Secondary outcomes will include cost per disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) averted, disaggregated analyses by country and facility, and incidence of catastrophic healthcare expenditure (CHE). detail.abstract: This paper examines how exposure to Western cultural content shapes gender norms and family formation behaviors. We exploit China's 1994 film-import reform as a quasi-natural experiment and employ a cohort-based difference-indifferences design. Our analysis documents that a one-standard-deviation increase in exposure to the film-market opening reduces the Gender Attitude Index by 0.076 standard deviations among women, with no statistically detectable effects for men. These attitudinal shifts translate into behavioral responses at the intensive margin: exposure delays women's age at first marriage by 0.174 years and age at first birth by 0.228 years, while leaving extensive-margin outcomes-such as the probability of ever marrying or having a child-unchanged. Furthermore, by applying large language models to film narratives and implementing a difference-in-discontinuities design, we find that Western films after the reform contain a significantly higher proportion of modern values, particularly themes of autonomy, defiance of social conventions, and individual agency, relative to local productions.

detail.abstract: Business schools teach students to converse with generative AI, while the work those graduates will do is being reshaped by intentional autonomous agents that execute multi-step tasks across files and applications and return finished deliverables. This paper argues that the resulting gap is wide enough to require a change at the level of the curriculum, and that fluency in directing such agents should become a graded competency in the MBA core rather than an optional elective. The argument draws on the authors' experience teaching the adjacent discipline to software engineers, adapting a discipline-based curriculum for agentic software engineering to the deliverable-centred work of the business graduate. The competency is defined not as a checklist of equal parts but as a single analytical judgment, the direction of an agent, with oversight, verification, and the safe handling of data and access as dimensions of doing that one thing well. Empirical work on knowledge-worker productivity, on the failure modes of agentic systems, and on the shallow ways students currently use these tools supports both the diagnosis and the design. The paper offers a concrete teaching pattern built around a planted error, in which an agent produces a result that is plausible and wrong and the student's task is to catch it, because the value a graduate adds lives in the check rather than in the generation. It closes with two models for placing the competency in a programme, the obstacle of faculty readiness, and an honest admission that the framework awaits empirical validation.

detail.abstract: The traditional joint family system has long been a defining feature of Indian society, promoting unity, oneness, and a sense of familial interconnectedness. However, with the advent of urbanization, globalization, and changing socioeconomic factors, nuclear families are increasingly taking precedence. This shift towards nuclearization of family has significant implications for the tribal households of Arunachal Pradesh. In this article, we will explore the changing dimensions of family structures from joint to nuclear, probing the reasons behind this transition and its impact on the tribal society. We will also discuss the challenges and benefits associated with both types of family setups. By employing a mixed research design, primary and secondary data, including interviews and existing publications have been taken into consideration to delve into the personal experiences, opinions, and reflections of different respondents on the subject and sheds light on the erosion of familial bonds and values, the rise of individualism, and the need to fortify the basic social unit known as the family. Prime factors found to be facilitating this paradigm shift were economic burden to sustain large family and rural to urban migration for higher educational and job opportunities and achieving a better standard of living. While this transformation brings certain advantages, such as increased autonomy and flexibility, it also poses challenges to the traditional fabric of society. The erosion of familial bonds, the rise of individualism, and the influence of technology require a proactive and collective response.

detail.abstract: The label "peer-reviewed" can be read as a currency: journals issue it, careers spend it, and the scrutiny of reviewers backs it. This note examines, in a stylized model, what may happen to the circulation of that currency when the papers reaching review grow exponentially and the pool of reviewers does not. The note applies the information-limit and cost results of the Correction Freeze Problem to that setting and adds dynamics of its own; the results are derived with elementary tools and checked numerically. With Gaussian review traces, the information a label carries falls as the square of the ratio of capacity to load once load exceeds capacity, and if reviewers choose their effort, the cost route makes it fall to exactly zero at a finite workload. When reviewers leave at a rate that rises with their own workload, the pool has two stable sizes exactly when ρ < sup w wh ′ (w)h(w) , where ρ is replenishment relative to attrition and h is the attrition response, which for a Hill response means that its steepness exceeds (√ ρ + √ 1 + ρ) 2 , and collapse sets in while the freeze index is still below one. Circulation can fail in two ways: the flow can stall, with waiting times that grow exponentially once load passes capacity, or it can continue while the backing thins. In monetary terms, once the freeze index exceeds one the price level of the label rises at the growth rate of submissions, and the collapse combines a jump in that price level with a fall in real backing. When journals share one pool and each gains from issuing more, above a threshold number of issuers the model holds the freeze index above capacity, so that issuance can rise while the scrutiny behind each label falls. Under exponential growth, in the model, any policy that scales the load by 1/k delays collapse by exactly ln k/r and by no more, and only changes to the growth rate, to reviewer supply and its reward, or a cap set below the recovery threshold alter the long-run outcome. All results are theoretical, rest on stated functional forms, and are offered for discussion.

title: Overbooking with Preferences and Priorities: When Popularity Drives Inequality

detail.abstract: In many matching markets, resources need to be reassigned after the initial assignment due to opt out from the system. We study this problem through the lens of overbooking in settings where agents are assigned to capacity-constrained items while respecting both agents' preferences over items and items' priority ordering over agents. Our main finding is the presence of a bullwhip-like effect: under a broad class of overbooking policies, less popular items incur higher costs due to externalities generated by more popular items. We first establish this effect in a base model in which agents share identical preference lists and priority rankings, quantifying the asymptotic costs incurred by each item, and then demonstrate its robustness across several extensions. We also provide guidance on how to overbook in the presence of the bullwhip-like effect. We show the effect necessitates a tradeoff where costs can be made more equitable only by increasing costs at popular items. We characterize the cost-minimizing overbooking policy and show, despite the tradeoff, it performs well for many equity-adjusted objectives, motivating general heuristics. Finally, we validate our findings with simulations using school district data. We find a persistent cost disparity across overbooking policies, and show our heuristics significantly reduce costs but primarily at more popular schools.

detail.abstract: Consumer generative AI is sold on a price ladder (roughly $8, $20, $100 and $200 a month) that is nearly identical across countries. I document what this ladder costs relative to income in 201 economies, audit tax-inclusive local App Store prices for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini in 170 storefronts, and relate burdens to two independent measures of diffusion. Local dollar prices barely respond to income: the elasticity is 0.03–0.04 for $20 plans and 0.14 for ChatGPT Go, OpenAI's entry tier, compared with 0.23 under purchasing-power-indexed pricing. A $20 plan therefore costs 0.65% of per-capita income a year in the median high-income economy and 29% in the median low-income economy, and 60% of the covered economies' working-age population lives where it exceeds the 2% affordability benchmark for broadband. The income elasticity of any generative-AI use is 0.37, about half of which mirrors the income gradient in internet use, and the ratio of AI users to internet users is flat across middle- and low-income groups. Per-capita use of a frontier assistant (Claude; free and paid accounts pooled) rises twice as steeply with income (0.71), and its measured gradient steepened between August 2025 and February 2026. A two-tier adoption model, in which free tiers relax the budget constraint on whether people use AI but not on how much frontier capability they use, is consistent with this contrast, although cross-country data cannot identify price effects. Because exposure and access are both income-graded, larger conditional gains for less-skilled users need not produce cross-country convergence.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on U.S. employment growth across 14 major industry sectors using a difference-indifferences (DiD) approach. Using the November 2022 launch of ChatGPT as an exogenous shock, we compare employment trends in high AI exposure industry sectors (Information, Financial Activities, and Professional & Business Services) with those in low AI exposure industry sectors using seasonally adjusted Bureau of Labor Statistics Current Employment Statistics data from January 2021 to June 2026. We find slower employment growth in high AI exposure industry sectors following the introduction of ChatGPT relative to low AI exposure industry sectors, although the pooled effect is not statistically significant. Disaggregating the treatment group, however, reveals substantial heterogeneity. The Information sector experienced a large and statistically significant decline in employment growth relative to the control group, whereas Financial Activities and Professional and Business Services show no statistically significant effects. These findings are robust to an alternative control-group specification and to using the March 2023 launch of Claude as an alternative treatment cutoff. These findings provide suggestive evidence of AI-related labor displacement in highly exposed sectors, particularly Information, but the relatively short 3.5-year post-adoption period and statistical imprecision preclude definitive conclusions. To better understand the labor market effects of generative AI, future research using longer time horizons and more granular occupational data is needed.

detail.abstract: We ask whether the gendered division of work affects firm productivity across the spectrum of economic development. Personnel records of over 100,000 individuals hired by a global firm that operates in 100 countries reveal that the performance of female employees is higher where women are underrepresented in the candidate pool. This implies productivity gains from hiring more women, but realizing them would require increasing women's pay relative to men. The findings highlight how unequal gender norms in local labor markets create an equity-efficiency trade-off inside the firm, particularly in low-income countries with conservative gender norms.

detail.abstract: Engineering projects face cost and schedule deviations that can become difficult to reverse before conventional reports prompt action. Earned value management (EVM) measures performance against a scope-linked baseline, yet cost and schedule indices alone do not explain the causes of deviation or quantify future risk. This paper proposes a conceptual early-warning framework that integrates EVM, earned schedule, a maintained risk register and probabilistic forecasts. A focused synthesis of project-control studies informs five connected stages: baseline and progress assurance, performance signal generation, risk-event updating, joint cost and schedule scenario analysis, and escalation with documented action. The framework distinguishes an observed variance from an uncertain future outcome, separates approved scope changes from performance deterioration, and treats schedule exposure through network criticality rather than assuming that a monetary schedule variance measures time. Three tables define the data interfaces, trigger logic and governance responsibilities. Two reproduced figures from a peer-reviewed engineering project study, reused under its Creative Commons Attribution licence, illustrate the difference between a point cost forecast and a probability distribution and show how forecast intervals change over successive reporting periods; they are external published findings, not results of this paper. The paper contributes a testable decision architecture rather than claiming a validated improvement. Future evaluation should compare warning lead time, forecast calibration, false alarms and action outcomes against standard EVM and riskregister practices in real engineering projects.

detail.abstract: This paper examines changes in U.S.-India equity return connectedness from January 2015 to April 1, 2021. We pair S&P 500 and NIFTY 50 local-currency index closes, estimate a recursively updated two-market time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) on 326 weekly return pairs, and calculate row-normalized generalized forecast-error variance shares. Trading-time-aligned daily regressions complement the weekly analysis. Average bilateral connectedness rises from 14.49% in 2015-2019 to 31.47% from January 2020 through April 1, 2021: a 16.98 percentage-point difference (conditional HAC 95% interval, 12.13-21.84). The preceding U.S. session predicts Indian returns in both subsamples; the same-day Indian return is associated with the U.S. return chiefly during the observed pandemic period. detail.abstract: Scope change in complex engineering projects is often necessary to meet emerging requirements, correct design deficiencies or protect system performance. Yet the apparent merit of an individual request can conceal effects on interfaces, procurement, commissioning, cost and contractual obligations. This conceptual paper asks how a decision maker can compare proposed changes while preserving an auditable baseline and making downstream consequences visible. A focused, interpretive synthesis of engineering change management, change propagation, construction change control and project governance research informs a six-stage framework: register the request; define alternatives against the current baseline; trace dependencies; estimate consequences and uncertainty; apply transparent decision criteria and authority; and verify implementation and learning. The model separates a technically desirable solution from a commercially authorised change, and requires explicit treatment of safety constraints, stakeholder value, schedule criticality and the timing of commitment. Two figures reproduced from licensed, peer-reviewed papers explain the range of change propagation concepts and the distribution of research on analytical support. They represent those authors' published work, not original data or an empirically tested version of this framework. Three tables specify methods, decision variables and governance records. The proposed contribution is a testable decision architecture connecting product or asset interfaces with project baseline control and accountable approvals. Its value remains to be examined through prospective comparisons of decision quality, propagation accuracy, approval time, rework and disputes across different engineering contexts.

detail.abstract: We model market impact as the response to submitted order flow net of counterflow from latent traders, activated when price displacements from the level that would prevail without the order exceed individual thresholds. Order flow depletes this pool, and a generalized Langevin equation governs its recovery over several time scales. Its memory kernels are finite sums of exponentials, so its Markovian lift is exact rather than an approximation. For an undepleted pool, aggregation under explicit assumptions on individual trading responses yields an intermediate square-root regime between linear smalland large-order limits, without imposing a square-root impact law. Scaling thresholds and responses with price noise makes impact in this regime proportional to volatility, and thresholds that grow with the execution horizon make it independent of duration. With constant displayed depth, expected round-trip costs are nonnegative under the log-price convention, independently of the memory. Numerical experiments show that depletion narrows the square-root range and that memory spectra producing similar single-order impacts can respond differently after substantial prior trading. Calibration to market data is left to a companion paper.

detail.abstract: Career changes across occupations are central to the cyclical behavior of workers' earnings growth. Using SIPP data, we show that workers who switch both employers and occupations account for 58 percent of the increase in the left-skewness of earnings growth during recessions. This is driven mainly by cyclical variation in the earnings changes upon a transition, rather than in transition flows. In a business cycle model with on-the-job search over employer and occupation ladders, cyclical shifts in the quality of worker-occupation matches are the main source of cyclical earnings risk, but they generate procyclical skewness only through workers' optimal mobility decisions: without these, procyclical skewness becomes countercyclical variance. Our results give a structural foundation to reduced-form income processes with higher-order risk, and point to policies that target occupational reallocation directly.

detail.abstract: This study developed a sustainable coal governance framework combining interpretive structural modelling, fuzzy MICMAC analysis, and system dynamics modelling. It mapped 21 interconnected parameters and enabled dynamic simulation of coal mining over a 10-year horizon (2025-2035). The results show that land degradation is largely irreversible, PM10 and PM2.5 consistently exceeds safe limits, and noise poses enduring health risk, while water quality improving gradually. Additionally, sensitivity analysis on important parameters identified employee training and welfare, land reclamation, dust suppression, and effluent control as the most influential interventions. By leveraging sensitivity analysis, three policy scenarios-strict regulation, renewable adoption, and integrated mitigation-were evaluated. Despite land use trade-offs, strict regulation appears as the most effective mitigation measure. This proves that sustainability challenges of coal mining are structural not technological. The proposed framework is replicable and can support evidence-based governance while informing global sustainability strategies in the extractive industries.

detail.abstract: Many commercial processes yield a lower-value co-product alongside a high-value main product. Under free disposal and weak demand, co-products are frequently discharged as air, water, or land pollution. We provide the first formal treatment of co-product pollution regulation, showing that regulating the co-product is equivalent to taxing the main product. We corroborate the theory using data and a policy change from Canada's oil sector, where excess co-produced natural gas is flared. Flaring regulation caused a 55% reduction in oil production and substantial leakage. Our results suggest regulating the $54 billion worth of gas flared globally could have significant unintended consequences.

detail.abstract: On 1 August 2026 Ukraine's competition authority retired a guidance instrument that had governed the finding of dominance for twenty four years without a single amendment. This paper audits that instrument against the decisional record it was written for: 6,820 published decisions of the Antimonopoly Committee of Ukraine (AMCU) and 2,160 judgments of the courts reviewing them. The test is the one Schrepel and Jenny put to the European Commission: what a guidance instrument codifies, restating law that binds anyway, adds nothing and shows up in the record as a provision nobody needs to cite, while what it announces on the agency's own authority is where it does work. Three findings. First, the authority and the courts use different halves of the same instrument: 82.9% of the AMCU's pinpoint citations fall in the sections on market definition, and 3.3% in the section that states the dominance test itself, where the two provisions that define dominance and set the 35% threshold attract no agency citation at all in twenty four years. Second, this is not neglect but division of labour with the statute: of the 62 agency decisions that discuss the 35% threshold and mention the instrument, 52 cite Article 12 of the Law and three cite the corresponding provision of the instrument. What the instrument contributes on its own authority is market definition, and that is exactly where the authority uses it. The codified half is a codification nobody needs, and the record routes around it to the binding text. Third, four of its sixty six provisions were never cited by anyone, and seven state no rule that can be applied on its own: they are a table of contents inside the instrument, and the record can only repeat them. Whether a passage applies a rule or merely restates it is the audit's hardest judgement. Two independent language models on a shared protocol agree on 74.4% of passages; a human reading of the 79 passages that decide the outcome agrees with them on 97.4% of a blind control (Cohen's κ = 0.95) and is stricter than either where they differ. On that reading 41 of the 66 provisions show no application anywhere in the record, a lower bound, since the reader is stricter than the models that labelled the rest.

detail.abstract: Hard conditioning on an inferred latent state can abruptly replace an estimation subsample. We call this mechanism sample gating and decompose estimator updates into arrival and gating. With the data window fixed, a selector moves by a between-state distance, whereas posterior averaging is Lipschitz in the state probabilities and minimizes posterior squared risk for the state-indexed component target. The continuity bound propagates to minimum-variance weights; for pooled means, soft historical labels extend it to row probabilities. Pooling is a separate bias–variance choice. Across two point-in-time equity universes and a sector-ETF panel, the headline posterior reduces median transition displacement by 74–85% across six estimator classes, compared with 4–37% for pooling at the selected state. These magnitudes refer to an inherited selector with undefined-state and minimum-sample rules; same-posterior selection and alternative classifiers assess sensitivity. Relative to full-window estimation, posterior averaging with pooling lowers risk-forecast loss in 9 of 9 panel–loss comparisons. Relative to hard selection, it lowers minimum-variance turnover by 27–29%, with observed annualized volatility differences no larger than 0.23 percentage points. In known-state simulations, averaging improves transition stability, while adding pooling to averaging raises covariance estimation risk when the states are sharply separated and has small or classifier-dependent effects on it when they are close. These results distinguish selection instability from pooling’s costs and benefits, without establishing a universal rule for routing regime information.

detail.abstract: Women on the short side of the marriage market are expected to gain from their scarcity. I study what scarcity does to adolescent girls. The random sex of births generates idiosyncratic variation in the sex composition of birth cohorts in small places, which I use as an instrument for the marriage market a girl faces as a teenager. Using birth registry and census data from Mexico, I find that girls in boy-heavy cohorts form unions and become mothers early: an interquartile increase in the sex ratio of the market she faces raises births before age eighteen by 13 percent. The additional unions are mostly consensual and formed with boys of her own age. However, girls in these cohorts are also more likely to leave school and to report household chores as their main activity. A favorable dating market moves girls away from investment in schooling and toward early family formation, decisions that are often irreversible.

detail.abstract:
Organizations frequently approach governance as a collection of documents, meetings, titles, boards, policies, or compliance requirements. Across governance and institutional-design engagements conducted through Marie Management between 2024 and 2026, however, the underlying problem was broader: organizations were attempting to exercise authority, pursue funding, establish entities, distribute resources, or expand institutional responsibility before developing the governance infrastructure necessary to account for those activities.

This practitioner-based portfolio case study examines governance and institutional-accountability interventions across emerging coalitions, multi-entity organizational structures, and institutions developing mechanisms for public transparency and resource stewardship. The work included entity-structure analysis, operating-agreement development, board-role clarification, ownership criteria, nonprofit and for-profit structural separation, grant-governance readiness, resource-distribution planning, public-accountability mechanisms, and institutional reporting architecture.

A central engagement involved an emerging business coalition preparing to formalize its organizational structure while simultaneously pursuing external funding. The coalition was considering a multi-member LLC, nonprofit and for-profit functions, board responsibilities, ownership criteria, and a $40,000 grant application while also evaluating a substantially larger funding opportunity of up to $900,000. The intervention reframed funding readiness as a governance problem: before substantially larger resources could be accepted or distributed, the institution required an operating agreement, defined board responsibilities, clearer ownership expectations, appropriate entity separation, fund-development capacity, and systems capable of governing grants and institutional obligations.

The portfolio also demonstrates a broader form of institutional accountability in which governance extends beyond internal boards. In a separate operating framework, public-transparency mechanisms were designed around government agendas, budgets, public spending, capital projects, policy activity, education investments, and annual community-impact reporting. That operating model established a 10% annual gross-revenue reinvestment commitment to public education and lifelong learning and paired the commitment with annual public reporting of revenue, reinvestment, supported initiatives, and measurable outcomes.

The central finding is that governance becomes operational when authority, responsibility, resources, oversight, and accountability are deliberately connected. Institutional scale therefore depends not only on whether an organization can obtain authority or resources, but also on whether it has built the governance capacity required to steward them.

detail.abstract: Urban air mobility (UAM) can bypass congested ground corridors and provide substantial travel-time savings even before its supporting vertiport network is sufficiently dense to minimize ground access and egress. We study this mismatch between service attractiveness and infrastructure maturity in a setting where ride-sourcing provides both the direct ground alternative and UAM feeder service. Passengers differ in direct ride-sourcing travel time, so UAM selectively attracts travelers facing relatively time-consuming ground trips. We develop a two-stage model in which vertiport density is chosen before fares and passenger mode choice and compare decentralized air-ground provision with platform integration and a no-UAM benchmark. When pickup and repositioning are sufficiently efficient, UAM reduces ride-sourcing vehicle-hours traveled even with sparse vertiport coverage. Its effect on vehicle-kilometers traveled (VKT), however, changes sign at a unique vertiport-density threshold: below the threshold, long feeder movements increase VKT; above it, UAM reduces VKT. At a fixed network, integration lowers the door-to-door UAM fare and magnifies the prevailing VKT effect by shifting more passengers toward UAM. When vertiport investment is endogenous, integration also raises the private return to coverage and induces a denser network. For intermediate deployment costs, only the integrated network crosses the VKT threshold, reversing the sign of UAM's mileage effect relative to decentralized operation. A New York City application exhibits the same reversal: integration increases VKT on a fixed two-vertiport network but makes a third vertiport privately worthwhile, yielding lower VKT once infrastructure responds. Deployment support and a UAM fare instrument address the remaining coverage and passenger-allocation gaps. These results show that the transportation effect of platform integration cannot be assessed independently of the infrastructure investment incentives it creates.

detail.abstract: Large language models are known to be sensitive to the order in which they read their inputs. How much that sensitivity matters once a model sits inside a trading system whose final decision is made by deterministic code is not known. This paper reports a pre-registered test at the only point in a production multi-agent trading architecture (ZVAKTHOR) where a language model reads an ordered list: a Research agent that synthesizes five agent votes into one directional vote. Using the production prompt, 24 synthetic evidence sets in three strata, and 3,840 calls to deepseek-flash at temperature 0, we compare all 120 orderings of each set against 40 repeats of one fixed ordering, so that order effects are measured against the model's own noise. The mean diversity increase under permutation is 0.028 (Holm-adjusted p = 0.042 within the amended two-test family; not significant under the originally registered four-test family). The point estimate is below the pre-registered smallest effect size of interest (0.05), but effects of that size cannot be excluded, and equivalence is not shown; the registered verdict is inconclusive. We find no evidence of a primacy or recency effect (p = 0.49). Intrinsic noise is large where evidence conflicts: under an identical input, the modal direction in the balanced-conflict stratum is returned in only 72% of repeats. Traced through a replica of the production aggregator, no change in the synthesizer's output direction altered any consensus result: by construction of the stimuli and the rule, consensus is unreachable in 15 of the 16 conflict sets whatever the synthesizer outputs, and all 43 observed changes arose from confidence variation in a single near-threshold set. At this boundary the practical risk is nondeterminism rather than order, and how much of it reaches a decision depends on the aggregation rule, the weight it assigns, and where inputs fall relative to its threshold.

detail.abstract: Market-regime models typically assume a finite set of discrete latent states. We examine whether high frequency limit-order-book dynamics exhibit distinct regime separation or apparent regimes result from discretising an underlying continuum of market conditions. We analyse four years of deep limit-order book data for EURO STOXX 50 index futures across 987 clean trading days from 2022 to 2025, using 30, 45 and 60-second aggregation windows. Market states are represented by 15 × 15 symmetric positive definite covariance matrices constructed from price, liquidity, depth, book-shape and order-flow variables and analysed under Log-Euclidean and affine-invariant geometries; the resulting state cloud has an effective dimension of approximately 1.4. A causal anomaly layer filters statistical, calendar and rollover contamination, while label-free economic validation evaluates market-state separation independently of volatility-based proxy labels. A 17-method zoo spanning conventional and Riemannian representations, reinforced by full-cloud geometric certificates, consistently favours a continuum over a discrete regime structure. A dominant latent coordinate captures between 83.66% and 85.27% of variation in the covariance-state geometry and tracks VSTOXX without regime labels. This geometric stress axis remains stable across years, although its average level shifts with market conditions, indicating that conventional regimes are coarse quantisations of the underlying continuum. A divisive hierarchy spanning macro, macro-subregime, micro and micro-subregime tiers is evaluated using expanding-year walk-forward tests. Out-of-sample performance is strongest at the macro tier, while finer tiers fail to generalise. Continuous fine-scale information remains predictive; its discretisation causes the performance loss. The stress dial is highly persistent, yet deviations gradually return toward their typical level, halving within approximately 5-15 minutes. Forecasting performance peaks near ten minutes, reaching a maximum pooled R 2 OOS of 0.7483. Although incremental predictive value over volatility persistence strengthens toward one hour, it provides no improvement over HAR at the next-day horizon. Overall, the latent stress coordinate defines a stable, low-dimensional geometric continuum that captures market stress and its predictive dynamics. detail.abstract: Ask a chief executive how artificial intelligence is influencing the strategy of the firm and you will receive a confident answer. Ask which specific strategic decision it influenced last quarter, and the answer becomes vague. Organizational AI usage climbed from roughly 55 percent to 88 percent of surveyed firms between 2023 and 2025, and around 70 percent of organizations now place AI at the heart of their business strategy-yet agentic deployment remains in the single digits across nearly every business function, only about a third report deep transformation, and one widely discussed 2025 study put the share of enterprise generative-AI pilots delivering no measurable return at 95 percent. Adoption is nearly universal; influence is neither evenly distributed nor clearly located. This paper argues that the phrase "the influence of AI on strategic decision making" conceals three separable questions that management has been answering as if they were one: where in the decision process AI actually enters, how its entry changes the failure modes of that decision, and who holds the decision right when the recommendation is contested. Drawing on the strategic decision-making literature, the emerging empirical record on AI-assisted judgment, and observable practice in Indian technology services, product firms, and global capability centers, the paper makes three contributions. First, it decomposes the strategic decision process into six stages and identifies four distinct modes of AI influence-analyst, generator, challenger, and agent-showing that influence concentrates in scanning and evaluation and thins at framing and commitment, which are precisely the stages where accountability resides. Second, it maps the signal landscape: eight observable failure modes-automation bias, algorithm aversion, evaluation instability, option homogenisation, proxy mis-specification, self-fulfilling forecasts, the accountability gap, and confidential-strategy leakage-each paired with a signal a practitioner can watch for and a countermeasure available. Third, it proposes the AI-in-the-loop ladder, a five-rung allocation of decision rights matched to stakes, reversibility, feedback observability, and objective specifiability, operationalised through a decision charter that names a human owner for every strategic choice that touches a model. The framework is general, illustrated with Indian contexts where adoption is running ahead of governance. The paper is conceptual and practitioner-facing; it reports no proprietary model and no confidential dataset. Its aim is to help CEOs, corporate strategy heads, and investment committees move from asking whether AI influences strategy to deciding where, how much, and under whose authority.

detail.abstract: Cybersecurity failures increasingly originate outside the affected organization, as compromises of shared vendors, software components, and digital infrastructures propagate across thousands of dependent firms. This paper explains how such systemic cyber risk emerges from individually rational organizational choices. We develop the Micro-Macro Cybersecurity Choice Framework, which links ecosystem conditions, boundedly rational security decisions, and three system-level outcomes: collective underinvestment, correlated failure, and the erosion of trust and resilience. The framework integrates two mechanisms usually studied separately, information asymmetry and interdependence, and shows that they are endogenously linked. Unable to observe security quality, organizations delegate to providers chosen through common proxies, thereby concentrating the digital dependency networks through which failures propagate. Conceptualizing cybersecurity as a polycentric governance problem, we map institutional mechanisms to the failures they address and derive eight propositions. The analysis repositions cybersecurity from a technical control problem to a strategic problem of organizational choice and institutional design.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a time-varying firm-level measure of AI-washing that quantifies excess AI-oriented disclosure emphasis relative to observable capability building by contrasting AI-related narrative content in MD&A disclosures with AI-related hiring signals from online job postings. External validation shows that higher AI-washing is associated with greater subsequent policy support and external attention from media and investors, as well as a favorable short-window stock market response around annual report disclosures that is not detectable over longer horizons, while showing no corresponding increase in subsequent AI innovation outcomes. Driver analyses indicate that AI-washing rises when perceived narrative returns are higher, proxied by stronger local government emphasis on AI. Lower communication frictions are likewise associated with more pronounced AI-washing, as evidenced by larger increases following the commercialization of ChatGPT among firms with limited publicity budgets. Our findings highlight how inflated AI narratives can distort external assessments of firm capability and lead to resource misallocation, underscoring the value of more verifiable disclosure around AI claims.

detail.abstract: Firms increasingly deploy large numbers of LLM agents as "digital workers", and vendors already bill them per resolved task—a piece rate in all but name. Personnel economics decomposes the productivity effect of piece rates into an incentive effect (existing workers exert more effort) and a selection effect (the pay scheme changes who stays). We argue that for AI workers the weight of this decomposition shifts: the incentive channel is weak and, in our setting, quality-neutral, while the selection channel carries the multitask distortion predicted by Holmström and Milgrom (1991). We test this in two experiments on agentic tasks with a genuine effort margin and a hidden quality dimension, with outcomes and tests fixed before the main runs. In Experiment 1 (288 work shifts, three frontier models, programming tasks), telling agents they are paid per completed task significantly changes how they work—fewer self-checks (−1.2 per shift, Holm-adjusted p = 0.026) and earlier stopping—and the effect is driven by pay rather than by the mention of audits; but quality does not fall. In Experiment 2, we evolve a population of 12 agent configurations (model × work-style prompt) that are never told how they are evaluated. Across four replicates, selecting on completed pieces raises pieces per agent by 76% while the error share among accepted pieces rises from 11% to 42% and net value per agent falls by 64%; selecting on net value keeps the error share at 12%, and a random-selection control stays at 7%. The mechanism is a work-style that skips the page stating the reporting period—never incentivized, only selected. For AI workforces, the design problem is less how to motivate agents than what to select them on.

detail.abstract: Digital start-ups increasingly leverage external digital components (EDCs), such as development frameworks and marketing automation modules, to build products and engage customers in the early stages. Existing research has found that EDCs can facilitate product development in resource-constrained start-ups but has only examined single EDCs in isolation, without considering how their architectural properties vary across the functional areas they support. Product-oriented EDCs typically provide domain-agnostic building blocks, and so they exhibit high integration complexity and low functional completeness. Conversely, customer-oriented EDCs typically provide ready-to-use functionalities for customer engagement and marketing tasks, and so they exhibit low integration complexity and high functional completeness. These architectural properties determine the extent of effort start-ups expend for EDC usage, which affects their time to early-stage funding. Using data from 7,772 digital start-ups and employing survival analysis models, we find that a 1% increase in the use of product-oriented EDCs is associated with a 0.221% longer time to early-stage venture capital funding (i.e., Series A), whereas a 1% increase in the use of customer-oriented EDCs is associated with a 0.200% shorter corresponding time. We further find that absorptive capacity through employee hires mitigates the negative effect of increased product-oriented EDC use but may substitute for customer-oriented EDC use under certain conditions. By explaining how EDCs supporting different functional areas differ in their architectural properties and resource demands, we extend research on digital entrepreneurship and specify when employee hires complement versus substitute for EDC use.
